author: backnotprop
body:
## What changes for you

Switching between light and dark, or picking a new colour palette, is now instant. The new colours appear in one frame. Before, the page froze for about 0.4 s and then faded every colour over 150 ms.

This works everywhere the theme can change:
- the Inbox: the sidebar sun/moon toggle, Settings → Appearance, and the tour's "Make it yours" step;
- plan review, code review and annotate (their Settings theme controls);
- "Match system", including when your computer itself turns dark or light.

Under reduced motion it was already instant in the Inbox, and it stays that way. Hover effects, menus and sheets keep their own animations.

## Why it was slow

Every element on the page has a 150 ms colour transition (`theme.css`, the `*` rule). A theme switch changes every colour, so the browser started thousands of transitions at once and recomputed styles for each of them on every frame.

## How it works

- `ThemeProvider` (`@plannotator/ui`) is the one place every theme change passes through. When it swaps the theme classes on `<html>`, it adds `pn-theme-switching`. The class stays until two frames after React has redrawn the new theme.
- Under that class, `theme.css` sets every transition's duration and delay to 0 s. Only the timing changes: a transition that is already running (a sheet sliding, a menu fading) finishes normally. When the class goes, hover fades work again.
- The code review diff colours (Pierre) are read again one frame later. That code now calls a new `extendThemeSwitch()` before it redraws, so the diffs also switch without a fade.
- The Inbox's old `ib-theme-instant` class, which only applied under reduced motion, is removed. The shared mechanism replaces it.

`@plannotator/ui` consumers (Workspaces): nothing changes except that the switch is instant. Hosts that use `ThemeProvider` get it automatically. A host that sets the mode itself can add `pn-theme-switching` in the same way (see the README). The generated Inbox stylesheet for hosts no longer has a page-level rule to drop.

## Measured

Measured with the theme-split bench, S data, the 300-message thread with 30 messages open, sidebar toggle light → dark, 6 clicks each, this Mac, sandboxed data dir:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Click → next frame (page frozen) | **382 ms** | **66 ms** |
| Style recalculation over 2 s | 597 ms | 80 ms |
| Main-thread busy time over 2 s | 962 ms | 151 ms |

Filmed light → dark: on main the screen shows no change until about 0.8 s after the click. With this PR the first frame after the click is already dark.

## Tests

- `packages/ui/components/ThemeProvider.test.tsx`: Settings' mode buttons, a palette pick, Match system and an OS change each hold `pn-theme-switching`, and the hold goes away afterwards. A palette change for the half that is not on screen holds nothing.
- `packages/inbox/themeToggle.test.tsx` and `tour.test.tsx`: the sidebar toggle, Settings' Match system and "Make it yours" switch instantly with or without reduced motion. These replace the old reduced-motion-only assertion.
- `tests/e2e/theme-instant-switch.spec.ts` (real Chromium): counts the colour transitions that start during a flip. It must find none in the Inbox (toggle, Settings, Match system, OS change), under reduced motion, or in plan review and code review. It also checks that an already-running transform transition keeps running through a switch, and that hover fades come back afterwards.

Without the fix (base `35fb692bb`), the new tests fail: the ThemeProvider test, the toggle test and the Match system test fail (the class is never held), and the e2e spec counts 561 colour transitions for one Inbox toggle, 11,159 for plan review and 3,586 for code review following the OS. The reduced-motion and running-transform tests pass on main as well, because they guard behaviour that must stay the same.

## One thing not covered

A few elements use Tailwind's `dark:` variant, and in this codebase that variant follows the computer's colour scheme through a media query, not the app's theme. When the OS scheme flips, the browser restyles them before any script runs, so they can still fade, and they already show the wrong shade when the app is set to an explicit Light or Dark that differs from the OS. The new e2e test leaves those elements out of its count. This is a separate issue and is not changed here.

author: robertoaraneda
body:
Two follow-ups from #253 (plan 016), in two commits.

## Without a model, a FHIR type question is a guess (docs)

With no model a value read from a resource carries only the System type of its JSON. A question naming a FHIR type is then answered by the System type that FHIR type converts to:

| Expression | No model, this engine | No model, fhirpath.js 5.2.0 | R4/R5 model, both |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Patient.gender is String` | `true` | `true` | `false` |
| `Patient.gender.type().name` | `String` | `String` | `code` |
| `Patient.gender is code` | `true` (guessed) | internal error | `true` |
| `Patient.telecom.value is code` | `true` (guessed, wrong) | internal error | `false` |
| `Patient.descendants().ofType(integer64)` | `[2, 5]` (guessed, wrong) | internal error | `[9]` in R5 |

The README said these heuristics "work for most cases". It now says the guess can be wrong and that FHIR resources need the model whenever an expression asks about a FHIR type. CONFORMANCE.md has a new section, "Without a model, a FHIR type is a guess".

- **Why the table stays:** plan 016 had a follow-up to derive `fhirPathSpecMap` from the model. It was withdrawn after measuring two things. With a model the table is never consulted. Without one there is no package to derive it from.
- **fhirpath.js's error:** recorded as JS-11 in `docs/upstream-findings.md`. It is not reported upstream yet.
- **Evidence:**
  - `node difftest/batteries/no-model/measure.js` measures fhirpath.js.
  - `conformance/no_model_types_test.go` holds this engine's answers. It fails when `integer64` or `code` is taken out of the table.

## Decimal cost tests bound bytes allocated, not time (tests)

Five tests in `types` checked by elapsed time (50 ms or 10 ms) that a decimal far beyond the bound is not written out or rescaled. Under load they failed with no defect. During mutation runs they also counted mutants as caught when only the load had slowed them down.

- **The new bound:** the tests now limit the bytes allocated (`allocatedBy`, `withoutWritingOut`), which do not depend on load.
- **Measured:**
  - The fast paths allocate 30 KB at most, except `InDecimalRange`, which copies its 2 MB coefficient once and is held to twice that.
  - Counting or rescaling allocates 42–50 MB.
- **Mutants:** the 15 mutants these tests caught are all still caught. Four of them (M02, M10, M11, M32) change only the cost, not the result, and the new bound is what catches them.
- **Load:** the five tests passed ten runs in a row next to 24 busy loops.

`make check` is green.

author: auser
body:
Part of #4839 — the "Consolidate the `mvm-gpu-*` shim crates … into the single umbrella crate `mvm-gpu`; no standalone `mvm-gpu-*` crates remain" item. PR #5018 removed `mvm-gpu-shim-core`; this removes the remaining three.

## What changed

- `mvm-gpu-cuda-shim`, `mvm-gpu-cudart-shim`, `mvm-gpu-nvml-shim` are gone. Their sources move verbatim (git renames) to `crates/mvm-gpu/examples/{cuda,cudart,nvidia_ml}.rs`, declared as `crate-type = ["cdylib"]` examples — the same mechanism the crate already uses for `gpu_guest_probe`.
- An example has no build script, so the `-Wl,-soname` each shim advertised from its own `build.rs` now comes from the builders, which already carry the soname in the cdylib table:
  - `mvm-build` guest-bins extras: per-target RUSTFLAGS per invocation.
  - `nix/packages/mvm-gpu-shims.nix`: one derivation per example, RUSTFLAGS carries the soname flag (inert on host-built build scripts).
  - conformance GPU e2e staging: one zigbuild invocation per shim with the same flag.
- `GuestCdylib` gains `kind: CdylibKind` (`Lib` vs `Example`) and derives `cargo_selection()` and the output path (`examples/lib<name>.so`) from it. Table tests now verify the example declarations in `mvm-gpu`'s manifest and agreement with the Nix recipe's example-keyed attrset.
- `EXTRAS_SOURCE_INPUTS` fingerprint now hashes `crates/mvm-gpu/examples` instead of the three crates.
- NATIVE-WITNESS.md build/run commands updated (its old `libmvm_gpu_*_shim.so` paths were already stale against the crates' `[lib] name`).

Historical audit tables in `specs/contracts/` (`cleanup-preservation-ledger.md`, `build-dependency-decisions.md`, `cleanup-inventory.md`) still name the old crates; they are point-in-time snapshots and two are ledgers queued for retirement under a separate #4839 item.

## Validation

- `cargo check -p mvm-gpu --examples` — clean.
- `cargo test -p mvm-build --lib guest_bins` — 48/48 pass (includes the reworked cdylib-table and Nix-agreement tests).
- `cargo test -p mvm-gpu` — all pass (one `endpoint` test needed a short `TMPDIR`; its Unix-socket path exceeds macOS's 104-byte limit under a long tmpdir — pre-existing, unrelated).
- `cargo clippy -p mvm-build -p mvm-gpu -p mvm-conformance --all-targets` — clean.
- `nix-instantiate --parse nix/packages/mvm-gpu-shims.nix` — parses; the Nix derivation itself was not built on this macOS host (CI/image builders exercise it).
- The live GPU e2e witness lane was not run locally.

author: marguerite347
body:
The new community articles exposed two assumptions in catalog normalization: only older long capture captions were accepted, and every listing required a successful full-source review date. Accept the owner-approved Docs walkthrough/Concept overview labels and preserve a dated observation separately when a listing has no successful full review.

The Four Lanes article keeps a null successful-check date because its linked Reddit reply is inaccessible. Its source observation is retained as provisional; no review success is invented. Added a regression test covering the normalized evidence and rejection of missing observations.

Validation: 84 tests passed, content/schema checks passed, and the real site build passed. This corrects the failed merged checks for PR161 before publication.

author: psryland
body:
## Summary

Fix an intermittent `0xC0000005` process exit in the native unit-test runner, including runs with zero selected tests.

Namespace-scope thread-local shader resources are constructed on foreign DLL threads as well as test threads. An empty Debug `std::vector` allocates an iterator proxy. CDB caught a foreign thread destroying `g_coupled_velocity_replay_frame_failures` and calling `_free_dbg` after the main thread had started uninitializing the executable's static CRT, leaving its heap lock unavailable.

- Use `pr::vector<T, 0>` for emulated structured buffers so unused resources allocate nothing.
- Construct test fixture lists through function-local TLS, avoiding initialization on unrelated threads.
- Let `PackShape` append to caller-owned growable buffers without depending on `std::vector` inheritance.
- Add regressions covering allocation-free empty buffers, binding/reset semantics, and per-thread resource isolation.

No CRT configuration changes, suppressed exceptions, forced process termination, or shader binding changes are involved. The separate buoyancy-volume investigation is excluded.

## Verification

- VS 2026/v145 Debug x64 native runner and physics library builds succeeded.
- `ShaderResourceLifetimeTests`: 3/3 passed.
- Original unfiltered `InertiaTests` and `ShapeBuilderTests`: 37/37 passed, exit 0.
- Affected Quick inertia/shape-builder/coupled-velocity selection: 16/16 passed, exit 0.
- 25 redirected `NoSuchClassXYZ -asserts:stderr` runs: all exited 0.
- CDB with first-chance access-violation breaking enabled: zero-selected process exited 0.

The full native suite has not been run for this change. It remains required before merging.

## Review

Ready: no unresolved findings in the completed fix. Unfinished buoyancy diagnostic logging remains uncommitted and is not included.

author: kvnloo
body:
Automated factory run `GEV-PORT-835` (Claude Code Opus on the MBP). Draft until reviewed by Opus.

### Agent summary
I've ported PR #835 onto `factory/gev-port-835` as commit `2c36619c`. The full test suite passes after the change (0 failures). It was not already on the branch: `viewportContextDecision`, the `viewport_context.*` events and the new test file were all missing, so this isn't a NOCHANGE. There's no `AGENTS.md` in this checkout, so I worked from `docs/` and the community-pr skill instead.

**What changed**
- **`src/voice/realtimeViewport.js`:** added `viewportContextDecision()`, which gives a short reason code for why a voice lookup sends an image or not. The image-sending code now uses it and writes those codes to the debug log, along with `capture-unavailable`, `capture-invalidated`, `sent` and `data-channel-send-failed`. Image contents are never logged. The #837 pointer-ground crop stays a separate path from the full screenshot, and the user-turn precedence and one-retained-image rules are unchanged. It adds no new image requests.
- **`src/voice/realtimeController.js`:** passes `debugLog` through to the viewport code. That log goes to the existing local file (`.gev-logs/realtime-conversations.jsonl`), not to any UI, so no Vue view or store was added and the voice store/presenter stays the only UI owner.
- **Tests and docs:** added `src/voice/realtimeViewportPolicy.test.mjs` from the PR and listed it in `scripts/format-scope.json`. Added one sentence to the point-and-ask paragraph in `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`. Added `changelog.d/835-viewport-escalation-reasons.md`, rewritten in the house style. All three were merged against current upstream text. `scripts/package-boundaries.json` already lists `realtimeViewport.js`, so it needed no change.
- **Credit:** the commit message credits kvnloo (original author), asturksever and quanticsoul4772 (they commented on the PR; it has no formal GitHub reviews), and bilawalsidhu (#837).

**Commands run**

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `npm ci` | ok | – |
| Targeted voice tests (`node --import=./build/registerVue.js --test`, pointerCrop, gevRealtime, pointAndAsk, pointAndAskReview, realtimeOwners; after also includes the new file) | 191/191 pass | 198/198 pass |
| `npm run format:check` | pass | pass (1649 files) |
| `npm run check:boundaries` | pass | pass |
| `npm run changelog:check` | – | fragment listed |
| `npm test -- --test-concurrency=4` | 9624 tests: 9622 pass, **1 fail**, 1 skipped | 9631 tests: 9630 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped |
| `npm run i18n` | not needed, no locales changed | – |

The one failure before the change was `src/tools/tool-schema-codepoints.test.mjs` ("stops counting past the limit"). It's unrelated to voice and passed on the next run, so it looks flaky.

**Proof the new tests fail without the change**

- **Base runtime plus only the new `viewportContextDecision` function:** 3 of 7 tests fail — runtime dispatch, capture failure/invalidated, and successful-send logging. The other 4 check the pure decision function and the closed-channel case, which already behaved this way, so they pass either way.

I restored the production files after each run and no existing assertions were changed.

author: hisamekms
body:
## Summary

Reworks what the facilitator can do with a finished work item in a collab, after a hands-on review. Four tasks from the integration branch `feat/collab-card`, each reviewed and checked before it was merged into the branch, then reviewed by a person on a seeded session. ADR 0026 is amended for each decision.

### Confirming a revision is removed
Nobody has time to mark results during a collab: the card menu's 「この作業の結果を確認済みにする」, the 確認済み divider, the end dialog's "unconfirmed results", the route `POST /api/session/revisions/:id/confirm`, the model's `Confirmed` state and the `revision.confirmed` event are gone. Migration 9 turns confirmed revisions back into recorded ones.

### Revert a work item instead of restoring the workspace
- The card's ⋯ offers 「この作業を打ち消す」: it reverts only that work's changes and keeps later ones, like `git revert`.
- A revert queues like any other change (stoppable while it waits). When its turn comes, the server reverts it mechanically (a line-level three-way merge, checked as a run is, then formatted); it needs no agent. When the changes overlap later ones or the check fails, it is left to the AI as a normal run, with the work's per-file diff and the instruction to undo only those changes.
- Only the facilitator can revert. The reverted work reads 打ち消し済み, and its assumptions are closed.
- The revert is followed in the chat alone: the facilitator's message 「〈作業名〉の変更を打ち消す」 and its card (queued with 前に n 件, done as an AI turn, nothing left to revert, stopped, failed). Every queued card now shows 前に n 件.
- Agents send their capabilities when they claim; an older subscriber is refused a revert (`SubscriberOutdated`) rather than mis-running it. Migration 10 adds `requests.reverts`.

### Restore moves to the collab menu
The snapshot restore stays as the last resort, as 「以前の状態に復元」 in the collab menu, with the earlier states named by what they were (コラボの開始時, 〈作業名〉の前, …).

### Three verbs
Stop (中止: 「実行を中止」, state 中止), revert (打ち消し) and restore (復元) no longer share 「取り消し」; menu labels lose their 「…」.

## Breaking changes
- Session API: `POST /api/session/revisions/:id/confirm` is removed; `POST /api/session/runs/:id/revert` is added.
- Agent API: claims carry `capabilities`; `revision.confirmed` is no longer sent; a run's start may carry `revert`.
- Session databases are migrated (9, 10).

## Test plan
- [x] `bun run build`, `bun run typecheck` (`bun check`), `bun run lint`, `bun run fmt:check`, `bun test`, `dt -r examples/shop check` on the branch head
- [x] Use-case, server and subscriber tests for both revert paths, queueing behind a running run, no agent connected, stopping a queued revert, no double processing between the server and an agent
- [x] Human review on a seeded session

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: the-troy-ellis
body:
## What
Part 4 of [spec 35](docs/specs/35-bigger-maps.md). Until now every 256 m square's far mesh was built at load and kept on the GPU for the whole match. Now a square's far mesh is built once the square is within the **reach** plus 150 m, and let go past 300 m more:
- **In the cockpit**, the reach is the fog's end (1,150 m at most, less in weather).
- **In the map view and the editor**, the reach is as far as the overhead camera's screen shows. `camView` now reports the point it looks at and that reach, and both views pass them on. Zoomed right out, it still draws the whole map.

So the GPU holds what's around you, whatever the map's size. At today's size the change is small, because the fog reaches most of the map:

| where | far squares held (of 81) | GPU |
|---|---|---|

author: ymichael
body:
## Human comments

## What was wrong

The Codex bridge built the `codex app-server` environment from its own process env and copied only the two Account Pooler variables (`CODEX_OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `CODEX_POOL_AUTH_TOKEN`) from the session's env vars (`appServerLaunchEnv` in `plugins/provider-codex/src/bridge/bridge.ts`). A `CODEX_HOME` set in project or machine environment settings reached Codex's shell commands through `shell_environment_policy`, but never reached the app-server process, which owns login and config. Threads therefore ran on the bridge's inherited home or `~/.codex`, so separate personal and work projects couldn't use separate Codex accounts. The session construction signature also left out the home, so changing it would not have rebuilt a live session. Issue: #6866.

## What changed

- `appServerLaunchEnv` forwards `CODEX_HOME` along with the pool variables. Start, resume, fork, rebuilds and `model/list` all launch through it.
- `constructionSignature` includes `CODEX_HOME`, so a turn with a different home rebuilds the session on the new home (`session/replaced`) instead of staying on the old account.
- With no override, behaviour is unchanged: the app-server inherits the bridge's environment as before.
- The fake app-server logs `CODEX_HOME` with each launch, so tests can assert on it.

No wire or protocol changes, and no CLI or docs changes.

Known limits, not addressed here:
- If an existing thread's home changes, the rebuild resumes the conversation from the new home. When its rollout exists only in the old home, Codex reports the missing rollout. bb doesn't silently switch accounts, and switching the home back restores the thread.
- Skill-root discovery (#3925) still reads the bridge's `CODEX_HOME`. `model/list` is per host, so it follows only a machine-level `CODEX_HOME`.

## How you verified

- New `plugins/provider-codex/src/bridge/bridge.codex-home.test.ts` covers concurrent threads with different homes, the default with no override, resume, fork, `model/list`, and a home change mid-thread. All 5 cases fail on `main` and pass with this change.
- Real `codex-cli 0.164.0`, run once through a scratch test (not committed) that drove the bridge's `thread/start` with `envVars.CODEX_HOME` set to an empty temp dir:
  - Before the fix, the project home stayed empty and Codex wrote its state to the inherited home.
  - After the fix, Codex wrote its state into the project home, including `thread-writer-locks/<providerThreadId>.lock`.
- `pnpm exec turbo run typecheck lint test --filter=bb-plugin-provider-codex` passes: 555 tests in 45 files.
- Not verified: an end-to-end switch between two real signed-in accounts in the UI.

Fixes #6866

body:
## Root cause
USM run https://github.com/tjsr/user-session-middleware/actions/runs/41552390851 passes tests but fails CommonJS compilation with TS7016 for testutils. CJS declarations were disabled, exports lacked conditional types, and CJS .js output inherited the root ESM package type.

## Fix
- Emit CJS declarations and export matching ESM/CJS types without changing runtime entry paths.
- Add a CommonJS package boundary and rewrite declaration-relative .ts paths to emitted .js paths.
- Explicitly include both distribution trees in the npm package.
- Test the actual npm-packed artifact in strict TypeScript ESM/CJS consumers and real Node import/require. No skipLibCheck or ambient-any substitutes.
- Use latest npm and narrow git allowance to root dependencies.

## Validation and remaining blocker
Unit tests (11), lint, distribution build, packed ESM/CJS type checks and ESM runtime import passed at 88b66c7001e2792bb4e01a022211289433088992. CommonJS runtime check correctly exposes an upstream defect in published @tjsr/fs-utils 0.0.8: its dist/cjs/index.js is interpreted as ESM and throws `exports is not defined`. The regression check remains enabled. Full run: https://github.com/tjsr/testutils/actions/runs/41553523636 .

## Release implications
Version remains main's staged 0.0.12. No package has been published. A fixed fs-utils must be released and this lockfile updated before testutils can pass fully and be released. USM remains on testutils 0.0.11 until authorized release and consumer update. Its separate simple-env-utils declaration/runtime packaging issue is tracked by https://github.com/tjsr/simple-env-utils/pull/199 .

Removes `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`. Nothing reads its result: no release, PR or merge gates on it, and its 3 AM run was not fully green in any of the 40 nights from 2026-09-20 to 2026-11-02.

author: punk6529
body:
> Stacked on #4587 (W6 C1: codec). Review the commits after it; GitHub drops them from this diff once #4587 merges.

## Issue

- PLAN-P2P W6, unit C2. Acceptance criterion A4 (with W2's D7 and W6's C4, which come later) needs a client that sends identical signed bytes to at least two gateways and walks the status ladder: Signed, Submitted, Committed ("reported by n"), Finalized, In decision. It also needs a deterministic mock gateway that CI can run.
- The design gives gateway rules, not an RPC (P41 §5.1 GW1-GW7; R1 §1.8). So the client's transport stays behind a port, and the mock speaks a small wire format of our own, versioned `v0`.

## Fix

- `lib/chain/status-ladder.ts`: the ladder as a pure function of accumulated evidence (P41 §5.3, P30 §10.4). It shows one label, never "Confirmed", and has the overlays Rejected, Failed, Expired, Replaced and Reduced. Claims count distinct operators (GW5). Finalized and In decision need verified evidence from a `ProofVerifier`. Without one, the ladder stops at "Committed (reported by n gateways)", as P41 §5.4 requires.
- `lib/chain/gateway/`: the port (`transport.ts`), wire format v0 (`wire.ts`, which validates every untrusted field), an HTTP transport, and the client (`client.ts`), which implements:
  - GW4: send to one gateway per operator, at least two operators;
  - swap a gateway that stays silent for two polls for a reserve, and resend the bytes;
  - rebroadcast when no gateway holds the transaction (P41 §5.3 `track()`);
  - claim expiry from gateway heads;
  - GW7: refuse a gateway list with fewer than two operators.
- `lib/chain/mock/`: a deterministic in-memory chain with gateway behaviours from P41's malicious-gateway table (honest, silent, censor, liar). Also a mock `ProofVerifier`, for tests only, and an HTTP server. The mock checks P40 §2.3 steps 1-4 and 6-9 plus the nonce (keyType-1 signatures by ecrecover), orders by nonce, enforces validity windows, and settles decisions on request.
- `scripts/mock-chain-gateway.cjs`: runs that server for CI and local work (`node scripts/mock-chain-gateway.cjs --port 0`), and prints one JSON ready line.
- The label vocabulary stays in code (`CHAIN_STATUS_COPY_EN`, `chainStatusCopy()`) for W6 C5, the label component and i18n keys, which waits for the i18n-split lane. Nothing renders it.

How C4 plugs in (not in this PR): `decisions.vote()` builds a VOTE_SET body with C1's codec, has the Signer port sign the txId, calls `track(bytes, { awaitDecision: true })`, and maps each `ChainStatus` into the DataSource's provenance. PLAN-P2P §2's `Transport.submitTx` wraps `submit()`.

## Changes

- New: `lib/chain/status-ladder.ts`, `lib/chain/gateway/{transport,wire,http-transport,client}.ts`, `lib/chain/mock/{chain,proof-verifier,http-server}.ts`, `scripts/mock-chain-gateway.cjs`.
- `knip.jsonc`: the `lib/chain` exemption is extended to the new directories. The script is a knip entry under `scripts/**`.
- No app importer; nothing in the running app changes (C11).

## Validation

- `__tests__/lib/chain/status-ladder.test.ts` (12 tests): each transition and overlay, operator counting, conflict flagging, monotonicity, and that no copy says "Confirmed".
- `__tests__/lib/chain/gateway-client.test.ts` (12 tests, in-process mock, one block per poll):
  - the full walk Signed → Submitted → Committed → Finalized → In decision with the mock verifier;
  - a stop at Committed (reported by 2) without a verifier;
  - a silent gateway swapped for a reserve;
  - censoring gateways ending in Expired;
  - a lying gateway outvoted by verification, or shown only as a conflicting claim;
  - Rejected, Failed (verified) and Replaced;
  - mock admission: signatures, nonces, duplicates, expiry.
- `__tests__/lib/chain/mock-gateway-http.test.ts` (4 tests): the client over real HTTP against three gateways, CheckTx codes for malformed and oversize bodies, silent-gateway connection drops, loopback-only CORS, and a spawn of `scripts/mock-chain-gateway.cjs` that reads its ready line and control API. This is the "mock gateway runnable in CI" check.
- `__tests__/lib/chain/gateway-wire.test.ts` (12 tests): round trips of every wire object, and refusal of bad versions, statuses, reasons, uint64 overflow, leading zeros, out-of-range codes and malformed hashes or evidence.
- Coverage of the new code: `status-ladder.ts` 98% statements, `gateway/client.ts` 88%, `mock/chain.ts` 94%, `mock/http-server.ts` 81%.
- `6529 run typecheck:changed`, `6529 run lint:changed` (tight config) and `6529 run deadcode:knip` pass for this branch.
- Bundle impact: 0 bytes (no app importer). E2E: no route, control or copy changes, so no Playwright spec or pack is affected. None was run. The A4 Playwright test belongs to C4.

## Risk

- Level: Low
- Why: new files only. The HTTP mock binds to 127.0.0.1 by default, answers CORS only for loopback origins, and caps request bodies (16 KiB for transactions, 4 KiB for control).
- Rollback: revert the PR.

## Review Notes

- Wire format v0 (`/g/{id}/v0/tx`, `/v0/tx/{txId}`, `/v0/head`) is ours, not the design's. A real gateway RPC becomes another `GatewayTransport`.
- The mock does not verify Ed25519 or contract-wallet signatures, resolve grants, charge fees or run handlers. Those keys live in grant state it does not keep. Every included transaction succeeds unless a failure is injected.
- The default poll interval is one 12 s slot (P42). Tests inject a sleep that produces a block, so they use no timers.

author: djdeveloperr
body:
A fresh ALARM KDE install logged five warnings or failed units on every boot or shutdown that a Mac would show too. This PR fixes each where it starts. I measured all of them on the arch-kde payload from main `221cdb23` (image run 41516942760), booted under QEMU 10.2 (TCG) from an installer-shaped plaintext disk (`encrypt=0`). The "after" boot is the same disk after `pacman -U` of the packages built from this branch, the same way `packages.yml` builds them.

### 1. asahi-scripts installs its battery units executable

`macsmc-battery-charge-control-end-threshold.{path,service}` ship as `-rwxr-xr-x` in asahi-alarm's `asahi-scripts 20261023-1`. systemd warns every time PID 1 reads them. On a Mac that is every boot, because the battery's udev rule pulls the `.path` unit in with `SYSTEMD_WANTS=`. In QEMU there is no battery, so `systemctl list-unit-files` or `systemctl status` triggers it.

```
systemd[1]: Configuration file /usr/lib/systemd/system/macsmc-battery-charge-control-end-threshold.path is marked executable. Please remove executable permission bits. Proceeding anyway.
systemd[1]: Configuration file /usr/lib/systemd/system/macsmc-battery-charge-control-end-threshold.service is marked executable. Please remove executable permission bits. Proceeding anyway.
```

The cause is upstream's Makefile (`install -m0755` in `install-macsmc-battery`). AsahiLinux/asahi-scripts#73 reports it and AsahiLinux/asahi-scripts#75 fixes it. Neither is merged, and I did not open a duplicate. This branch carries asahi-alarm's recipe (PKGBUILDs 8648855, same 20261023 tarball and digest) with #75's patch as `asahi-scripts 20261023-2`. Its contents match asahi-alarm's package byte for byte, apart from the two file modes. The aurora repository comes first in `pacman.conf`, so this copy shadows asahi-alarm's later releases. Drop it once asahi-alarm ships the fix.

`check-basics.py` now fails an image with an executable unit file or drop-in. In the current KDE image the two battery units are the only ones.

Fedora's `asahi-battery-20250713-7.fc44` already ships both units `-rw-r--r--`. NixOS does not install them.

### 2. The real root's firmware handoff retry could never work

With no vendor firmware on the ESP (as in QEMU), the initrd step failed. That failure stays listed after switch-root. Then `aurora-peripherals.service` retried by mounting the ESP read-only at `/run/aurora-esp`, but `/boot/efi` already has it mounted read-write:

```
archlinux systemd[1]: aurora-vendor-firmware.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
alarm load-vendor-firmware[427]: mount: /run/aurora-esp: /dev/vda1 already mounted on /boot/efi.
alarm load-vendor-firmware[427]:       * vda1: Can't mount, would change RO state
alarm systemd[1]: aurora-peripherals.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
$ systemctl --failed
aurora-peripherals.service  loaded    failed failed Admit Aurora peripherals af…
aurora-vendor-firmware.ser… not-found failed failed aurora-vendor-firmware.serv…
```

The retry fails the same way with a valid `vendorfw/firmware.cpio` on the ESP (exit 32), so this is a real bug on a Mac whose initrd handoff fails, not only a QEMU artifact. `load-vendor-firmware` now:

- reads the ESP where it is already mounted (`findmnt --source /dev/disk/by-partuuid/…`) and mounts it only when it isn't;
- treats an ESP without `vendorfw/firmware.cpio` as nothing to hand off: it logs a warning and admits the peripherals, and the unit succeeds;
- in the initrd, logs a failed handoff and leaves the result to the real root's retry, since a failed initrd unit stays failed after switch-root even when the retry succeeds;
- extracts with `--unconditional`, so a retry replaces files from a failed attempt.

`aurora-firmware` 20261018-5. This code is not in aurora-platform. Each distro carries its own copy. NixOS has the same bug in `modules/firmware.nix` (aurora-silicon/nixos-aurora#110). Fedora uses dracut-asahi's handoff and has no runtime retry.

### 3. drkonqi's ordering cycle on every session stop

drkonqi 6.8 orders `drkonqi-coredump-cleanup.timer` after `timers.target` and `drkonqi-sentry-postman.path` after `default.target`. Their default dependencies order them before `timers.target` and `paths.target`. Every Plasma session stop, so every shutdown, hits the cycle and systemd deletes a stop job:

```
systemd[603]: basic.target: Found ordering cycle: default.target/stop after drkonqi-sentry-postman.path/stop after paths.target/stop after basic.target/stop - after default.target
systemd[603]: basic.target: Job default.target/stop deleted to break ordering cycle starting with basic.target/stop
systemd[603]: drkonqi-coredump-cleanup.timer: Found ordering cycle: timers.target/stop after drkonqi-coredump-cleanup.timer/stop - after timers.target
systemd[603]: drkonqi-coredump-cleanup.timer: Job timers.target/stop deleted to break ordering cycle starting with drkonqi-coredump-cleanup.timer/stop
```

Upstream bug. It came in with drkonqi commits 0988446f8 and af23df73e (6.7.90), and master still has it. It's [KDE bug 528003](https://bugs.kde.org/show_bug.cgi?id=528003), with a patch attached but no MR. A drop-in can't remove `After=`, so `aurora-system-fixes` sets `DefaultDependencies=no` on the two units and restores `Conflicts=`/`Before=shutdown.target`. Those are the only other default dependencies a user timer or path gets.

### 4. nm-dispatcher activation fails on every shutdown

```
dbus-broker-launch[408]: Activation request for 'org.freedesktop.nm_dispatcher' failed.
```

NetworkManager 1.58 dispatches `dns-change` and `connectivity-change` while it stops, whether or not any dispatcher scripts exist (the image has none). nm-dispatcher exits after 10 s idle, and once shutdown is queued systemd won't start it again. This is upstream behaviour: [NetworkManager issue 1643](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/NetworkManager/NetworkManager/-/work_items/1643), whose fix !2075 (drop the idle exit) was closed unmerged. The `dbus-org.freedesktop.nm-dispatcher.service` alias is correct. `aurora-system-fixes` adds a drop-in that runs `/usr/lib/nm-dispatcher --persist` and orders it `Before=NetworkManager.service`, so it stops after NetworkManager has exited.

### 5. Plasma Setup's autostart entry is executable

This one wasn't in the original list but comes from the same first boots:

```
systemd-xdg-autostart-generator[615]: Configuration file /run/plasma-setup/.config/autostart/plasma-setup.desktop is marked executable. Please remove executable permission bits. Proceeding anyway.
```

plasma-setup's tmpfiles line `Z /run/plasma-setup 0750 …` sets every file in the setup user's home to 0750 (upstream master too). The recipe now patches it to `~0750`, so directories stay 0750 and the files become 0640. `plasma-setup` 6.8.1-2. I could not build this package on the test host (no disk space for its KDE build dependencies). For the boot test I applied the patch's one-line change to the installed `/usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/plasma-setup-tmpfiles.conf`. The patch applies to the pinned 6.8.1 tarball, and CI builds the package.

### After

Packages: `asahi-scripts 20261023-2`, `aurora-firmware 20261018-5`, `aurora-system-fixes 1-6`, plus the tmpfiles line.

```
$ systemctl is-system-running

$ journalctl -b | grep -E 'vendor firmware|aurora-vendor-firmware|aurora-peripherals'

body:
## Task

ORB-21686 — Dashboard widen+narrow grant applies the widening, then reports the whole request refused when the narrowing step fails

### Description

Introduced by ORB-21672 (commit 4a616cfee, PR #7903). `grant_resident` in `crates/orbit-web/src/api/residents.rs` now splits a mixed widen+narrow call into two core calls: it raises and answers the widening request as the human (a committed authority change), then runs the narrowing call. The narrowing step is validated only afterwards in core (`narrow_resident_authority`, `crates/orbit-core/src/application/resident/grant.rs`): a `deadline` that is not earlier than the mandate's current deadline is refused (`deadline only shortens the mandate`), and an unparseable deadline is refused at input parsing. When that happens the `?` returns an error from the closure after the widening is already recorded. `resident_write` then audits the whole `resident.grant` as `refused` and the HTTP response is an error, so the operator and the audit log say nothing was changed while the mandate was widened. Before ORB-21672 the same mixed call was refused up front by core and wrote nothing, so this is a new partial-failure path. The dashboard JS (`operations-residents.js` grant handler) has the same shape: when the second `write` of widen-then-deadline is refused, only `Refused: ...` is shown and the success line for the widening is replaced, although the widening applied (the form re-render does show the new authority). Repro: POST `/api/residents/<id>/grant` on an `--operator` dashboard with `add:["dispatch"]`, a `quote`, and a `deadline` later than the mandate's current deadline. Expected: either nothing is applied, or the response and audit state that the widening was applied and only the narrowing was refused. Actual: HTTP error, audit `refused`, authority widened. Pre-validate the narrowing input (deadline parse and shortens-only check) before the widening, or report the partial outcome explicitly. Severity low: needs an invalid deadline alongside a widening; the effect is a misleading refusal over a real authority change. No test covers the second-step failure (the added test covers only success).

### Acceptance Criteria

- A dashboard grant that adds rights or workspaces and carries a deadline that core refuses (not earlier than the current deadline, or unparseable) either changes nothing or returns and audits an outcome that says the widening was applied and the narrowing was refused
- A regression test at the POST /api/residents/{id}/grant boundary covers a widen plus a later deadline and asserts the agreed behavior

## Screenshots

No screenshots attached.

Resumed candidate (test only) completed per plan step 2. Server: grant_resident mixed branch now catches narrowing failure after answered widening and returns 200 {outcome:granted_narrowing_refused, narrowing_error, request, authority, effective_authority}; resident_write audits that outcome as Failure with error_message Widening applied; narrowing refused: <reason>. Module API doc updated. JS: operations-residents.js mixed widen+deadline now single POST /grant and success line shows both outcomes (widened + narrowing refused, or widened+shortened). Regression test dashboard_mixed_grant_reports_applied_widening_when_deadline_is_refused covers later, equal, and unparseable deadlines asserting widened authority, unchanged deadline, no narrowed entry, and Failure audit. author: gabrielbosse1
body:
## What does this change?

One line in `src/main/resources/fabric.mod.json`: the `depends` entry `"fabric": ">=0.165.0"` becomes `"fabric-api": ">=0.165.0"`. This PR also adds `verification/` containing the real-server boot logs and the full diagnosis.

## Why

Every install failed with:

> Mod 'Discord Voice Bridge' (discord_voice_bridge) 1.0.0 requires version 0.165.0 or later of fabric, which is missing!

`fabric` is not a mod id: Fabric Loader's builtins are `fabricloader`, `minecraft` and `java`, and Fabric API's id is `fabric-api`. PR #1 already nested the correct `fabric-api-0.165.0+26.3.jar` (id `fabric-api`, 44 modules) and `fabric-permissions-api-0.7.0.jar` in the release jar, so the dependency was physically present the whole time — Loader aborted mod resolution before ever considering it. The installed PR #1 CI artifact is byte-identical to a fresh rebuild of current `main`, i.e. this is not a stale or duplicate jar on the user's side.

STEP 0 branch (a) was established from the installed artifact's metadata and by reproducing the exact error line on a real server, not guessed.

## Real-server verification (not a simulation)

A genuine Minecraft 26.3 Fabric dedicated server was booted with JDK 25.0.4.1, the real Mojang server jar (62,294,556 B, SHA-1 `33680f5f2ac32864d6d7cf5e56a705fdb3e05f4c`, matches the Mojang manifest), the official installer-generated 616-byte `fabric-server-launch.jar`, real Fabric Loader 0.20.1 + ASM 9.10.1 + sponge-mixin, `eula=true`, flat/offline `server.properties`, and `java -Dfabric.log.level=debug -Xmx2G -jar fabric-server-launch.jar nogui`.

| run | `mods/` | result |
|---|---|---|
| A | fixed jar only | `Loading 44 mods` with nested `fabric-api 0.165.0+26.3`, `Done (0.813s)!` |
| B | deliberately broken control (`"fabric"`) | exact user error, exits in 3 s, no `Done (` |
| C | fixed jar + standalone Fabric API 0.165.0+26.3 | `Loading 44 mods`, no duplicate-id clash, `Done (0.745s)!` |
| A2 / B2 / C2 | required re-run on the final artifact | `Done (0.940s)!` / exact user error / `Done (0.809s)!` |

Extra boots D (two copies of the mod in `mods/`), E (fixed + real Simple Voice Chat 2.6.27+26.3, `Loading 46 mods`) and F also reach `Done (`, eliminating the duplicate-jar and SVC suspects.

Full unabridged logs: `verification/logs/*.log`. Full report — hashes/sizes, `depends` and `jars` verbatim, every nested jar id+version including all 44 Fabric API modules, STEP 4 eliminations, minimal diff: `verification/REPORT.md`.

| artifact | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---|
| installed PR #1 CI jar | 21,161,849 | `e36df57ab9a46e4adced60c0f438fc53326668062ac0abd9128f965d5b6cecce` |
| final jar built from this branch's source | 21,161,849 | `b55fa1e9bd62da4350e55994a57100396ddc370f9746713ff8669a94457d24f9` |

The final jar is reproducible: a fresh `./gradlew clean build --no-daemon` from the committed source produced the identical sha256. Verified with Loader 0.20.1's own `VersionPredicateParser` that `>=0.165.0` accepts `0.165.0+26.3` (build metadata is ignored), so the version string was never the problem.

## Separate finding (out of scope, not fixed here)

After `Done (` the mod's `DiscordVoiceBridgeConfig.save()` throws `com.google.gson.JsonIOException` on Java 25 because it serializes non-`transient` `ReentrantReadWriteLock lock` and `Path configPath` fields. It happens after mod resolution, is unrelated to the dependency error, and every fixed run reaches `Done (` with no dependency error. Left out to keep this diff minimal; happy to follow up with `transient` fields / a config DTO and the same A/B/C re-run.

## Checklist

- [x] Build and tests pass: this PR's `ci.yml` run [41553084426](https://github.com/gabrielbosse1/discord-voice-bridge/actions/runs/41553084426) completed green with `./gradlew clean test build` on Java 25. The booted jar was additionally produced by `./gradlew clean build --no-daemon` on Temurin 25.0.5 / Gradle 9.8.2 / Loom 1.19.3 (`verification/final-build-PROVENANCE.txt`). Note: this sandbox cannot reach `services.gradle.org`, so the wrapper was executed in CI rather than in the sandbox.
- [x] No new dependencies — `build.gradle` is untouched.
- [x] No user-facing strings changed; nothing to add to `pt_br.json` / `en_us.json`.
- [x] AI-generated: yes, produced by an agent on Arena.ai. All artifacts and logs come from real builds and real `java -jar` boots; no synthetic or hand-written jars/logs were used.

author: dorelljames
body:
## Problem

Every service with functions failed to deploy in the run triggered by merging #97 ([run 41552612417](https://github.com/getcebby/cebby/actions/runs/41552612417)). Each job stopped before bundling with:

```
[inbucket] in supabase/config.toml is no longer supported. Use [local_smtp] instead.
```

`deploy-services.yml` installs the Supabase CLI with `version: latest`, and v3.0.0 became `latest` on 2026-11-02 at 12:18 UTC. All seven `services/*/supabase/config.toml` files have `[inbucket]`. `core` showed green only because it has no functions, so its deploy step was skipped.

## Change

- Pinned both jobs (functions and migrations) to CLI **2.122.0**. That was `latest` when the last successful deploy ran (2026-10-26, run 40268944477).
- No `config.toml` has changed since then, so this is a known-good combination.
- `ingest-watchdog.yml` already pins its CLI (2.100.0), so this follows existing practice.

## Not in this PR

- **Moving to CLI v3:** `[inbucket]` → `[local_smtp]` in seven configs, and `--project-ref` → `--remote` (deprecated, removed in v4), plus whatever else v3 changed. That needs its own tested change.

## After merge

Workflow-only changes don't match the `services/**` push filter, so the deploy has to be started by hand: `gh workflow run deploy-services.yml -f environment=production`. That redeploys every service. The only `services/` changes since the last good deploy are #97's.

body:
Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 W4A16 on Metal (M5 Max): prefill goes from about 40 tok/s to about 750-870, and MTP k2 becomes the 27B Metal default. Both defaults were approved by the user on 2026-11-02. The scoreboard's "27B ckpt does not load" was stale: the checkpoint already loaded on main.

## Defaults changed (27B on Metal only)
- `matmul_mxfp4_nax` for prompts above 8 rows: weights decode to bf16, then the existing fp8 NAX GEMM. `INTARSIA_METAL_MXFP4_NAX=0` turns it off.
- `[tuning.metal]` in `recipes/qwen3_5_vl.toml`: `prefill_chunk = 2048`, `busy_chunk = 256`, `mtp_default_k = 2`, `mtp_draft_vocab = 65536`. `--spec off` turns MTP off.

## Speed (served localeval, medians of 3, 1k / 4k / 16k)
| arm | prefill tok/s | decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| new defaults (#7974) | 768 / 869 / 728 | 27.5 / 26.8 / 22.1 |
| new defaults, rerun (#7998) | 813 / 747 / 661 | 29.4 / 25.3 / 19.1 |
| `--spec off`, rerun (#8021) | 702 / 759 / 698 | 21.7 / 20.2 / 17.3 |

Main's prefill was 40.9 / 39.5 at 1k / 4k from plain `generate`; 16k was not measured. Absolute speed drifted 10-20 % between windows with identical code, cause not found; an in-window A/B of two builds showed no difference. The MTP k2 gain is a range, about 1.10x to 1.35x in the control-last pairs, not the 1.17x first reported.

## Gates on the final merged build
- Accuracy against the HF W4A16 golden: prefill KL21 5.888e-4, top-1 99.51 %; decode KL21 9.556e-4, top-1 99.38 % (#7963). The golden was regenerated on endor; its sha256 differs from the provenance record, so the HIP comparison is the same recipe but not the same bytes.
- MMLU n=1425: 0.8161, against CUDA 0.818 and HIP 0.822 (#7970).
- MTP k2 and k3 greedy ids identical to `--spec off` on 4 pairs (#7966).
- `kernels test --backend metal`: 49 kernels, 972 cases, 0 FAIL (#7967). Workspace tests 1204 passed, 0 failed (#7968).
- `plan show` for 35B and Qwen3-8B on Metal identical to main (#7964).
- Peak memory at a 16k prompt: 2.68 GB max resident, 3.75 GB footprint above the 18 GB of weights (#7969).

## Not checked
- **`accuracy --mode reuse` at chunk 2048 cannot run:** the golden's longest prompt is 700 tokens, so every prompt is skipped and the gate reports FAIL. At chunk 512 one prompt runs and passes. As a substitute, a 4096-token prompt reusing 4095 cached tokens gave text identical to a fresh server over 48 tokens, on one prompt (#7989). The gate stays open until a 27B golden with a 4k prompt exists.
- `serve --max-batch` above 1, W4A4 on Metal, 32k context, GSM8K.

## Summary

PR 3 of HOST-008 (spec `specs/HOST-008-host-serve-mode/`, #525): `host serve` keeps running through outages and reports them. Stacked on #558 (PR 2); it retargets as the stack merges. `host check` published, the auth key file guard and the docs follow in PR 4, which closes #522.

Refs #522

## Changes

- `internal/serve/bootstrap.go`: `Supervisor` restarts a dead SSH bootstrap with exponential backoff from `DialBackoffBase` (1 s) to `DialBackoffMax` (30 s) with jitter, resets after a recovery, reports each outage once (`ERROR reason=ssh_bootstrap_failed`) and marks readiness down meanwhile. `Health` folds per-source readiness into `/health/ready`.
- `internal/serve/control.go`: `WatchControlSession` reads the node's IPN bus; any state other than `Running` reads not ready with `reason=control_plane_unreachable`. tsnet's control client does the reconnecting.
- `internal/health`: `Handler` with an optional `Report` adds `node` and `services [{kind, port, published}]` to `/health/ready`; without one the body is connect's, unchanged.
- `cmd/cli/host_serve.go`: wires the supervisor, the control watcher and the health server on `host.mesh.health_addr`; serve no longer exits when the bootstrap dies after READY (AC4, AC6 server side).
- Production diff 336 lines (`*_test.go` and specs excluded), mostly doc comments; the rest of the original PR 3 moved to PR 4 to stay near the cap.

author: juanccadavid
body:
## Qué cambia

**Modelo de abandono (`make abandono`)**: además de Ridge y KMeans ahora entrena, con el mismo preprocesador y las mismas variables sin fuga:

| Modelo | Tipo |
|---|---|
| Ridge | lineal |
| Regresión logística | lineal |
| Random Forest | **bagging** |
| HistGradientBoosting | **boosting** (estilo LightGBM) |

Reutiliza `get_models` y `build_pipeline` de `models.py`. Imprime una tabla comparativa sobre los asociados nuevos, guarda un `.joblib` por modelo y la matriz de confusión pasa a 5 paneles.

**PyCaret (`make pycaret`, opcional)**: `scripts/comparar_pycaret.py` le da las mismas variables a PyCaret, que arma solo el preprocesamiento y compara `lr`, `rf`, `et`, `ada`, `gbc` y `lightgbm` con validación cruzada. Después valida sus mejores modelos y los nuestros con los mismos asociados nuevos.

## Ojo

- **PyCaret 4.0 alfa** (`==4.0.0a8`): la estable 3.3 exige `pandas<2.2`, `joblib<1.4` y `matplotlib<3.8`, incompatibles con el proyecto. Va como extra opcional (`uv sync --extra pycaret`), así que no lo instalan `make setup` ni el CI, y su prueba se salta sola si no está instalado.
- La API de la 4.0 cambió: no hay `setup()`, se usa `ClassificationExperiment(...).fit(X, y)`. Codifica las categóricas con OrdinalEncoder (no OneHot) y no compensa el desbalance.
- El lock baja `ipython` de 9.17 a 8.39 para todos, porque PyCaret pide `ipython<9`. Ningún otro paquete cambia de versión.
- PyCaret escribe `logs.log` en la carpeta actual: quedó en `.gitignore`.

## Resultados (entrenando con `data/ejemplo`, 50 filas; validando con 1000 nuevos)

| | ROC-AUC | Recall | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ridge | 0.853 | 0.731 | 0.651 |
| Regresión logística | 0.946 | 0.843 | 0.813 |
| Random Forest (bagging) | 0.962 | 0.410 | 0.580 |
| HistGB (boosting) | 0.853 | 0.750 | 0.674 |
| PyCaret `et` | 0.964 | 0.675 | 0.785 |

Con tan pocos datos los árboles ordenan bien (AUC alto) pero con umbral 0.5 se pierden retiros. LightGBM en PyCaret no logra dividir (AUC 0.5 con 35 filas): es el riesgo de sobreajuste/subajuste en datasets pequeños.

## Pruebas

- `ruff check` y `ruff format --check` limpios.
- `pytest`: 111 pasan y 1 se salta (PyCaret, sin el extra, igual que en el CI). Con `--extra pycaret` también pasa.

author: akhileshthite
body:
- **Back.** One Back now leaves a YouTube video and goes back to the list. YouTube adds `&ra=m` to a video's address after it opens, and the tab took that as a new page, so the video was in the tab twice. Now a page that rewrites its address, closes its own popup with Back, or redirects with `location.replace` stays one step, as in Safari and Chrome. The page says what it did through the Navigation API where the WebView has it (Chrome's WebView and newer iPhones), and older iPhones get a fallback. Its reports carry the tab's token, like the hyper bridge's, and a page can only change its own steps.
- **Redirects.** A page that redirects while it loads no longer stays blank.
- **History.** A search bar finds pages by title or address. Days are headings, each page shows its time, and buttons along the top show one day at a time. The trash button clears the last hour, today, today and yesterday, the day picked, or everything, and each choice says how many pages it clears. Tabs closed in that time go from Recently closed too. The new text is in all 24 languages.
- **PeerChat on Android.** When the system stops PeerSky while the phone is locked, PeerChat connects at the unlock, where it stayed offline saying it connects when you unlock your phone. It tries again a few seconds later and each minute while the phone stays unlocked.

author: r7kamura
body:
## Problem

The version bump workflow differs from the bump-request workflow used in other r7kamura repositories, and it merges the bump pull request and runs the release workflow automatically, leaving no chance to review the bump before release.

## Cause

.github/workflows/bump.yml was implemented as a custom script that creates, merges, and releases in one run, instead of using r7kamura/bump-request.

To fix this, the following should change:

- Replace .github/workflows/bump.yml with .github/workflows/bump-request.yml that uses r7kamura/bump-request.
- Keep reading and updating the version in src/manifest.json.

## Changes

### Implementation

- Remove .github/workflows/bump.yml.
- Add .github/workflows/bump-request.yml, which takes a required version input and runs r7kamura/bump-request@v0.7.1 with a command that updates only the version line in src/manifest.json.
- Update .github/workflows/actions.lock with gh actions-lock.

### For users

- No impact on users.
- For release work, run the bump-request workflow from the Actions page with the next version (e.g. 0.5.2). It creates a pull request that changes the version in src/manifest.json, and merging it triggers the existing release workflow.

author: ryan-mistt
body:
## Problem

Agent and shell children inherit every variable of the runner's environment. A caller that needs the child environment to be an explicit list cannot ask for one.

## Change

- New option `--env-allow <NAME>` (repeatable). With it, only the named parent variables are passed to agent and shell children.
- Still present, because the runner or the recipe sets them: the `HOME` and `PATH` fallback defaults, the session-tree variables (`AMPLIHACK_SESSION_DEPTH`, `AMPLIHACK_MAX_DEPTH`, `AMPLIHACK_MAX_SESSIONS`, `AMPLIHACK_TREE_ID`), `AMPLIHACK_AGENT_BINARY`, a step's `env:` block and `RECIPE_VAR_*`. `CLAUDECODE` is never passed, even if named.
- The restriction applies in `build_child_env_with`, so the CLI-subprocess agent path, the Codex agent path and the shell path all use it.
- Library: `CLISubprocessAdapter::with_env_allow`.
- **Default unchanged:** without the option every parent variable is inherited as before.

author: clmoralesl
body:
### Descripcion
Corrige los dos defectos de los scripts de despliegue en AWS detectados en el redespliegue del 2026-10-26.

**1. `infra/aws-ec2/scripts/bootstrap-apps.sh`**
Terraform procesa el archivo con `templatefile` y trata todo `${...}` como interpolacion propia, por lo que la linea 58 (`${RUTAEXPRESS_SECRETO_INTERNO:-...}`, introducida en #69) hacia fallar `terraform plan`. Se escapa como `$${...}`; Terraform entrega al servidor la sintaxis de shell original. Las demas interpolaciones (`RABBITMQ_PRIVATE_IP`, `KAFKA_PRIVATE_IP`, `API_GATEWAY_URL`) son variables legitimas de Terraform y no cambian. No hay directivas `%{`.

**2. `infra/aws-ec2/inyectar_wallet.ps1`**
En Windows PowerShell 5.1, con `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"`, cuando PowerShell captura el stderr de un programa externo, cada linea se convierte en `NativeCommandError` y aborta el script aunque el programa termine con 0. El progreso de `docker compose` cortaba la sesion SSH a mitad de la recreacion y dejaba cuatro servicios detenidos con nombres temporales.
- Nueva funcion `Invoke-ComandoNativo`: ejecuta `terraform`, `scp` y `ssh` con preferencia local `Continue` y decide el exito por `$LASTEXITCODE`. Ante un fallo real muestra un mensaje claro y termina con el codigo del programa.
- En el servidor, `docker compose up -d` agrega `--no-build` (reutiliza las imagenes del bootstrap), `--force-recreate` (garantiza que los contenedores relean el wallet) y `2>&1`.
- Verificacion final por SSH: los cuatro contenedores (envios, catalogo, auditoria, BFF) deben estar `Up` con su nombre normal; si no, el script termina con codigo 2.

**3. `infra/aws-ec2/README.md`**
Paso de inyeccion del wallet y seccion "Recuperacion tras una inyeccion interrumpida" con `docker compose up -d --no-build --force-recreate`.

No se modifican contrasenas: el retiro de contrasenas de `bootstrap-apps.sh` corresponde al #94, que toca el mismo archivo y se fusiona despues de este.

Closes #96

---

### Criterios de Aceptacion Validados
- [x] La plantilla se renderiza sin errores con `terraform console` (codigo 0) y el script resultante pasa `bash -n`.
- [ ] `terraform validate` / `terraform plan`: no verificado localmente; `validate` falla por el proveedor AWS ("Plugin did not respond"), ajeno al cambio.
- [x] `inyectar_wallet.ps1` sin errores de sintaxis en PowerShell 5.1 (`Parser::ParseFile`).
- [x] Prueba simulada: un programa que escribe en stderr y termina con 0 ya no aborta el script; un fallo simulado de `ssh` (codigo 255) termina con mensaje claro y codigo 255; la verificacion de contenedores rechaza nombres temporales.
- [ ] Prueba en un despliegue completo en AWS Academy: **no verificado en AWS** (infraestructura destruida desde el 2026-10-28).
- [x] Compilacion: no aplica (solo scripts y documentacion).
- [x] Pruebas unitarias: no aplica; se reemplazaron por las verificaciones anteriores.

author: catduckgnaf
body:
## Summary and user impact

Part 2 of #792 (parts 1 and 3 shipped in #796): the Discord filament flows can no longer bind the wrong spool quietly. Every filament picker now shows one consistent label shape, a color that parses to garble gets a confirm-or-correct step instead of being minted into a spool record, replaced spools default to the shelf with archive only as an explicit named choice, and the picker paths that bound on selection alone now confirm the exact spool first.

## Problem and cause

For a bug fix: describe the observed problem and the verified cause. For other changes, remove this section or write "Not applicable."

The motivating session is recorded on #792: picker options mixed bare colors, color+material labels, and parse garble ("term NoPLA+ Natural"); the first pick bound spool #18 "Rose red blue green PLA" to slot 2 and it was later archived while the spool it replaced merely went to the shelf; several paths bound a spool the moment a picker option was selected, with no confirmation naming the exact spool.

## Proposed changes

- One label shape everywhere: `spool_picker_label()` in `discord_print_summary.py` renders "color · material · #id · grams left" (unknowns are said in place: "grams unknown", "color unknown"). Applied to every filament picker found in the audit:
  - `print_alert_buttons.insertion_select_options` (insertion "Existing spool" select and the spool-question replacement select) — previously "#id <name+material> <grams> g" with grams silently dropped when unknown.
  - `print_alert_buttons.intake_color_options` (color/finish picker) — all options now "color · material"; the option value stays the exact color string (the #796 contract).
  - The guided change shelf picker in `plugins/print-feedback` — lines and registered choices both normalized; typed legacy "#id name" answers still resolve.
  - `_spool_type_label` (guided-new filament-type picker) — "color · material · brand" (a type has no spool number or grams).
  - `moonraker_event_listener.spool_display_label` (#483 prompt, slot question, load confirmation) and the runout recovery offers (`compatible_offers`, `manual_resume_tracking_message`).
  - Slot pickers (`_spool_slot_ask`, `new_spool_slot_options`) keep slot labels; a fully recorded slot's current-contents description now uses the normalized spool label.
  - Audited and deliberately unchanged: `slot_load.py` (no picker), intake brand/swatch options (not spool pickers), `spool_sync.list_text`/`loaded_text` (inventory listings, not pickers), model-part color selection (not a filament picker).
- Parsed-color sanity: `filament_color.color_sanity()` / `color_sanity_text()` flag a parse yielding multiple colors, unrecognized fragment words beside a recognized color, or a truncated fragment, and name what was understood. Wired as:
  - a `colorcheck` step in the #512 intake walkthrough (picker-picked, typed-modal, and label-photo colors all pass it before weight/disposition/confirm);
  - a confirm-or-correct question with a re-type loop on the guided-new typed-color path;
  - a named refusal in spool-question text answers and in the one-shot `/spool new` (which has no confirmation step, so it refuses and offers the guided form).
  A lone unreadable name (e.g. "Galaxy") is deliberately not flagged — the existing swatch step handles it.
- Shelf vs archive: the audit found every `bind_slot` call site already defaults the displaced spool to the shelf, with archive/depleted/delete only from explicit disposition choices named in confirmations; the runout-only depleted pattern is retained as documented runout behavior and, on the Discord select path, is now named in the new bind confirmation.
- Bind confirmations: the insertion and spool-question selects previously bound on selection alone. They now land on a confirmation (`pbbindconfirm`) naming the exact spool — re-read from Spoolman — plus the displaced spool's fate; only "Confirm bind" writes. The guided change confirmation and the guided-new load path gained the same exact-spool confirmation.
- Phrase corpus grown from #796: runtime suggestion pins ("please swap the roll", "I need to replace a filament roll"), guided NL phrases ("please swap the roll", "replace a spool", "I want to change the filament"), and a garble corpus for `color_sanity` ("Rose red blue green", "term NoPLA+ Natural", "term No...", plus clean negatives).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] User facing feature
- [ ] Maintenance or refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI or tests
- [ ] Breaking change

## Verification and test results

- Checks run:
  - Local full `tests/hermes`: 1641 passed, 3 skipped, 11 subtests passed (finished log on the pre-rebase head; the rebase onto main 1482639 was conflict-free and touched no overlapping logic).
  - Local after the rebase: `tests/hermes/test_issue_792_picker_hardening.py` (new) + `test_spool_guided.py` + `test_issue_512_intake.py` + `tests/bot/test_runtime.py` — 167 passed (finished log).
  - Local `tests/core tests/bot`: 1149 passed, 8 skipped.
  - Existing #512/#514 walkthrough tests were updated to click through the new colorcheck step; the runout multi-color guard test now passes its walkthrough answer with `color_confirmed`, matching the new sanity gate.
  - CI on this exact head: checked before merge.
- Checks not run and why:
  - No live Discord or printer checks: the flows are covered by the offline suites; live use is the operator's normal Discord session.

## Risks, limitations, and follow up

- The extra confirmation step on insertion/spool-question selects adds one click to those flows — deliberate: binding the wrong spool was the failure being fixed.
- The Web UI has no spool picker today (that is #789's scope), so no Web UI picker was normalized here.

## Related issues

- Related: #796 (parts 1 and 3), #798, #512, #514, #475
- Fixes: #792 (Closes #792 — part 2 was the only remaining part; the issue's reopening comment tracks exactly this scope)

## Scope and acceptance criteria

- Acceptance criteria:
  - Every filament picker shows options in one consistent shape. (Audit list above; covered by the new tests.)
  - A spool whose color parses to multiple colors or a fragment cannot be created without an explicit confirm-or-correct step. (colorcheck/refusal paths; garble corpus tests.)
  - Replacing a spool sends the displaced one to the shelf unless the operator explicitly chooses archive; the confirmation says which. (Audit + named fates in confirmations.)
  - The part 1/3 acceptance items were delivered by #796 and are not reopened here.
- Out of scope / remaining work:
  - Web UI spool pickers (#789); HelixScreen inbound sync (#791).

## User-facing release note

Filament pickers in Discord now all read the same way — color, material, spool number and grams left — so similar spools are easy to tell apart. A color that looks like a parsing mistake (several colors in one name, or a cut-off fragment) now gets a "did you mean this?" check before any spool is created, swapping a spool sends the old one back to the shelf unless you explicitly choose archive, and picking a spool from the insertion or replacement lists asks you to confirm the exact spool before anything is bound.

## Safety, compatibility and deployment

- Safety/compatibility impact: Confirmation coverage increases (two select paths gain a confirm step); no confirmation is removed and no print/readiness guard changes. Typed legacy picker answers still resolve, so existing habits keep working.
- Live checks or deployments performed (or "None"): None.

## Documentation and attribution

- [x] Relevant setup, configuration and user documentation updated, or reason given below.
- [x] Contributor credit and third-party licenses preserved where applicable; no invented coauthors.
- [x] No credentials, private model files or personal runtime records included.

## Documentation impact

Documentation: not needed
Reason: This is behavior hardening of existing Discord flows with n

author: timogilvie
body:
## Summary
`src/lineage/weight_commitment.py` and hokusai-token's `scripts/lib/weight-commitment.js` both claimed `sha256-merkle-v1` but built different trees:

| | Leaf | Odd node | Single file |
|---|---|---|---|
| hokusai-token (set on-chain `weightGenesis`) | `sha256(utf8(path) ‖ 0x00 ‖ sha256(bytes))` | paired with itself | hashed as a leaf |
| this repo (before) | `sha256(bytes)` | duplicated | root = file digest |

Every DeltaOne MintRequest built here would have reverted on chain with `LineageParentMismatch`. This PR switches to the on-chain scheme. The exclusion rules (`MLmodel`, `metadata/`, `registered_model_meta`, symlinks) already matched and are unchanged. The algorithm ID stays `sha256-merkle-v1`, because the JS library and the on-chain values are the reference.

## Evidence (real MLflow artifacts from S3)
| Model 30 | Before | After | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| v5 (`m-c602ac9b…`) | `0xc504…a192` | `0xce7f…554c` | = mainnet `weightGenesis(30)` and current head |
| v8 (`m-f53c99cd…`) | `0x7b71…c554` | `0x9600…5d93` | = JS library output |

## Changes
- Path-bound leaves, UTF-8 byte ordering, odd-node self-pairing, no single-leaf shortcut.
- New `commitment_from_file_digests()` to check a manifest (path + file SHA-256) without the bytes.
- `tests/fixtures/weight_commitment/conformance_vectors.json`, three vectors:
  - hokusai-token's pinned Sepolia rehearsal fixture, with real bytes
  - the mainnet v5 genesis manifest
  - v8
- Updated the two unit tests that pinned the old leaf rule, and added tests for rename-in-same-order and odd-count pairing.

- [x] Commitment users: `test_technical_task_router.py`, `test_compute_weight_genesis.py`, `test_gate3_offchain_pipeline.py` (85 passed)

author: shoko-official
body:
Based on https://github.com/Shoko-official/StudentLLM/pull/427, which is still open, so this PR targets its branch. Retarget it to `main` once that PR merges.

## Summary

A wide inline formula with no break point was cut off in chat by `.chat-scroll { overflow-x: hidden }`. In notes it widened the page: 1240 px at 300 and 375 px, 1622 px at 1280 px. Wide display math, headings and tables also overflowed the notes column.

KaTeX can only break a formula between its runs (`.katex-base`), and CSS cannot tell whether a run fits its line. `RichText` now measures this after layout, again when the KaTeX fonts arrive, and when its width changes. A formula with a run wider than its line gets `.katex-scrolls`: it sits on its own line, scrolls, has a tab stop, and still wraps at operators inside.

Other changes:

- The note column has a bounded track (`grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)`).
- Markdown tables scroll in every view. Cell text no longer breaks one letter per line, and a short table now takes its content width in notes.
- A formula block no longer pushes the start of a wide formula out of reach by centring it.
- In notes, display math and tables take a tab stop only when they overflow.
- In plain-text notes the `role="img"` element is the scroller, because focus inside that role would not reach assistive technology.

## Why it measures

Only formulas that need it become scrollers, because a scroller clips ink KaTeX draws outside its boxes on purpose (`\mathclap`, `\rlap`, `\smash`, negative spaces, and `\neq` or `\notin` through their laps). I tried and rejected two simpler designs:

- **`overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: hidden` on blocks:** cuts glyphs such as `\overbrace`, as the task warned.
- **A scroller on every run, with `inline-flex` and negative margins:** this was the first version of this branch and never reached the remote. Independent review measured glyph loss in formulas that fit (`x\stackrel{\mathclap{...}}{=}y` lost 195 of 559 ink pixels), a scrollbar that could not be dragged when runs stacked, and keyboard focus inside `aria-hidden`. Excluding laps by class could not work, because `\neq` and `\mathrel{\rlap{..}}` produce the same markup.

## Verification

- [x] `npm run check`
- [x] `npm run benchmarks:check`
- [x] `npm run test:run`
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm run test:e2e` (UI path affected)
- [ ] provider smoke check: not affected, no real model or key used

The full `npm run verify` passes: 907 unit tests, 113 Chromium e2e tests with 1 skipped, 5 CSP tests, and the Python checks.

`tests/e2e/wide-math.spec.ts` is new and runs in Chromium. It covers:

- **Matrix:** chat and imported Markdown notes, at 300, 375 and 1280 px, light and dark. No page overflow beyond the 20 px at 300 px from `body { min-width: 320px }`, every scroller's start and end reachable, and no formula cut off without one.
- **Pixels:** each scroller and display formula is compared with itself at `overflow: visible` across its scroll range, allowing at most 2 lost ink pixels per step.
- **Formulas that fit:** no scroller and no tab stop, including 24 constructs whose ink leaves their boxes, and small formulas in lines that shrink to fit them (table cells, user messages, formula blocks).
- **Behaviour:** keyboard scrolling, axe, a draggable scrollbar with classic scrollbars visible, and following the page width.

The measuring logic and the main CSS rules were removed or altered in turn, and a test failed each time. The rules no test pins are listed under limitations. That check also caught gaps in the tests themselves: the vertical padding looked unnecessary until a 3 px clip of `\overbrace{...}^{n}` showed up in notes in dark mode, so it stayed.

Fonts matter to the measurement: the same run measures 609 px while they load and 732 px once loaded. One measuring pass over 1500 formulas takes about 6 ms. Relayout times with and without the refit on that document were within noise. In the worst case, where every formula crosses the threshold at once, review measured about 3 ms per `RichText` instance.

Independent adversarial review: REQUEST_CHANGES on the first design, REQUEST_CHANGES on the redesign (false scrollers on small formulas in shrink-wrapped lines, now fixed), then APPROVE with one test to add. That test now pins both sides of the allowance below.

## Limitations and risks

- **Chromium on Windows only.** WebKit and Linux were not run, and neither was a screen reader. Chromium makes overflowing scrollers focusable by itself; here they also get an explicit tab stop.
- **Formula layout:** a formula with a run too wide for the line now starts on a new line.
- **Ink still lost in a scroller:** it cannot show ink beyond its padding. A long `\mathllap` or `\hspace{-3em}` at the very start of an already wide run loses that ink (375 of 1699 ink pixels for `\mathllap{abcdefgh}`), and a deep `\smash[b]{\underbrace{..}_{..}}` beside a wide run loses part of it (about 70 px).
- **Allowance:** `scrollWidth` counts the 2 px each KaTeX stack hangs past its box, plus rounding, so a run counts as wide only when it passes the line by more than 3 px. Stacks measured at most 2.5 px across sizes, scales and nesting. So an unmarked run can pass the text column by about 3.4 px. In chat this relies on the 4 px gutter, and pixel checks there found no loss where the control could detect one.
- **False scrollers remain in shrink-wrapped lines** for laps and trailing negative spaces, such as `\cancel{xy}`, `x^2_i\!` and `\mathrel{\rlap{ab}}x` in a table cell. They add a tab stop and some height, with no ink lost. `x\rlap{ab}` or `\mathclap{abc}` there does get a real scrollbar, and its ink is cut until scrolled; the left half of `\mathclap` cannot be reached.
- **Focus and scroll position:** focus drops to the body if a focused scroller stops scrolling because the page widened. `scrollLeft` resets when the content changes, which predates this PR (`components` is rebuilt per render).
- **Fonts after a hidden mount:** a `RichText` mounted while hidden, then shown while fonts are still loading, is not measured again when they arrive. Nothing in the app mounts it that way today.
- **Console notice:** review saw "ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications" twice across 323 viewports. It looks harmless.
- **Cosmetic:** in notes, text after a scroller keeps its leading space.
- **Not pinned by a test:** `overflow-y: hidden` on `.katex-scrolls` (review removed it and nothing failed). `overflow-y: hidden` on `.latex-block` and tables, `overflow-wrap: normal` on table cells and `scrollbar-width: thin` were checked by eye only, or not mutated.

## Checklist

- [x] tests added or the reason is documented
- [x] documentation updated when public behavior changes (`CHANGELOG.md`)
- [x] diff reviewed for unrelated noise

author: wired-square-garth[bot]
body:
**Wire fix.** The device encodes a frame-definition signal as 17 bytes, with `quantity` (u8) at offset 8 (ws-framelink `lib/framelink/frame_def.c`; `FL_SIGNAL_DEF_ENTRY_SIZE` in `rule_entry.h`). The host had 16 bytes since framelink-rs. So FRAME_DEF_ADD was NACKed INVALID_PAYLOAD for any definition with a signal, and FRAME_DEF_RESP misparsed from the first signal on. `FrameSignalDef` gains `quantity` (a `types::QTY_*`, or'd with `QTY_PER_SECOND` for a rate), and encode and parse use 17-byte signals. The golden wires change only by that byte.

**Refusals.** `build_frame_def_add` returns `Result`, and refuses three things before sending:
- a signal whose `bit_length` is outside 1 to `SIGNAL_MAX_BITS` (64): `Error::SignalBits`;
- more signals than `MAX_SIGNALS` (255) fit in the count byte, which used to be truncated: `Error::TooManySignals`;
- `RESERVED_IDS`, the signal store's `FRAME_DEF_ID_USER` (0xFFFE) and `FRAME_DEF_ID_DEVICE` (0xFFFF), which the device refuses: `Error::ReservedFrameDefId`. `frame_def::next_available_id` skips them.

The device's advertised per-frame signal cap (`MAX_SIGNALS_PER_FRAME`, default 16) is for callers that hold its capabilities.

**Versions.** `FrameSignalDef` has public fields, so wslib-framelink-protocol goes to 0.2.0. wslib-framelink-board, wslib-framelink and wslib-instruments expose protocol types, so they go to 0.2.0 with dependency floors of 0.2.

author: neo-desktop
body:
Adds classic AmigaOS to the clang-dos package, so it is a redistributable Amiga SDK as well.

## What changes
- `build-llvm.sh` builds the experimental M68k target and ships `llvm-elf2hunk`, which the driver runs to make hunk executables. This changes the LLVM cache key, so the first run rebuilds LLVM.
- `build-sysroot.sh m68k-amigaos` runs amiga-sdk's `build-sysroot.sh` (picolibc with its AmigaOS layer and the compiler-rt builtins, for the 68000). It runs in the DOS sysroot job and takes a few minutes, so no new job is added.
- `assemble.sh` puts the sysroot in `m68k-amigaos/` next to `bin/`, which is where the driver looks. It copies `amiga-ndk.py`, `lha.py`, `fd2stub.py`, the Amiga examples and the README into `share/clang-dos`.
- `bin/amiga.cfg` is new. `smoke-test.sh` builds `hello.c` for the 68000, 68020 and 68040 and runs each one in vamos, which the workflow installs from pip.
- `toolchain.yml` takes an `amiga_sdk_ref` input. BRANCHES.txt and the nightly's change check now list amiga-sdk.

## What is not in the package
None of the NDK, Kickstart or Workbench files are included. `amiga-ndk.py` downloads NDK 3.2 from Aminet (with a SHA-256 check) and installs its headers and `libamiga.a` into `m68k-amigaos/`. Plain C programs build without it.

## Depends on
- clang-dos/llvm#20 (68000 codegen fixes, sysroot builtins)
- clang-dos/picolibc#10 (AmigaOS layer)
- clang-dos/amiga-sdk#2 (`build-sysroot.sh`, `amiga-ndk.py`)

CI here goes green only after those three are merged.

## Testing
I tested this locally with a mock package layout: `bin/clang --config=amiga.cfg`, with the sysroot holding only crt0, libc, libm and the builtins (no NDK). The build linked, and vamos printed `Hello, world from smoke! 42 123456789 3.25` for each of the 68000, 68020 and 68040 builds.
