author: mgyamada
body:
The function checker previously validated each recorded call but could accept an independently audited pass with a missing record. Dispatch records also lacked the emitted function ID. The checker now reconstructs call occurrences from every returned Core body and compares counts, in both directions, by unique caller specialization and emitted target ID. An omitted repeated call cannot borrow another call's record.

Generic targets are recognized from the actual target origin and reconstructed method/key definition table. Each dispatch record must match the caller's lexical body scope, the finite winner and its emitted origin. The public `CallCoverage.legacy_wire`, `indexed_wire` and `resource_wire` corollaries cover the exact audit/executable Cores of protocols 2–9, including resource pure fragments. The matching unit is caller specialization + target + multiplicity; this does not claim a bijection of distinct source locations, source operational correspondence or native refinement.

Regressions remove all/one repeated record, duplicate records, forge callers and emitted targets, remove calls from the actual Core, duplicate specialization identities and cover both branches. No public syntax or wire change. A separate documentation clarification identifies backend Lean `UInt64` and the planned Vastitas source name `U64`; the latter remains unimplemented.

Partial #432: numerical schedule-to-origin occurrence coverage and full source correspondence remain open. Stacked on #501 for focused review; merge to main only after predecessor integration and final-head CI/review.

Validation:
- Rust fmt, strict locked all-target Clippy, `cargo test --locked --all-targets`: 401 passed / 13 optional numerical tests ignored / 38 suites, including all four 20,000-function watchdog shapes.
- Kernel 189 jobs, complete regressions 155, oracle 197, axiom audit 30,470 declarations / 4,119 private plus strict least-fuel audit.
- Indexed native: 23 standalone fixtures. Storage native: preflight, layouts, aliases, all 144 regroup pairs, failure cleanup, FFI Unit, 13 guard theorems and 5,488 layout / 13 narrowing cases passed.
- Documentation equality/size, compiler/oracle boundaries and complete diff checks passed.
- On an uncontrolled macOS arm64 host, 4,000-function chain/shared graphs (with/without a lambda) added roughly 0.8–3.4% to the observed median kernel check time. All 32 warmup/sample checks passed; commands, hashes and raw timings are in `experiments/compiler_scaling/results/2026-11-03-macos-call-coverage/`. This measures compiler cost, not generated-program performance.

author: devkimhongjin
body:
## 요약
저장소를 연결하면 README에 CodeArchive 정보가 들어가도록 합니다. 대시보드에서 새 저장소나 브랜치 연결이 서버에 저장되면, 서버가 **저장된 연결 대상**의 루트 README에 아래 블록을 넣습니다.

```
<!-- codearchive:start -->
[![Automated by CodeArchive](https://img.shields.io/badge/Automated%20by-CodeArchive-685ca9)](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/codearchive/mlhibjadcbklfdllkonhjjajhmhnoalj)

이 저장소의 알고리즘 풀이는 [CodeArchive](...)로 관리합니다. 지원 사이트에서 PASS한 풀이가 설정에 따라 자동 수집·동기화·커밋됩니다.
<!-- codearchive:end -->
```

## 동작
- **위치:** README 첫 줄이 `#` 제목이면 그 바로 아래, 아니면 맨 위에 넣습니다. CRLF와 BOM은 유지합니다.
- **이미 있을 때:** 표시 주석으로 블록을 찾아 그 자리에서만 갱신합니다. 사용자가 옮긴 위치는 유지되고, 내용이 같으면 커밋하지 않습니다(`UNCHANGED`).
- **README가 없을 때:** CodeArchive `README.md`를 만듭니다(`CREATED`). 빈 저장소의 "README로 초기화" 내용(`INITIAL_README`)에도 같은 블록이 들어가므로 이어서 중복 커밋되지 않습니다.
- **건너뛰는 경우:** 보호된 브랜치, 아직 없는 브랜치(첫 풀이 커밋 전 빈 저장소), 마크다운이 아니거나 여러 개인 README, 깨진 표시 주석, 64KB 초과 README는 쓰지 않고 `SKIPPED`와 이유를 돌려줍니다. 대시보드는 이유를 토스트로 알립니다.
- **트리거:** 저장소·브랜치가 바뀐 연결이 서버에 확인됐을 때 한 번만 실행됩니다. 같은 대상에서 폴더만 바꾸거나 다른 설정을 저장하면 다시 쓰지 않습니다.
- **끄는 방법:** 폴더 선택 단계에 "연결하면 README에 CodeArchive 배지 추가" 체크박스(기본 켜짐)가 있습니다. README에 쓰지 못해도 연결은 유지됩니다.

## 구현
- `POST /api/github/targets/readme-section`: 요청 본문 없이 서버에 저장된 설치·저장소·브랜치만 씁니다. 저장소 ID도 설치 토큰으로 owner/name을 찾아 정하므로, 브라우저가 다른 대상을 지정할 수 없습니다.
- 쓰기는 기존 `addFile`(새 파일만 생성)과 `replaceFile`(읽은 head·blob과 같을 때만, 강제 갱신 없이)을 그대로 씁니다. 커밋 작성자는 다른 쓰기와 같이 저장소 소유자입니다.

## 확인한 것
- 대시보드 `npm test` 285개 통과(새 테스트 2개: 연결 후 한 번만 호출, 체크박스를 끄면 호출 안 함), `npm run typecheck` 통과.
- 서버 테스트 추가: `GithubReadmeSectionTest`(삽입 위치, CRLF·BOM, 이동한 블록 갱신, 깨진 표시 주석), `GithubFileAdditionTest`(추가·갱신·변경 없음·새 README·보호 브랜치·지원하지 않는 README를 가짜 GitHub로 검증), `GithubTargetControllerTest`(저장된 대상만 사용).
- 로컬에 Java 8만 있어서 **서버 테스트는 이 PR의 CI에서 처음 실행됩니다.**

## 미확인
- 실제 GitHub 저장소에서 배지 표시와 커밋 기록.
- 사용자에게 반영하려면 서버 배포와 확장 새 버전(대시보드 포함)이 모두 필요합니다.

body:
**This builds on #21 (SKUs and Inventory Guardian), so its base is #21's branch.** Merge #21 first, then retarget this PR to `main`. Etsy and Vinted were already platforms on `main`, so this PR adds only the two new ones and a guide to every platform.

## What's new
- **Two new platforms: `Facebook` (Marketplace) and `ThredUp`.** They work everywhere the platform list is used: order filters, Add order, Import CSV, inventory listing columns, auto-delist toggles, pricing rules, Inventory Guardian checks and analytics.
- **ThredUp is limited to Direct Listing.** ThredUp opened peer-to-peer Direct Listing in June 2026 (open beta, 0% seller fees, ThredUp handles returns). Clean Out bag consignment items aren't the seller's sales, so the app says they don't belong here.
- **Fee estimates.** Facebook charges 10% of shipped sales, with a $0.80 minimum. ThredUp Direct Listing charges sellers nothing.
- **Listing links.** IDs are parsed from `facebook.com/marketplace/item/<id>` and `thredup.com/product/<slug>/<id>`, so the new platforms work with #21's listing links and checks.
- **Settings > Connections** now lists each marketplace with how orders, labels and listings work on it (`src/lib/platforms.ts`). It only names routes the marketplace allows:
  - Facebook has no API for personal Marketplace sellers. Orders are added by hand or by CSV. The label is Facebook's prepaid one if the account has it, otherwise a SellSync label with the tracking number pasted into Facebook.
  - ThredUp has no seller API or export, so orders are added by hand.
  - Etsy has an official Open API for orders, tracking and listings. The app notes that connecting it needs an app key approved by Etsy, which is a later step.
  - Vinted has no public seller API. The app says SellSync doesn't scrape Vinted or work around its bot protection.
- **Demo data** includes a few Facebook and ThredUp sales.

## Notes
- No database change. Platform values are stored as text.
- The platform key is `Facebook` so filter chips and table columns stay short. The full name "Facebook Marketplace" shows in Settings.
- This uses the colors on #21's branch. If #19 (the rebrand) merges first, the two new platform colors in `ui.tsx` are the only lines that could conflict.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 90 pass, including new ones for Facebook and ThredUp fees and link parsing.
- `tsc` and `vite build` pass.
- Checked Settings > Connections, Inventory and Analytics in demo mode at 1280 px and 390 px. There's no horizontal scroll on the phone layout.

body:
the three never-exempt cites read the board again, and the catalogue gets the producer it lacked

The subject-axis promotion landed, so the board is 34 axes, 34 measured, 0
unmeasured. Three surfaces that are never allowed to hold a stale count were
still publishing "34 axes · 23 measured": interop/gspc-one.json,
publisher-health.json and owm/v0.1/latest.json. All three are rebound by the
estate's own producer, from this commit's own board — a number that depends on
which deployment happens to be live is not a property of the commit.

The master catalogue gets the producer it never had.

Until now its live_state was typed by hand, which is why it could carry 331
leaves while the root carried 428. scripts/surface/rebind-catalogue-live-state.mjs
is now the ONE producer of that block and of the matching rows in the page: it
reads the estate, derives every number, records the URL, the HTTP status and a
digest of the CONTENT that produced each count, and refuses to write if any row
no longer matches what it expects — a moved layout fails loudly instead of
half-writing. The board row is this commit's own board; the rest are live reads.

It publishes a new dated edition, never an edit of an older one. The 2026-11-02
edition that another lane published is untouched: its corrections table, its
repair record, its jewel rows and its owner gates all survive into the
2026-11-03 edition, and the new edition names the one it supersedes. The
producer also refuses to publish over an edition of the same date that it did
not write, so two lanes cannot silently overwrite each other on the same day.

The rules live in scripts/surface/catalogue-live-state-lib.mjs so they can be
tested without the network. Eleven tests, and five of them prove the rules can
still go red: a missing row, a doubled row, a stale board-count sentence, another
lane's edition of the same date, and an unmeasured list that is empty because
every slot is measured — which must render as an em-dash row, not as a broken
empty table.

The facts table's recorded observation and the facts-gate's own overclaim
fixture were carried into master by another lane while this was in flight, so
neither is changed here.

Measured: the commit board and the live board both read 34 axes · 34 measured ·
0 unmeasured; the live root carries 428 leaves as_of 2026-11-01T15:09:42Z; the
x402 catalogue carries 30 resources; the corrections ledger carries 93 entries.

Job: D of the years-to-days plan. The published surface must be true today, and a
number that moves must be followed everywhere it is published.

Catalog refresh repeatedly resolves the same provider and parses equal endpoint URLs for model rows, metadata overlays, and configured-model merges. Allocation profiling identified URL parsing as 11.438% of sampled allocation in the prior candidate.

## User Impact

Reduces repeated provider selection and route normalization during catalog refresh without adding a cache or config option. body: Enhance Job Application Submission and Management ([SCRUM-267](https://soen341.atlassian.net/browse/SCRUM-267)) Add multi-resume support: applicants can save multiple resumes and select one when applying, instead of only ever having one resume on file. Attach a snapshot of the selected resume to each application at submission time, so recruiters can view/download exactly what was submitted even if the applicant later edits or deletes that saved resume. Let applicants cancel a submitted application; cancelling removes it from the recruiter's applicant list and immediately frees the applicant to re-apply. Hide the "Apply Now" button once an application is on file (replaced with "Cancel Application") instead of leaving it visible with a static "already applied" message, and show it again after cancelling. Block duplicate active applications for the same job. Add a "Replace" action per resume so an applicant can swap a saved resume's file in place without losing its id/history. Show only the most recently uploaded resume by default on the profile page, with an inline preview (PDF iframe, or a view/download fallback for DOC/DOCX), and a "Show other resumes" toggle to reveal the rest. Let recruiters download the resume attached to each applicant via the dashboard. Changes ### Backend New Resume model/collection (one user can now have many saved resumes). Application model embeds a resume snapshot (originalName/contentType/size/data) at submission time. POST /api/applications now requires auth + a resumeId, validates resume ownership, and blocks duplicates. New endpoints: GET /api/applications/status/:jobId, DELETE /api/applications/:id, GET /api/applications/:id/resume. Resume routes rewritten for multi-resume CRUD: GET/POST /api/resumes, GET /api/resumes/:id/file, PUT /api/resumes/:id (replace), DELETE /api/resumes/:id. One-time data migration for existing users whose resume lived under the old embedded User.resume field, moved into the new Resume collection (verified byte-for-byte before clearing the legacy field). ### Frontend - JobDetail.jsx: resume picker + Apply Now when not applied, Cancel Application when applied, prompt to upload a resume when none exist. - ResumeManager.jsx: shows the most recent resume with an inline preview, Replace/View/Download/Delete actions, and a collapsible list of older resumes. - RecruiterDashboard.jsx: added a Download Resume button per applicant. - New applicationApi.js client module for status/submit/cancel/resume-download calls. ### Testing Added/updated unit tests for resumeQueries, applicationqueries, resumeApi, applicationApi, ResumeManager, JobDetail, and RecruiterDashboard. Added integration tests (resume.integration.test.js, application.integration.test.js) covering auth requirements, ownership checks, duplicate-application prevention, cancellation removing the application from the recruiter's list, and resume download authorization (applicant + owning recruiter only). All unit, integration, and lint checks pass on both client and server. Manually verified the full flow in the browser and via the API (apply → recruiter views/downloads resume → cancel → re-apply; resume replace). ### Images - Recruiters are able to download resumes - Users are able to upload multiple resumes - Users are able to select which resume they want to submit in order to apply and they are able to cancel their application

author: draquel
body:
Decision D-VP2 (FINDINGS.md): keep the textures, add slope-aware rock in the shader (VP2-O3). Soft material borders (VP2-O4) are not in this PR; they wait for the user's look at this.

## What changed

- **Per-material data.** `FVoxelMaterialTextureConfig::SlopeMaterialID` (-1 = never): the material this one turns into on steep smooth terrain. `BuildMaterialLUT` writes it into the slice row's unused A as ID + 1 (`GetSlopeMaterialID`: none for -1, the material's own ID, or an unconfigured ID). Rendering only: voxels, digging, the map and scatter keep the real material.
- **Shader.** `Shaders/Private/VoxelSlopeRock.ush`: weight = smoothstep(0.08, 0.19) of 1 - N.Up (about 23-36°) on the interpolated vertex normal, with the slope moved ±0.04 by a value noise about 3 tiles across. The vertex normal is continuous, so there are no per-quad edges. Both triplanar nodes compute the same weight. Where it is between 0 and 1 they read both materials' slices (shared variation offsets) and blend albedo, roughness and the UDN normal detail. At 0 or 1 they read one material, as before.
- **Local up.** World +Z, or radial from the planet's centre: a `LocalUpCenter` vector parameter inside each function (xyz centre, w radial; default 0). The LWC subtraction from the absolute world position happens in the graph, before the Custom node demotes to float. `UVoxelRegionComponent` sets it in `UpdateMaterialAtlasParameters` and in `SetRadialFaceUp`, and the crossfade MIDs copy it like every vector parameter. **Why a MID parameter, not an MPC:** MPC values are per `UWorld`, so two voxel worlds in a level would share one, and the region component already sets the per-world parameters on its own instance.
- **Tests.** `VoxelWorlds.MaterialAtlas.SlopeMaterial` (LUT A), `VoxelWorlds.Rendering.SlopeRock.Assets` (wiring) and `.LocalUpParameter` (the MID value on a heightmap world and a planet, before and after the instance exists). `SliceRowMatches` now expects A = slope + 1.
- **Docs.** `MATERIAL_SYSTEM.md` "Slope-Aware Rock (visual polish VP2-O3)" with the result; the config listing, the node inputs, the slice row and the binding are updated.

## What this touched in `M_VoxelMaster` (for the D-VP3 session)

**No node in `M_VoxelMaster` or `M_VoxelMaster_Fade` changed.** Both were recompiled and resaved so their cached parameter list includes `LocalUpCenter` (a cooked game reads the saved list). All graph edits are inside `MF_TriplanarSampleAlbedoRoughness` and `MF_TriplanarSampleNormal`:
- the Custom node's code;
- includes `VoxelTextureVariation.ush` + `VoxelSlopeRock.ush`;
- two new node inputs, `FromCenter` and `RadialUp`;
- new nodes: VectorParameter `LocalUpCenter`, WorldPosition and Subtract.

The material edits are scripted in the parent's `Scripts/setup_slope_rock.py` (headless, idempotent).

## Gates (all on this worktree, D: engine)

- Build: 0 warnings (baseline `build_warnings_2026-11-02.txt`: Claudius CS0618 only); no new.
- Headless suite: main 764/764, change 767/767 (+3 new tests). Warning kinds: only the clock-seeded `SelectEntranceRoom` count (19 → 20), known noise.
- Mesh digests: 209 vs 209, identical.
- `editor_gate.py`: 22/22 Success (the 18 plus the 3 new tests and `TextureVariation.Assets`). GPU parity: 111 lines, identical to the record.
- Explored maps (VoxelDemo, PlanetTest): byte-identical to main's (g100's main captures). The map reads voxel materials.
- Shader compile: no errors on SM6. SM5/FXC (`-d3d11` editor): compiles and draws. The slowest material job was 5.4 s, a base-pass PS; no material job was pathological. (A 31.8 s `FGenerateVoxelDensityCS` is generation, untouched here.)
- `check_docs.py`: 0 broken links or paths; no new unknown names.

## The look

Screenshots are in the worktree's `Saved/QA/vp2o3/`: `voxeldemo_main_vs_change.png` (main build vs change, same 5 poses) and `planets_ab.png` (in-session A/B, atlases' slope materials off/on).
- **VoxelDemo:** rock patches on the steepest hill flanks with irregular borders; the gentle ground is unchanged.
- **PlanetTest** (equator, lat 70, pole) and **Review_Planet_M** (lat 70): little turns. These planets are gentle; the mean pixel change is 0.3-1.5/255, mostly foliage wind. Flat equator ground did not turn to rock, which shows the radial up is in use.
- **Thresholds:** set by eye. 37° turned almost nothing on these worlds.

New finding **G106**: ground scatter still grows on the rock, because scatter places by the voxel material.

Merge order: this PR first, then the parent PR (it moves the gitlink to this PR's merge commit).

- [ ] Existing implementation and related open PRs were checked; this PR does not duplicate:
- [ ] This PR changes a current reachable app/backend/package/docs surface, or it is explicitly scoped as test/devex hygiene.
- [ ] Reachable production attach point:

- [ ] Production surface proved:

- [ ] Maintainer edits are enabled, or the reason they cannot be enabled is listed here:
- [ ] If this is one PR in a stack, the predecessor PR is linked here:
- [ ] If this responds to requested changes, the new commit or material explanation is described here:

## 🛑 Tri-Flow Architecture Check

the layer as not applicable with the reason.

- [ ] **Web**: Next.js implementation (`app/api/...`)

Playwright spec/command, screenshot, video, or why browser proof is not
applicable.

## 📌 Summary / What
Promotes integrated development changes from `dev` into `staging`, encompassing core spatial intelligence pipelines, Apple Foundation Models on-device diagnostics, and Apple HIG ergonomics across ADRs 0032 through 0043:
- Aperture-aware ceiling outlines, interior partition pruning, universal floor grounding, and multi-wall capture quality gates.
- Panero & Zelnik anthropometric clearance engine, constraint-driven parametric layout optimizer, and dynamic ModelIO USDZ room parser.
- Apple Foundation Models spatial diagnostics, tool calling, and grounded layout insight engine.
- Adaptive iPad/iPhone lighting workspaces and 2D floor plan coordinate alignment.

## 🎯 Why / Motivation
Consolidates Phase 2 and Phase 3 feature branches into the `staging` pre-release environment for comprehensive integration testing, ensuring all spatial math, SwiftData models, and on-device AI pipelines are validated prior to production release promotion.

## 🛠️ How / Technical Changes
- **Spatial Architecture & Geometry**:
  - **Aperture-Aware Ceiling Outlines & Interior Partitions** (ADR 0034, ADR 0035): Traces perimeter cycle while pruning open interior branches and preserving partition walls for clearance.
  - **Universal Floor Grounding & Deterministic Legacy Migration** (ADR 0043): Enforces universal floor contact ($Y = 0.0$), restricts elevation to small wall shelves, and gates legacy transformation on $positionY < -0.2$.
  - **Scanned Room Plan Layout Alignment** (ADR 0029 update): Passes normalized room coordinates and yaw directly to 2D projection, eliminating double-transformation.
  - **Capture Quality Gate**: Rejects single-wall slice scans ($\\ge 2$ walls and $\\ge 1.0\\text{m}$ clear span required).
- **Anthropometrics & Parametric Layout Optimization**:
  - **Anthropometric Clearance Engine** (ADR 0037): Codifies Panero & Zelnik clearance standards, edge-to-edge spatial intervals, and doorway swing envelopes.
  - **Parametric Spatial Solver** (ADR 0041): Dynamic constraint-driven optimizer adapting to room geometry, windows, and circulation paths.
- **On-Device AI Diagnostics & Spatial Tools**:
  - **Apple Foundation Models Integration** (ADR 0039, ADR 0042): Diagnostic assessment with schema-validated tool-calling and deterministic headless rulebook fallbacks.
  - **Room Preferences & Grounded Insights** (ADR 0040): Interactive lifestyle preference survey, grounded insight cards, and 3D layout suggestion flow.
- **Lighting Simulation & Ergonomics**:
  - **Adaptive Workspaces** (ADR 0032, ADR 0033): Decomposed responsive workspaces for iPad and iPhone, neutral layout previews, and gesture-conflict-free tablet canvases.
  - **Compass Consolidation** (ADR 0036): Decommissioned standalone post-scan compass in favor of unified navigation.
- **SwiftData / Persistence Impact**:
  - [x] **No Schema Changes** (Safe to merge without teammate impact)
- **Edge Cases & Error Handling**:
  - Polygons with acute wall angles, headless test environments without foundation models, legacy unmigrated LiDAR scans.

> [!NOTE]
> Validated with real-world scan fixtures `Room.usdz` and `Room-2.usdz`.

author: francescok
body:
Follows up #10742 and its CodeRabbit thread (https://github.com/matz/spinel/pull/10742#discussion_r4438558338), which leaves the program's own iterator methods to follow-up PRs.

Probed at master `e380e3178`, macOS, Apple clang 21.

#10742 reads the block of a builtin iterator's name on a literal of a builtin class the program does not reopen as running at once, for certain, so a class's `respond_to?` asked in it folds to the answer before a later def. A public top-level def is an Object method, and a literal's `tap`, `then` or `yield_self` reaches it when the program defines one, so that method's body decides when the block runs. When it keeps the block and runs it after the def, CRuby answers `true` where Spinel folded to `false`.

```ruby
class S; end
public def tap(&b)
  $b = b
  self
end
1.tap { p S.respond_to?(:z) }
def S.z = 1
$b&.call
```

| | CRuby 4.0 | Spinel (master) | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| the program above | `true` | `false` | as CRuby |
| the same with `def then(&b)` and `public :then`, on `"x".then` | `true` | `false` | as CRuby |
| `public def tap(&b) = (at_exit { b&.call }; self)`, on `[1].tap` | `true` | `false` | as CRuby |
| `public def tap(...) = (keep(...); self)`, `keep(&b)` stores it | `true` | `false` | as CRuby |
| `public def tap(&b) = (keep(&b); self)`, or `(&)` handed on as `keep(&)` | `true` | `false` | as CRuby |
| `public def tap` that stores `proc { yield self }`, a lambda calling `b`, or a `hold { yield self }` block that keeps it | `true` | `false` | as CRuby |
| `[1].each { 2.tap { ... } }` with a keeping `tap` | `true` | `false` | as CRuby |
| a bare `public` word before the keeping def; `alias tap keep_it` with `public :tap` | `true` | `false` | as CRuby |
| a yielding `public def tap` replaced by a keeping one before a second call | `false`, `true` | `false`, `false` | as CRuby |
| a module's yielding `tap` included at the top level, then main's keeping `public def tap` | `true` | `false` | as CRuby |
| a keeping `public def tap` in a `require_relative`d file; a public alias `tap` of a keeping def whose original is then redefined to yield | `true` | `false` | as CRuby |
| a `public def tap` that yields in `Fiber.new`, `Enumerator.new`, a lazy `map` or a `Thread.new` block | `true` | `false` | as CRuby |
| `public def tap(&b) = ($b = b)`, then `$b.call` (`then`, `yield_self` alike) | `true` | `false`, NoMethodError | `true`, NoMethodError (below) |
| `public def tap = (yield self; self)`, `public def tap(&b) = (b.call(self); self)`, a conditional yield, a yield in `[1].each`, an alias of a yielding def, `then` / `yield_self` that yield; `b.call(self) if b`, `return self unless b`, `b.to_proc.call(self)`, `b.curry[self]`; `instance_exec(self, &b)`, `super(&b)`, a helper that yields given `&b` | `false` | `false` | `false` |

- `elab_block_when` (analyze_elab.c) answers `ELAB_BLK_NOW` for an iterator name on a literal when no header of the program reopens a builtin class. That is right for the builtin's iterator, but the record did not ask which method the call reaches: a top-level `public def tap` is Object's public `tap`, and Integer, String and Symbol answer `tap`, `then` and `yield_self` through Object.
- `cplan_cmethod_later` folds `S.respond_to?(:z)` to `false` when every block around it runs at once for certain (`elab_blocks_run_now`), so the block that the program's method keeps for later got the answer of before the def.

Found by CodeRabbit on #10742 (the literal-receiver reading), reproduced through a top-level public def.

**The record reads the program method a literal's call binds to for when it runs the block (load record layer: analyze_elab.c).** `elab_block_runs`, the block-timing answer `elab_blocks_run_now` and so `cplan_cmethod_later` read, now asks, for a call on a literal whose builtin class does not answer the name itself, which method of the program's the record binds it to (`lr_target_runs_block`): main's live version of the name at the call (`elab_method_at`), through an alias to its original's version where the alias was made, when the called name is public there. A private or protected one is not called on a literal (CRuby raises), so the builtin's reading stays, and so does it for a version the record cannot place at the call (a def in a loop's block). `lr_def_block` then reads that def's own nodes (`nt_subtree_ids`, those whose body is the def's) and sorts each use of the block: a yield, a read of the block parameter, of a local it is copied to whole (which covers the desugared `&b` rename) or of a closure holding it (`l = lambda { yield self }`), and a hand-on through `&b`, `&`, `...` or a `super` without a block. A use keeps the block only on positive evidence: stored to an instance, global or class variable, a constant or an element, passed as an argument, returned or left as the body's value, captured in a closure that escapes in one of those ways, in an `at_exit` body or in the block of a call that runs it later, or handed on to a call that keeps it. A value is placed by the value edges (`vp_climb`), and a closure (a lambda, or a Proc made by `proc`, `lambda` or `Proc.new`, of a literal block or of the block parameter itself: `proc(&b)`, `Proc.new(&b)`) is placed as its own value: called there, or dropped, it keeps nothing. A use runs the block at once when it yields or calls it (`call`, `()`, `[]`, `yield`, through `to_proc` or `curry`) through blocks that run at once, or hands it on to a call that runs it at once (`lr_hand_on`: a builtin iterator on a literal; a method of the program's that does not keep it, read in turn when the program defines it once and no builtin class answers the name, since the body runs on the literal and is read for every call that reaches it, and a literal's call inside a method body reads its callee under the same rule, and only for a name Object has no method of (`lr_target_runs_block`): the call has no place in the load to say which version is live, and until main's one def of an Object method's name the call reaches Object's, which runs the block at once; a `super` to Object's builtin of an iterator's name, the builtin_ops.c fact `object_iter_runs_now`, which a module included at the top level would precede, a shape refused on both builds). A truth test (`if b`, `unless b.nil?`, `b &&`) and a dropped statement are neither. A body that keeps the block and never runs it, or may run it, before it answers reads `ELAB_BLK_ASSUMED`, which the fold does not trust, so `respond_to?` keeps its answer as of the whole program; a body that runs it at once, or that the reading cannot place, keeps the call's reading by name, as on master, where a run at once is answered right. The keep evidence and the reading of the call a block is handed on to are one rule: a hand-on is a keep exactly when the receiving call keeps the block, so reading a body without its callees would answer for `keep(&b)`, `keep(...)` and a `hold { yield }` block by name, which is the false answer this PR fixes. The reading is memoized per def in the load record; a def asked while its own reading is in progress (a recursive hand-on) answers that it cannot place the use, and a def read inside such a cycle keeps that answer, which keeps the call's reading by name. Every other call keeps its reading, `lr_literal_kind` now asks the new `lr_literal_class` map, and no name test, no `comp_ntype` read and no global is added.

**Cost.** The reading walks only the def's own nodes, once per def. Master and this PR interleaved, best of 5, `-c`: for N literal calls `i.tap { p S.respond_to?(:z) if x < 0 }`, each in an `[i].each` block, with a yielding top-level `public def tap`, N = 1,000 / 2,000 / 4,000 / 8,000 retires 4.348 / 8.682 / 17.473 / 35.050 G instructions on master and 4.366 / 8.733 / 17.551 / 35.206 G with this PR (+0.4 / +0.6 / +0.4 / +0.4%; `--timing`'s `cg_main` phase, on a loaded machine: 32 / 68 / 205 / 255 ms against 35 / 66 / 188 / 290 ms). author: itluckswan-coder
body:
## Problem
The banquet card on the BEO page lists items, but the function sheet's **รูปแบบการจัดห้อง** box showed only the FYI part. The sheet holds a typed copy of that box, so it stopped following the card.

A typed copy appears in two ways:
- Someone typed or cleared the box earlier.
- The sheet editor (`ui.draft`) was left open while someone edited the card on the BEO page. Saving the sheet afterwards compared that old copy with the new system value, found them different, and stored the old text as a typed copy.

## Fix
- **The card edit wins:** saving a department card (`beoDept`) drops the matching typed box (and its rich copy) when the items changed. The mapping is banquet → `layout`, kitchen → `kitchen`, hk → `hk`, av → `av`, front → `front`.
- **No stale editor copy:** an untouched draft is rebuilt on every render. Only a draft with unsaved edits is kept.
- **Only changed boxes are stored:** the draft remembers what each box showed when editing began (`d.base`). `fnDSave` skips boxes that are still the same, so untouched boxes keep following the system.
- Service-worker cache bumped to v123.

For a sheet that already has the problem, open the department card, press **แก้ไข → บันทึก**, and the sheet shows the card again. The ↺ button in the sheet editor also still works.

## Test
Playwright:
1. **Old typed copy:** with `fn.layout = ''`, the box showed only FYI. After editing the banquet card, the box shows the card's lines.
2. **Editor left open while the card changed:** the editor shows the new card line. After saving the sheet, the box shows all the card lines and no `layout` copy is stored.
3. **Real typed text is kept:** typing in ข้อความบนเวที and saving keeps it.
4. No JS errors.

body:
Number keys and key shortcuts are now one thing, and holding a number works in every app.

**Changed**
- Holding a number is a shortcut like any other. The Number keys list on Gestures and keys shows what each number does when held, and tapping one opens the normal shortcut editor. "Add shortcut" accepts number keys, which are always held.
- Holding a number with no shortcut on the home screen opens the shortcut editor with that number filled in, with every action available. The old "Choose an app" search screen is gone.
- Holding a number runs its shortcut in other apps even while typing, so the phone's speed dial no longer takes over in Messages. A quick press of that number is typed into the text box when the key is let go.
- On the lock screen, number keys only type the PIN. Other keys' shortcuts work there. Ones that open something (an app, a call, Smart Search) ask to unlock first, then run.
- The Settings page shows how many shortcuts are set, not just number keys.

author: samestrin
body:
Epic 02 T3 (EST-4310). Each page is now routed to a method.

- `POST /v1/extract` takes two new fields, `method` (`auto` by default, or `text_layer`, `tesseract`, `vision`) and `model`.
- `auto`: the text layer when it is usable, else the vision model if one is configured, else Tesseract. With no vision config the pages are read exactly as in epic 01.
- Each page states its `model` (JSON `"model"`, Markdown `· Model: …`). It is set only for `vision` pages, and it is the model name the endpoint reports.
- A `model` outside the operator's list returns **400 `model_not_allowed`**. With no backend configured, every model is refused. `method=vision` with no backend returns **400 `vision_not_configured`**. Both checks run before any page is read.
- Vision pages are rendered on the request thread and read in parallel, at most `OCR_LLM_CONCURRENCY` at once. A page that fails is `failed` / `vision_failed` with the sanitized message, and the other pages are still returned. T4 adds the error codes and the Tesseract fallback.
- `/ocr` routes as `auto` and still ignores the 0.0.1 `model` field.
- The config is read once (`get_vision_config`) and checked at startup, so a bad `OCR_LLM_*` value stops the service.

Contract changes in existing tests, made on purpose:
- `test_extract.py` JSON schema: adds the `model` key, the `vision` method, and the `no_text_layer` / `vision_failed` codes.
- `test_api.py::test_a_model_field_downloads_and_loads_nothing`: `/v1/extract` now answers 400 to a model that is not on the list. It still opens no network connection and loads no model library.
- New `tests/conftest.py` overrides the vision config to "off" for every test, so a developer's own `OCR_LLM_*` environment cannot change test results.

Verified: `ruff check`, `ruff format`. `pytest` gives 208 passed, 3 skipped, 99.8% coverage, and `extract.py` is at 100%. The full suite also passes with `OCR_LLM_BASE_URL`/`OCR_LLM_DEFAULT_MODEL` set in the shell. `tests/test_routing.py::test_routing_table` is the routing table. `test_api_refuses_a_model_outside_the_list` covers the disallowed-model 4xx, end to end against the fake OpenAI-compatible server.

author: leonxlnx
body:
## What the user saw

A background picture always came with the same fixed dim and blur. There was no way to change either, and no way to see in Settings how the picture would look behind the window.

## Cause

The dim was a constant scrim in `app-background.css` (black 40% in dark, white 45% in light) and the blur a constant in `app-background-image.ts` (`DISPLAY_IMAGE_BLUR = 14`, baked into the stored display copy). Settings only had Choose / Change / Remove.

## What changed

- **Two new levels**, stored like the other window-background keys: `harness.appBackground.dim` (0-100) and `harness.appBackground.blur` (0-40, in pixels of the 1600px display copy). Garbage or out-of-range values fall back to the defaults.
- **Defaults reproduce today's look exactly.** Dim 50 is the old scrim strength in both themes (the scrim is now a colour plus `opacity: strength * --app-bg-dim`, with the factor 1 at 50, 0 at 0 and 2 at 100). Blur 14 keeps the version string `blur14@1600`, so the display copies already stored are reused and nothing is rebuilt until the slider moves.
- **The window follows live.** Dim is a CSS factor on the layer and applies on every step. A new blur rebuilds the display copy from the stored original, but only once the value has rested for 220 ms, so a drag rebuilds once and not on each step; the old picture stays up until the new one is ready (no fade-out gap). The window still paints a plain pre-blurred bitmap, never a live CSS filter.
- **Settings > Appearance > Window background**, once a picture is chosen, adds:
  - *Preview*: a 176x110 thumbnail of the picture as the window will show it. It blurs the stored original with a CSS filter scaled from the display copy to its width and lays the same dim over it, so it updates on the same frame as the slider. The filter only ever covers this thumbnail.
  - *Dim* and *Blur*: native range inputs that write on every step.
- A newly picked picture is prepared at the current Blur.

## Review fix: a late blur rebuild could restore a replaced picture

`backgroundDisplayImage` saved the rebuilt display copy with a plain `store.save` of the record it had loaded. The layer's `cancelled` flag only skipped showing the result, so if a new picture was chosen (or the picture removed) while a rebuild was still encoding, the late save wrote the old picture back into IndexedDB, and the new revision then showed the old picture.

- Each prepared picture now carries an `id` (`StoredBackgroundImage.id`).
- The rebuild writes through a new `BackgroundImageStore.saveDisplay`, which reads the record and puts the rebuilt copy in **one readwrite IndexedDB transaction**, only while the stored id still matches; it resolves whether it wrote. A plain "is the layer still current" check before `save` would not be enough: Settings saves the new picture before it bumps the revision, so the layer cannot yet know it was replaced.
- Pictures stored before the id existed have none and still match only themselves, so they are rebuilt and saved as before.
- New `apps/web/src/app-background-image.test.ts` (canvas and `createImageBitmap` stubbed, encodes held until the test releases them): a picture chosen during a rebuild stays, a picture removed during a rebuild stays removed, an unchanged picture keeps its rebuilt copy, a legacy record without an id is still rebuilt, an up-to-date copy is not rebuilt, and two prepared pictures get different ids. Against the pre-fix `app-background-image.ts` (21ef611f) it fails 3 of 6 (the chosen and removed cases, and the id); with the fix it passes 6 of 6.
- Not covered by a test: the IndexedDB `saveDisplay` transaction itself (happy-dom has no IndexedDB and the repo has no fake-indexeddb); the tests use an in-memory store with the same contract.

## Local checks

Windows, each command through the machine's low-priority wrapper, one test file at a time (`apps/web`):

After the review fix, at 2d33eac1:

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/app-background-image.test.ts --maxWorkers=2`: 6 passed (3 of 6 failed against the pre-fix source)
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/ui/AppBackground.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2`: 10 passed
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/ui/AppBackgroundSettings.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2`: 6 passed
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p apps/web`: exit 0, no output
- `oxlint` (0 warnings, 0 errors) and `prettier --check` on the four touched files: clean
- `@harness/contracts` dist built here with `pnpm --filter @harness/contracts build` for the typecheck.

Before the review fix, at 24107743:

- `npx vitest run src/app-background.test.ts --maxWorkers=2`: 15 passed
- `npx vitest run src/ui/AppBackground.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2`: 10 passed
- `npx vitest run src/ui/AppBackgroundSettings.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2`: 6 passed
- `npx vitest run src/styles/app-background-css.test.ts --maxWorkers=2`: 5 passed
- `tsc --noEmit -p apps/web`: exit 0, no output
- `oxlint` and `prettier --check` on the touched files: clean

The workspace packages' `dist` (needed by the typecheck) came from a build of the same base commit `e0902263`; nothing was built here. The full `pnpm lint`/`typecheck`/`test`/`build` gates and `App.test.tsx` were not run (one heavy job at a time on this machine).

## Screenshots

Browser renderer (release-edition server, fake home), 1280x800, Settings > Appearance > Window background with a test picture. The sliders were moved by input events, as a drag sends them.

Default levels (dark), which match the old look:
![settings with the default dim and blur, dark](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/tastecode/blob/21ef611f/docs/evidence/window-bg-settings-image-dark-20261103.png?raw=true)

Dim 80, Blur 30 (light):
![settings with dim 80 and blur 30, light](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/tastecode/blob/21ef611f/docs/evidence/window-bg-settings-image-dim80-blur30-light-20261103.png?raw=true)

Dim 10, Blur 2 (dark), and the window after it:
![settings with dim 10 and blur 2, dark](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/tastecode/blob/21ef611f/docs/evidence/window-bg-settings-image-dim10-blur2-dark-20261103.png?raw=true)
![window with dim 10 and blur 2, dark](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/tastecode/blob/21ef611f/docs/evidence/window-bg-image-dim10-blur2-dark-20261103.png?raw=true)

## Assumptions (Leon was not available)

- Dim 0-100 with 50 = today's dim, Blur 0-40 with 14 = today's blur; no numeric readout next to the sliders.
- Sliders and preview appear only once a picture is chosen.
- See the screenshots for the look; every visual choice is listed under "Taste calls" below.

## Taste calls (all reversible, please pick)

- Slider look: the native range input with `accent-color: var(--light)` (the token the on-switch uses), 176px wide.
- Preview: picture only (no mock sidebar or chat), 176x110, 1px `--line` border, `--r-md` radius, in its own "Preview" row under Image; then Dim, then Blur.

## Not checked

- Not run inside Electron (agent rules); checked in a browser renderer against a release-edition server with a fake home.
- Rebuild time of the display copy for very large pictures on a slow machine was not measured; it runs once per pause of the slider, as the existing rebuild-on-version-change path already did.

body:
Lets you set both ends of the dashboard's time window, not just its end. This is a dashboard-only change: `/api/query`, `/api/log` and `/api/events/summary` already take any start and end.

### Custom range
- **Range → custom…** shows **from** and **to** fields (date and time, to the second). It starts from the window currently on screen. A start after the end is refused with a message.
- ◀ ▶ step both ends by one window length, and the scrubber slides the window keeping its length. A custom window can go back as far as the store keeps data (`--db`, 7 days by default), not just the scrubber's last 24 h.
- **back to live** returns to the range the custom window replaced.

### Drag to zoom
- Drag across any time-series chart (mouse or touch) to set the board's window to that stretch. The cursor becomes a crosshair, and hovering a chart says "drag to zoom in · double-click to zoom out".
- Double-click steps back through earlier windows, then to live.
- The click that ends a drag doesn't also click through to an entity or the log.
- Zoom is off in edit mode, where dragging moves widgets.

### Links
- The address carries the board (or template), window and variables, for example `#dash?board=Ops&span=custom&from=1793000000&to=1793001800&v.site=7`. It updates as you change the view.
- **copy link** copies it. On plain HTTP to a LAN address, where browsers don't allow the clipboard API, it shows the link in a box to copy instead.
- Opening a link goes straight to that board, window and variables. Leaving the Dashboards tab clears the address.

### Testing
There's no browser on this machine, so I drove the real page in jsdom (scratchpad only, not in the repo) with stubbed API answers. All 19 checks pass:
- a link opens the right board, window and variables, and the widgets query exactly that window;
- dragging the middle half of a chart zooms to the middle half, and double-click goes back;
- typed times apply, and a start after the end is refused;
- ◀ moves both ends, including for a week-old window;
- copy link offers the full link; back to live restores the earlier range; leaving the tab clears the address.

author: chaliy
body:
## What changed

Add an optional standalone DataFusion companion that copies retained live/archived events into immutable object-backed segments, resumes finite backfills, tails new events, and compares bounded queries and sampled payloads against PostgreSQL. Explicit all-org mode uses a durable bounded tenant cursor, discovers new organizations and keeps global backlog/failure gauges. It is disabled by default and the normal server/Framework do not link DataFusion or acquire an S3 dependency. All product reads and canonical writes remain on PostgreSQL.

Architecture: `knowledge/operations/trace-storage.md`; exact configuration and commands: `crates/trace-store/README.md`.

Changelog: not user-facing (operator qualification; no product read-path change).

## Why

Qualify an open-format object-backed event store with measurable correctness, latency, resource use and cost before proposing historical retention or application read cutover. Keep object-store availability independent from event emission and self-hosted installations.

## Before / After

Before: no object-backed trace engine or resumable qualification workflow.

After:

- Disabled `run`, with no DB/S3 configuration, returns `{"enabled":false}` before creating connections, directories or listeners.
- 31 focused tests pass: unit/CLI checks plus 23 real PostgreSQL/S3 integration tests covering publication/retry/concurrency, tenant isolation, finite archived/live backfill, append catch-up, gaps/conflicts, rotating comparison windows, checksum corruption, deletion/GC and failure isolation.
- A separate end-to-end smoke applied all 79 platform migrations, archived two of five events, completed a finite backfill, classified an append as `lagging`, then caught up two new events with summary and full-envelope `match`. Metrics/readiness/probe passed; payload marker absent from logs. GC removed six analytical objects and retained all seven canonical events. This used a local SeaweedFS S3 protocol service; it is not cloud/performance evidence.
- `migrate-catalog` uses its own checksum ledger and leaves `_sqlx_migrations` unchanged, preserving restart compatibility for an older running server. Future platform adoption uses the same idempotent DDL.
- A second S3 smoke used the 76 migrations from an earlier public platform revision plus independent catalog migration, then exercised all-org startup, backfill, catch-up and global status. All canonical events remained intact.
- The cloud implementation uses patched object_store 0.14 through a manifest-scoped read-only bridge to DataFusion’s 0.13 API; the vulnerable older cloud/XML dependency is absent.
- Full `just pre-push`, focused all-feature Clippy, OKF and migration-order checks passed. Normal server dependency tree excludes DataFusion.

## Risk

Medium. This is a privileged operator process that reads sensitive canonical history and writes a second copy. It adds optional catalog DDL, dependencies and source DB load. Bounded batches, query memory/time/file budgets, explicit org scope, immutable publication and a separate process limit exposure. Object request latency can exceed indexed PostgreSQL latency. This phase increases storage; it does not claim PostgreSQL capacity savings.

## Security

Reviewed TM-TENANT, TM-SQL, TM-FS and TM-DOS: bound typed predicates; live org-scoped source checks; tombstones; scoped manifest/payload keys; checksum-verified envelopes; create-only uploads before transactional publication; cancellation-safe SQLx transactions; coordinated compaction/GC; admission byte limits before source transfer; fixed low-cardinality metrics without payloads/raw errors. Database access is a narrow unpublished-companion exception; worker/runtime boundaries remain enforced. Disabled mode has no storage side effects. Versioned-bucket noncurrent objects/backups require separate erasure policy. No public query API is exposed.

## Follow-ups

No implementation follow-ups for this qualification component. Production placement and observation belong to the private SaaS rollout. Product read cutover, canonical retention and full-text/distributed queries are outside this phase.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated
- [x] Backward compatibility considered
- [x] Security review performed against relevant threat model categories
- [x] Final CI ran checks affected by this PR
- [x] All review comments addressed (code change or written reasoning)

body:
## T-3322 — the rest of the 18th-20th block's grounds: 1900 Prairie's front walk

**What.** An audit of every worked 1904 house on Prairie between 18th and 20th Streets found one gap. Every house has its boundary, yard and front walk except **1900 Prairie** (Elbridge G. Keith's). T-3207 put it onto K01 after T-3206 had given its neighbours their yards, so it stood with an opening in its coping wall and nothing behind it. `tools/check_house_walks.py` was carrying it as its last PENDING house.

This PR gives it a K14 yard. The flagged front walk runs from the stoop's foot through the wall's opening (s 4.4-7.0 m) to the public walk, 2.5 m wide, as the one period photograph shows (the museum's '1900 PA': a light paved walk square between the two posts to the stoop). The lawn is the app's own ground, as at 1801 and 1901. The ground rises 44-54 mm toward the street under the yard, so the yard is lifted onto it (`yard.grade_m`, measured in the published app). Without the lift the 60 mm flags would be half-buried.

- `tools/check_house_walks.py`: PENDING is now empty, so all 54 worked 1904 houses can be walked into.
- Liberty `L-k14-walk-1900-keith-3322` (width, flags and wear are the kit's; the print's hedges are not built).
- `walk_joins_1904.json` re-laid: 1900's walk gets a 0.30 m join to the public walk.
- Rights census: `form.yard` is banked. It cites the photograph, whose rights are unresolved, but it is not sole-support because the 1911 Sanborn sheet stands beside it. This follows T-3206's precedent for the same yards.
- The photo match was re-rendered and its verdict set back to `differs`, with the walk item marked fixed. Its other open items are unchanged and belong to the house's own lane.
- `tools/qa_house_walks_t3322.mjs` and stills in `docs/RESEARCH/house-boundaries-T-3322/`.

**Verification**
- `check.sh` parts 1-4 green on the gated tree. The first pass had three reds, all derived files: walk joins, source-use backlinks and the rights bank. All three were regenerated.
- The branch was rebuilt on current dev with every derived file regenerated. The GLB is byte-identical (sha b8cedd3f…).

Desktop 1 hit the 600 s ceiling after 62 passes with zero page errors, the same kill dev's own record shows for that part on this runner. author: sanika-cs
body:
## Task

<!-- "Refs", not "Closes": after merging, the API user and its keys still need to be created (docs/business-health-check.md). -->
Refs TASK-2026-01177

## What and why

### In simple words

1. **A business owner finishes the Business Health Check on our website.** A new record appears here in Helpdesk, under **Business Health Check**, with their business name, contact name, phone, email and a **link to their report**.
2. **They press "Call me back" on the website.** The **same record** gets their phone and email. No duplicates.
3. **Our team opens the record and clicks Open Report.** This shows the client's full report: health score, the real gap, what to do next, and which of our services (ERP, digital marketing, AI) would help. The team can present it to the client in a meeting.
4. **Sales clicks Create Lead.** A lead is made in ERPNext (Leads) with the client's name, business, phone and email, and the report link is added to the lead as a note. The record then shows **Open Lead**. If a lead with the same phone or email already exists, it asks first.
5. **The website gets its own restricted login.** It can **only add and update these records**. It can't see tickets, customers or anything else in Helpdesk.
6. **Nothing arrives until we switch it on.** That means creating the website's API user and key, and giving the key to the website team.

### Technical details


The TBO website's **Business Health Check** ([tbocloud/Business-Diagnostic](https://github.com/tbocloud/Business-Diagnostic)) is a guided check-up for business owners. Each finished check-up needs to reach the CRM so a BDE can follow up. This PR adds a small DocType the website writes to over the REST API: **basic client info plus a link to the client's report**. Nothing else in the app changes.

- **`Business Health Check`** DocType (module Helpdesk), named `BHC-#####`:

  | Field | Type |
  |---|---|
  | `business_name` | Data (title) |
  | `contact_name` | Data |
  | `phone` | Data, Phone |
  | `email` | Data, Email |
  | `report_link` | Data, URL, **mandatory** |
  | `lead` | Data, read-only: the ERPNext Lead made with Create Lead |

  Text is trimmed on save, and a blank business name becomes "Unnamed business".
- **Open Report** button on the form (http/https links only).
- **Create Lead** button: a whitelisted `create_lead` method on the controller calls the Leads page's own `helpdesk.api.leads.create_lead` and `add_note`. So Leads access (`require_leads`), the acting user and the ERP site's duplicate check all stay the same. The lead is made from the **saved** record (`reload()`), and one check makes one lead.
  - A "Possible duplicate" refusal returns `{"duplicate": message}`, and the form asks **Create a new lead anyway?** (`allow_duplicate=1`).
  - If the note fails, the lead is kept (`noted: false`) and the form says so.
  - Once `lead` is set, the button becomes **Open Lead** (`/helpdesk/leads/<name>`).
- **Permissions:**
  - System Manager: full
  - Agent Manager: read, write, report, export
  - Agent: read, report
- **`Health Check API` role** (no desk access) with **Create / Read / Write on this DocType only**, for the website's API user. A post-model-sync patch (`setup_health_check_api_role`) sets it up, re-run safe. Fresh sites can run it with `bench execute`.
- **Tests** in `test_business_health_check.py`.
- **Docs:** `docs/business-health-check.md`.

The website side is already merged and switched off until it gets the API key. It creates a record when a check is finished and updates the same record when the client presses "Call me back".

## How to test

1. `bench --site <dev site> migrate`. **Business Health Check** appears, and the role **Health Check API** exists with Create/Read/Write on it only (Role Permissions Manager).
2. Create a record by hand with only a `report_link`. It's named `BHC-00001`, the business name becomes "Unnamed business", and **Open Report** opens the link.
3. Saving without `report_link` must fail (mandatory).
4. **API:** create a user with only the Health Check API role, generate keys, then:
   ```bash
   curl -X POST "https://<site>/api/resource/Business Health Check" \
     -H "Authorization: token <key>:<secret>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"business_name":"Test Co","report_link":"https://example.com/results/#id=1&k=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"}'
   ```
   It returns the new record. The same key must **not** be able to read other DocTypes (e.g. `/api/resource/HD Ticket` → 403).
5. **Create Lead** (needs Settings → CRM with Leads on): press it on a record. A lead appears in Leads with the details and a note holding the report link, and the button becomes Open Lead. Press it on a second record with the same phone: it asks before creating.
6. `bench --site <dev site> run-tests --doctype "Business Health Check"`. The Create Lead tests fake the ERP site with `FakeCRM`.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added (`test_business_health_check.py`). Not run locally (the local bench is on another branch), so they run in **server-tests** here
- [x] No ERPNext dependency: the hub runs without ERPNext
- [x] Spec or docs updated: `docs/business-health-check.md`
- [x] No secrets, tokens, passwords or customer data in code, tests or screenshots

Lint was run with the repo's pinned versions (black 22.6.0, isort 5.12.0 profile black, flake8 5.0.4 strict config, prettier 2.6.2): all clean.

**Labelled `no-auto-merge`** so the CRM owner can review and decide when it goes in. Remove the label to let it auto-merge.

author: nrdptel
body:
A planning review: a met target tightened, four ideas, a faster gate order, and one measured speed-up.

**What changed**

- **The cause-free apogees, tightened** ([ADR-318](https://github.com/nrdptel/fusionspace-eridanus/blob/main/docs/decisions/0318-the-2026-11-02-review-the-cause-free-apogees-tightened.md)). The six RocketPy comparisons flown on the same inputs with no written model difference agree on the apogee within +0.1123% (Valetudo), against a bound of 0.5%. The bound goes to 0.35%, 3.12 times the largest difference and about 550 times RocketPy's largest solver movement (6.35e-6). All nine same-drag apogees read high (+0.0383% to +1.2084%); too low an apogee flatters a waiver, so a new test, `no_same_drag_apogee_reads_low_adr_318`, stops any of the nine reading low past 0.001%. The three flights with a written cause keep 3%. The six case files, `same_drag_speeds_and_cause_free_apogees_hold_adr_289s_bounds`, the report and the pages that quote the bound follow.
- **Four ideas** in `docs/research/ideas.md`, each with its user, workflow, the scoreboard number it moves and a done-when: several flights, one drag; the intervals by sample rate; OpenRocket's next release measured before it ships; the wind's error as measured. The 2026-10-31 review's five ideas moved to the flight-data and ecosystem notes, and two older sections to the avionics and clubs notes, keeping `ideas.md` under its 200 lines.
- **The gate's order** (`scripts/gate.sh`): deny, evidence and site now run before validate and examples, and a failure of any of them, like a code step's, skips the slow steps. From 2026-10-25 to today the site failed 30 of 149 full runs that reached it and validate 1; the slow steps ran 10.1 hours in full runs that site, evidence or deny had already failed.
- **The smoother, about 10% faster** (`crates/hpr-flightdata/src/smoother/kalman.rs`): `solve` and `mul_transposed` work on a row's twelve columns at once, each entry's operations in the same order as before (sums from −0.0, as `Iterator::sum` starts), so the results are bit-identical.
- **The evidence register:** rows G35 to G38 record the 2026-11-02 search for real samples.

**How it was verified**

- Apogee numbers from `validation/reports/latest.json`; solver movement from `validation/fixtures/flight/rocketpy-whole-flight.json`'s `solver.relative_change_from_loose`.
- The speed-up, release builds, medians of six alternated rounds: `hpr analyze` on `axial.csv` 36.10 → 32.22 ms (−10.8%, spread 8%), `synthetic-pnut.pf2` −9.3%, the own-logger `flight.csv` −8.4%; text and JSON output byte-identical on 206 logs (412 outputs, every log fixture and 137 cached public logs).
- `scripts/gate.sh`: a full run on the final head; its result is added below when it finishes.

**What's left.** #1081's done-when (25% off `analyze`) isn't met by this alone; its comment lists the larger lever.

body:

| | |
|:---|:---|
|**_Related Issue(s)_**| Fixes #5897 |
|**_Has Unit Tests (y/n)_**| y |
|**_Documentation Included (y/n)_**| y |
|**_Generative AI was used in this contribution (y/n)_**| AI |

---
## Change Description

`Svc/Ccsds/CfdpManager/Types`:

- `PduHeader::fromSerialBuffer` now returns `FW_DESERIALIZE_FORMAT_ERROR` for headers that announce protocol features the body decoders do not implement: a CFDP version other than 1, the CRC-present flag, and the 64-bit large-file flag when `FileSize` is narrower than 64 bits. The check runs before the PDU data length and IDs are read, so no body decoder runs against an unsupported layout.
- Source entity ID, transaction sequence number, and destination entity ID are still accepted in any wire width from 1 to 8 octets, but the decoded value must fit the configured `EntityId`/`TransactionSeq` type; values that do not fit are rejected with `FW_DESERIALIZE_FORMAT_ERROR` instead of being silently truncated by the cast. The three fields share a new `decodeFieldInSize<T>` helper.
- `NakPdu::m_segments` is sized from `NakMaxSegments` instead of a hard-coded `58`, so raising the configuration constant cannot overrun the array.
- `PduHeader::CFDP_VERSION` names the supported version used by both `initialize()` and the new check.

Tests: seven raw-byte header tests in `Types/test/ut/PduTests.cpp` (unsupported version, CRC flag, large-file flag vs. configured `FileSize`, 8-octet IDs that fit, and source EID / TSN / dest EID one past the configured type), plus a component-level test `Event.FailPduHeaderDeserializationUnsupportedVersion` in `CfdpManager/test/ut` that pushes a version-2 header through `dataIn` and asserts the `FailPduHeaderDeserialization` event with `FW_DESERIALIZE_FORMAT_ERROR`. Three existing malformed-buffer tests (`FailAck/Fin/NakPduDeserialization`) had a flags byte of `0x00` (version 0); their first byte is now `0x20` so they keep exercising the truncation path they were written for.

Docs: `CfdpManager/docs/sdd.md` "Input Robustness" describes the header validation and the `NakMaxSegments` sizing.

## Rationale

As described in #5897, the header decoder accepted any version, CRC, and large-file flag and any EID/TSN width, then cast the values into the configured types. A peer using wider identifiers than this node is configured for would have its PDUs routed under truncated IDs, and a CRC-present or 64-bit-offset PDU would be decoded against the wrong body layout. The NAK array size was decoupled from the constant that bounds `m_numSegments`. Rejecting such PDUs at the header, through the existing `FailPduHeaderDeserialization` path, makes the failure explicit and keeps the engine from acting on misdecoded data. No FPP, port, event, or configuration interface changes.

## Testing/Review Recommendations

- `fprime-util check` in `Svc/Ccsds/CfdpManager/Types` (70 tests) and `Svc/Ccsds/CfdpManager` (207 tests; run through `ctest`, which sets the working directory the test data files require).
- Review `PduHeader.cpp` `fromSerialBuffer` ordering: flag validation happens before the data-length read, so a rejected header leaves `m_pduDataLength` and the IDs untouched.
- The large-file check is deliberately one-directional: a 64-bit flag is accepted when `FileSize` is `U64` because the body decoders already use `sizeof(FileSize)`; `initialize()` still emits the 32-bit flag unchanged.
- CfdpManager is not part of `Ref`, so no GDS integration test was run; the component-boundary behavior is covered by the `dataIn` test above.

## Future Work

- When `FileSize` is `U64`, the body decoders read 64-bit offsets regardless of the large-file flag, and the sender always sets the 32-bit flag; aligning the flag with the configured `FileSize` on both sides is a separate change.

author: 404wolf
body:
## Why

Dynamic-UI views had no typed source of truth. The web kept a Zod schema, a script turned it into JSON Schema for the model, a hand-written walker in `crates/dynamic_ui` checked views against that JSON, and every reader picked fields out of a `serde_json::Value`. AI chat drew `DisplayResults` from the model's streamed arguments and validated them in the browser.

## What

- `crates/dynamic_ui` defines `View`, `Widget` (`#[serde(tag = "type")]`: md, timeline, list, channelMessage, container) and the list widget's Soup `Query` as serde types. Unknown fields are dropped.
- Decoding is the validation. `decode_view` uses `serde_path_to_error`; problems name the place and leave out the value serde would quote. A container's `gap` is a `nutype` newtype bounded at 8, and the schema shows the bound. `check.rs`, its keyword lists and the generated JSON are deleted.
- schemars generates the PresentView schema that ExecuteCode's description includes (snapshotted with insta), and the `DisplayResults` tool schema. A widget's doc comment is its model-facing guidance, so a new widget is one Rust variant plus one arm in the web's exhaustive `match`.
- specta generates the web's view types (`just gen-dynamic-ui-types`, checked in CI's Check Specta Types step). The Zod schema, its generator script and the browser-side validation are gone.
- Every view reaches the browser decoded:
  - `DisplayResults` deserializes its view in `ai_tools` and returns it as the result;
  - `execution.views.present` decodes before presenting, and the harness writes the decoded view into the call's result;
  - the fold folds both calls to a new `ToolDetail::View` read from the result only, never the streamed arguments. `ActivityCard::View` holds a `View`, and so does the DM card.
- `dynamic_ui` is excluded from workspace-hack, like `agent_fold`, because the fold builds for wasm.
- No compatibility with old session logs or stored cards.

Error paths stop at the enclosing widget: serde buffers an internally tagged variant, so a problem inside a nested container names the widget, not the field.

Stacked on #8885, which is now merged; this targets main.

Macro tasks:
- MACRO-4564

author: kapong
body:
## Summary
`Rebroadcaster.copyInterleaved` crashed the app with `IndexOutOfBoundsException` on a Xiaomi MiTV-AFMU1 (Android 14) hardware encoder, so the multicast rebroadcast is broken on that box.

## Cause
On the last row, when the encoder's U-plane view is one byte shorter than the interleaved UV block, the method sets `lastUV.limit(y * width + n)` and then reads `lastUV.get(y * width + width - 1)`. That absolute index is at or past the limit just set, so the read throws.

## Fix
Lift `lastUV`'s limit to its capacity before the absolute read. The byte read is the last NV12 byte written for the current frame, so no stale data or out-of-range memory is read. The next row resets the limit, and the buffer is cleared after the loop.

## Testing
- `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug :app:testDebugUnitTest` passes.
- A standalone JVM reproduction of the method's buffer steps throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` with the old code and writes the correct last byte with the new code.
- Not yet verified on the device (the box is busy with other testing).
- No unit test added: the method is private and takes `android.media.Image.Plane`, which can't be constructed in JVM tests without a refactor.

Found during the WHEP fan-out spike for #8.

author: rohank6
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** Knowledge item types, statuses and shared counts, the theme top bar frame title, and three stat counts read in the active language, with a singular form for one.

Knowledge shows the raw item type and status ("meeting notes", "active") in every language and glues the shared count outside its key ("3 общий" in Russian). The theme top bar frame is titled "theme topbar (dark)" in every language. Mochi busiest day, the filtered Members count and the Telemetry trend point read "1 msgs", "1 of 1 mates" and "1 starts".

## Why it matters

These are everyday labels on Knowledge, Members, Telemetry and Mochi. Screen-reader users hear the English frame title on every themed page.

## Not a goal

- Other labels outside these files.
- Translating user-entered item titles or namespaces.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

The labels skipped the catalog, or passed an already-formatted number, so no translation or plural form could apply. Each one now comes from a catalog key with its count inside.

| Surface | Change |
|---|---|
| Knowledge type and status | `itemTypeLabel` / `itemStatusLabel` in `website/src/pages/knowledge/helpers.ts`, used by DetailView, ItemCard and the type filter |
| Related items | `pages.knowledge.detailView.shared_count` plural key |
| Theme top bar frame | `components.themeExperienceLayer.theme_topbar_dark` / `_light` |
| Mochi, Members, Telemetry | `busiest_day`, `member_count_filtered`, `daily_trend_point` become plural keys: raw `count`, formatted `n` |

The helpers look up their own keys only, so a stored type such as `toString` falls back to its own name. The detail badge uses singular status labels. The Mochi page formats the busiest-day date like the settings panel does. All 12 shipped catalogs get the keys; `en-XA` is regenerated.

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: stored item types and statuses are unchanged and still sent as filter values; only displayed text changes. English reads the same except "Active" / "Archived" capitalised and singular forms for one.

Reader: website/src/pages/members/MembersPageRoster.tsx:MembersPageRoster -- crew page -- member_count_filtered; MembersPage.filters.test.tsx

Reader: website/src/apps/mochi/src/renderer/SettingsPanel.tsx:SettingsPanel -- app -- busiest_day; knowledgeThemeLabels.test.ts

## Tests

`website/src/i18n/knowledgeThemeLabels.test.ts` checks the English text, German, Spanish, Russian, French, Japanese and Bengali output, the unknown and inherited-name fallbacks, and that each file routes its label through the catalog. Its checks fail on main and all pass here. Two coverage tests read the capitalised status and the formatted date.

Proof: not provable -- frontend test (prove.py runs Python only)

Rendered the labels from the shipped catalogs in a real Chromium page, on main and on this branch (screenshots below). The i18n render gate for `knowledge`, `developer-telemetry` and `crew-companion` reports the same counts as main.

author: connor-xy
body:
This PR makes Megatron DDP, `finalize_model_grads` and Megatron-FSDP use only the process groups of the model they serve. Today, NCCL user-buffer barriers, the DCP optimizer-key gather and several gradient reductions run on WORLD or on the global grid. They hang or pair the wrong ranks when one job holds several models or grids, or when ranks own different buffers. Callers that pass a `pg_collection` and maintainers of the data-parallel wrappers are affected. The PR consolidates 5 draft PRs from #6307 without changes. Each member is one commit, so review it commit by commit. It has no code dependency on other units or open PRs. The last commit regenerates `tools/process_group_usage_allowlist.json`. Members 4 and 5 already target the `mcore_adapter_v1.py` / `mcore_adapter_v2.py` split from #8471.

## Review

The unit's own commits: https://github.com/Connor-XY/Megatron-LM/compare/e82e85845ad95121e0d871ba36674a19afd1dbc5...0d09ab7cbaf3a9c36335ec27ec5e0137b497f5ab

The branch is a linear chain on main. The full PR diff also shows the PRs and units below this one until they merge.

## Members

- #8815: Scope DDP's NCCL user-buffer warmup barriers to the DP group. With `nccl_ub=True`, `_ParamAndGradBuffer` runs its two warmup barriers on the buffer's data-parallel group instead of WORLD, so pipeline stages with different expert buffers no longer hang at setup.
- #8816: Use Megatron-FSDP's own groups for UBR barriers and DCP key gather. It drops the WORLD barrier in the buffer constructor, runs the `manual_buffer_registration()` barriers on the user-buffer groups, and gathers DCP optimizer-state keys over the DP group, plus the expert DP group under EP.
- #8027: Read only the caller's process groups in finalize_model_grads. With a `pg_collection`, it uses only that collection's groups, raises `ValueError` for a missing one before any communication, and no longer reduces `num_tokens` over WORLD, which made per-token-loss gradients 4x too small on TP=2 x PP=2.
- #8051: Create Megatron-FSDP v1 TP groups collectively and validate pg_collection. It creates single-rank TP groups once with `new_subgroups_by_enumeration` on every rank, only for the axes the model uses, and raises `ValueError` naming any group the collection lacks.
- #8725: Reject GTP weight remat in Megatron-FSDP v1. `FullyShardedDataParallelV1` raises `ValueError` when dense or expert GTP weight remat is above 1 in the config or in the collection, because v1 cannot shard or reduce GTP shards correctly.

## Behavior changes for callers

- Without `nccl_ub`, without `preproc_state_dict_for_dcp_ckpt` and without a `pg_collection`, nothing changes.
- With `nccl_ub`, DDP and Megatron-FSDP buffer setup no longer synchronizes ranks outside the buffer's groups. Megatron-FSDP runs one fewer barrier at construction.
- Under EP, the DCP key gather adds one small gather over the expert DP group.
- `finalize_model_grads` with a `pg_collection` requires `tp` and `pp`, `embd` when PP > 1, and the DP x CP and TP x DP x CP groups its options use. A missing group raises `ValueError`. A missing `tp_dp_cp` used to raise `AssertionError`.
- Megatron-FSDP v1 raises `ValueError` instead of `AttributeError` for a collection missing a needed group.
- Megatron-FSDP v1 with GTP weight remat now fails at construction. Expert GTP > 1 is rejected even for a dense model.

The members touch files registered for determinism coverage but not their reductions, so this PR needs the `determinism-exempt` label.

## Teams

core-adlr, core-nemo, data-parallelism, megatron-fsdp

## Testing

Each member was GPU-tested against its base before consolidation. The consolidated chain (every unit in landing order, on current main) was run against main on 4 GPUs: 258 test files, and no test fails on the chain that passes on main. Tests in 28 files fail on both, mostly tests written for 8 GPUs, and one file times out on both.

author: aman-katyal
body:
* 💡 What: Replaced branching and slow conditional FPU division in `pmbus_linear11_to_float` and `pmbus_linear16_to_float` with a precomputed static lookup table (`PMBUS_EXP_LUT`).
* 🎯 Why: On ARM Cortex-M architecture with a single-precision FPU (like Cortex-M33), FPU multiplication is very fast (1-3 cycles) but division is slow (~14 cycles). Eliminating the conditional check for negative exponents and the subsequent division speeds up parsing telemetry in high-frequency loops.
* 📊 Impact: Converts bitwise math to O(1) array access and replaces a conditional slow division with a guaranteed fast FPU multiplication for negative exponents.
* 🔬 Measurement: Observe total cycle time of PMBus driver telemetry decoding and run CI tests. Verified against `ctest` test suites.

author: verigence-admin
body:
## Why
Live 2026-11-03: after the billing-documents rule of 2 Nov, 178 open "Deal charged below the standard price" tasks still read only booking-form figures.

A booking's checks run when its facts change, not when a rule changes. BOOKING_REBUILD recomputes only the bookings whose stored values would change, and leaves the checks to the worker.

## Change
New worker job `RULES_RERUN`:
- reports: the journey references, or none for every booking;
- a dry run unless the label ends with `-commit`;
- it queues each booking's native checks forced, the same call AUDIT_TASK_CLEANUP uses (`_rerun_native`).

The checks decide in the worker as usual:
- a check that now passes, or can no longer be judged, resolves its finding and closes its task;
- a check that still fails is refreshed.

## Tests
`tests/test_rules_rerun.py`: the dry run queues nothing; the commit queues the forced checks; unknown references are listed.

author: patel-om
body:
P3-K2, part 1 of 2, of the RTL pilot (council record `council/records/2026-10-18-capability-buildout.md`, section 9). This PR adds four knowledge documents. No skill card cites them yet. Part 2 is a separate PR because of the three-team limit: it adds `docs=` to the four cards and the packet tests, and it opens once this one merges.

## What changes
- `knowledge/design/buffering_flow_control.md` (new, 5,070 characters): the valid/ready handshake on each side of a single-clock FIFO; pointers, full, empty and count at a power-of-two depth and at any depth (wrap bits); registered flags, read latency, reset and clear; sizing; failure modes; how a FIFO is proved and simulated.
- `knowledge/design/pipeline_design.md` (new, 5,443 characters): handshake styles for pipelines; the skid buffer (register slice) as a three-state machine and in its two-register form; stalls that lose no data; buffered pipelines; failure modes; properties, covers and simulation.
- `knowledge/design/fsm_design.md` (new, 5,124 characters): FSM structure and Yosys's `fsm` pass; a timer as a state machine (idle, count, expire, one-shot or periodic, the running flag that clears itself, tick and prescaler); expiry and its interrupt; failure modes; properties and simulation.
- `knowledge/design/control_logic_design.md` (new, 4,962 characters): GPIO output data and output enable (direction), masked writes, input synchronisers and filtering, edge and level detect, sticky write-1-to-clear status, mask and the interrupt output; failure modes; properties and simulation.
- `capability/levels.json`, regenerated: the four documents are listed with `counts: false` ("no check record"). Totals do not change, and no level is claimed.

Every first body line is "Knowledge only: no tool run backs this.", the tier computed from each skill's own tools (none).

**Domain cap (pilot risk 4).** Every RTL seat already reads `rtl_design` (7,608). With part 2 the case totals will be: sync-fifo 12,678; skid-buffer 18,121; axil-timer 20,177 (with axi); apb-gpio 19,793 (with apb). The widest pilot block (an AXI4-Lite timer with a FIFO and an APB GPIO, which `tests/test_pilot_refinements.py` already plans) will carry six documents, 37,432 characters, under the 40,000 cap. Part 2 adds packet tests for all of these.

## Sources
All are `open`, and the writer read each one in full in this session. Bracketed tags in each document name the source; lines marked "inference" are the document's own reasoning.
- buffering_flow_control: Gisselquist's ZipCPU tutorial lesson 10 (FIFO) and his 2017 blog article on the basic FIFO; OpenTitan `prim_fifo_sync.sv` and `prim_fifo_sync_cnt.sv` (Apache 2.0); LaForest's Pipeline FIFO Buffer, FPGA Design Elements (MIT); Gisselquist's "AXI Handshaking Rules".
- pipeline_design: Gisselquist's "Building a Skid Buffer for AXI processing" and "Strategies for pipelining logic"; LaForest's Pipeline Skid Buffer (MIT); "AXI Handshaking Rules".
- fsm_design: Gisselquist's ZipTimer article and ZipCPU tutorial lesson 3 (FSMs); the Yosys command reference page for the FSM passes; OpenTitan rv_timer theory of operation and the OpenTitan Comportability Specification, interrupt handling (Apache 2.0).
- control_logic_design: OpenTitan GPIO theory of operation and the Comportability Specification, interrupt handling (Apache 2.0); Gisselquist's "The ZipCPU's Interrupt Controller" and "Some Simple Clock-Domain Crossing Solutions".

## What is not used
- **Cummings' SNUG and ICU papers** (asynchronous FIFO design; FSM design). The author site redirects to a library page that lists them but links no file. The open sources above back those topics instead.
- **Paid textbooks** the pilot plan named (Harris and Harris; Dally and Harting): not used.
