author: asuka109
body:
Fixes #1626.

## What this PR does

After a guardian approved an action in a Telegram, Feishu, Discord or WeChat chat, the agent's reply to the result never reached the chat. The approval task ran the continuation turn and read its output, but a messaging channel has no session stream to carry it, and nothing sent it on the channel. Defer and timer continuations already send their reply; approval continuations did not.

## Design & Invariants

- A reply the agent writes after an approval reaches the chat that asked for the action, the same way a deferred or timed reply does.
- An empty reply, or a reply from an agent whose text is private, sends nothing.
- The action has already run when the reply goes out. A reply that cannot be sent never marks the approval as failed and never runs the action again.
- Webchat is unchanged. Its reply still rides the session stream.
- Nothing here depends on reply streaming. The fix applies to whole-message sends, so it needs no switch.

## Test plan

- [x] Approve an action raised from a Telegram chat: the continuation reply arrives in that chat. Fails without the fix.
- [x] The continuation produces a blank reply: nothing is sent.
- [x] Deferred and timer continuations still send their reply as before (existing `backend-turn` tests).
- [ ] A send that fails after the action ran leaves the approval marked executed. Not covered: the fake channel cannot fail a send.
- [ ] `pnpm dev:all` run with a real channel. Not run.

The covered items are unit tests against the real wiring with a fake model and a fake channel. Local runs used Node 26 rather than the pinned 24.

## Not in this PR

- A rejected approval still drops the agent's reply on every channel. That is a separate behavior choice, tracked separately.

author: tgeorgiadis
body:
The web suite took over 12 minutes on Windows, nearly all of it in `controller.test.js`, because the test runner only parallelises separate files. Splitting that file makes the suite about 2.7 times faster.

## What changed
- **Split by area:** `controller.test.js` is now `browse`, `app-page`, `catalog-page`, `library`, `library-menus`, `settings`, `dialogs`, `input` and `tv-mode`. Each test moved word for word, and the helpers they share are in `web/controller.js`.
- **Shorter default wait:** `openApp` lowers Playwright's default from 30 s to 10 s, so a wrong selector fails sooner. This doesn't change the time of a passing run.
- **Warm-up step (not in the original plan):** `pnpm web` now runs `web/warm.js` first, which opens the app once so Vite fills its cache.
- **Separate navigation limit (not in the original plan):** navigation keeps its own limit of 90 s.
- **Fixed concurrency:** the script runs 4 test files at once.

## Why the extra steps
Without them, the split failed from a cold Vite cache. Nine servers bundled dependencies into the same folder at once, so first loads took about 80 s and the page then missed the 10 s wait:

| Cold run, no warm-up | Passed |
|---|---|
| 10 s limit on navigation too | 9 of 64 |
| 90 s limit on navigation | 30 of 64 |

Running `node --test "web/*.test.js"` directly on a cold cache still hits this, so use `pnpm web`, or run a single file. A single file doesn't need the warm-up.

## Timings
Full suite on Windows, on a 12-thread machine. Each file starts its own Vite server and WebKit browser, so tests run slower side by side, but the suite still finishes much sooner.

| Setup | Time | Passed |
|---|---|---|
| Before: one big file (Vite cache cold) | **758 s** | 64 of 64 |
| After: `pnpm web`, concurrency 4 (first run cold) | **268 s, 269 s, 299 s** | 64 of 64, all three runs |
| Warm cache, concurrency 3 | 299 s | 64 of 64 |
| Warm cache, concurrency 5 | 234 s | 64 of 64 |
| Warm cache, default concurrency (11 here) | 224 s, 245 s | 64 of 64, then 63 of 64 |

The one failure at default concurrency was "Back on the Get button", which waited out its own 10 s for the focus to reach the versions dialog. It passed in every other run, so it looks like a load problem, and that's why the script pins concurrency. Default concurrency was no faster than 5. I chose 4 over 5 because CI runners have 4 vCPUs.

The test names match the baseline run exactly. The long-README test that has been flaky on Windows passed in all of these runs.

This PR contains the following updates:

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>jdx/mise-action</summary>

### [`v5.2.6`](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/releases/tag/v5.2.6): : Fix step hanging after a failed cache restore

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.2.5...v5.2.6)

The action now exits as soon as its work is done. Before this release, a cache restore that failed during the download could leave the step running for up to ten minutes after setup had finished.

##### Fixed

- **A failed cache restore no longer leaves the step hanging.** If the mise cache download failed partway through, for example with `getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN`, the action logged a warning, installed the tools and saved the cache, then stopped producing output. The step stayed in progress until the job was cancelled or a timer inside `@actions/cache` fired after 10 minutes. That timer is left running when a download fails ([actions/toolkit#2470](https://redirect.github.com/actions/toolkit/issues/2470)), and it kept the Node process alive. The action now exits explicitly after both the main step and the post step finish. It waits up to 5 seconds for log output to flush, then exits. The exit code set by any earlier failure is kept. Errors that aren't `Error` objects now mark the step as failed with their message. Before, they caused an unhandled rejection. ([#​718](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/pull/718) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx) and [@​kjanat](https://redirect.github.com/kjanat), fixes [#​717](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/issues/717))

body:
## Description
Implements an automated, non-destructive, one-command local native PostgreSQL bootstrap pipeline (`scripts/bootstrap_local.py`) enabling all six team members to initialize, migrate, seed, populate, verify, and synchronize the entire GridLens data warehouse and Next.js BI dashboard without requiring Docker, Docker Desktop, or cloud databases.

### Key Changes & Architectural Improvements:
1. **One-Command Automated Bootstrap (`scripts/bootstrap_local.py`)**:
   - **Environment Validation**: Validates Python runtime (>= 3.11), automatically provisions `.env` from `.env.example` if missing, and verifies raw dataset integrity (`data/raw/manifest.json`).
   - **Safe Database Provisioning**: Safely checks and creates `sl_grid_warehouse` and `sl_grid_warehouse_test` with UTF-8 encoding via local PostgreSQL maintenance database (`postgres`). Strictly non-destructive: never issues `DROP DATABASE`, `DROP SCHEMA`, or `DROP TABLE`.
   - **Sequential Migrations (001–022)**: Uses `MigrationRunner` to apply all 22 sequential forward migrations with SHA-256 checksum immutability, skipping already applied migrations cleanly.
   - **Least-Privilege Roles**: Configures login credentials for `grid_etl` and dedicated read-only `grid_analyst` from environment variables without password leakage.
   - **Conformed Dimension Seeding**: Idempotently seeds 13 conformed dimensions and reference tables (`dw.dim_date`, `dw.dim_interval`, `dw.dim_power_plant`, etc.) with zero duplicate rows.
   - **Historical Warehouse Population**: Idempotently loads authentic CEB 5-year sales (49 rows), NASA POWER 5-year weather (21,924 rows), and PUCSL March 2024 15-minute dispatch (107,115 rows), skipping tables already populated.
   - **Read-Only Warehouse Audit**: Verifies all 7 schemas, 4 fact tables, conformed dimensions, 5 materialized views, and read-only `grid_analyst` access.
   - **Next.js Environment Synchronization**: Automatically writes and synchronizes `web/.env.local` configured with `DATA_SOURCE_MODE=live` and correct local port.
   - **CLI Flags**: Supports `--dry-run` (simulation mode), `--verify-only` (read-only audit), and `--skip-data`.

2. **Automated Safety Test Suite (`tests/unit/test_bootstrap_local.py`)**:
   - 14 automated unit tests covering Python runtime gates, `.env` file generation, missing raw file warnings, AST verification against `DROP` statements, database creation idempotency, migration verification, role configuration, data loading skips, and CLI flags.

3. **Code Quality, Security & Link Sanitization**:
   - Added safe cursor helpers `_fetch_scalar()` and `_fetch_int()` eliminating `Any | None` indexability errors.
   - Converted dynamic SQL queries in warehouse verification to safe `psycopg.sql.SQL` + `psycopg.sql.Identifier` patterns.
   - Eliminated machine-specific `file:///c:/...` absolute links across `README.md`, `web/README.md`, and `docs/database/local-native-postgresql-setup-guide.md`, replacing them with relative repository markdown links.

## Branch & Phase Reference

- Working Branch: `fix/local-native-bootstrap-safety`
- Target Branch: `development`

author: myshevchuk
body:
## Summary

Runs OrgSynDB on a server with Docker or Podman Compose. Two containers share one image and one data volume:

- **`builder`** fetches the collection from Git and builds the site inside the container. It checks for new commits every `ORGSYNDB_INTERVAL` seconds (300 by default). The repository can be an `https://` or `ssh://` URL on the internet or intranet, or a repository on the server mounted under `/srv/git/`.
- **`web`** is Caddy, serving the current release on port 8080.

### Auto-update of the application

- The image holds a git clone of the application. `builder` fetches `ORGSYNDB_APP_REPO` / `ORGSYNDB_APP_REF` into it; the default ref is `main`, the stable branch. Moving the app off GitHub later only means changing that URL.
- A new app commit is built first with the newest collection commit. If that build fails, `builder` goes back to the previous app commit and builds the collection with it.
- A combination of app and collection commits that failed is not rebuilt. `orgsyndb-deploy retry` clears that record, for failures caused by something else, such as a network outage.
- A successful build is copied into `releases/`, and the `current` symlink is swapped to point at it. A failed build never changes what is served.
- An app commit that changes `deploy/docker/` is not used, because it needs a new image. `builder` notices this by comparing git tree ids and logs that the image needs rebuilding.
- The image includes the ox-hugo, tomelr and Pagefind caches, so builds in the container need no internet access.

## Files

- `deploy/docker/orgsyndb-deploy`: the updater, Python standard library only, with the commands `run`, `sync`, `status` and `retry`.
- `deploy/docker/Dockerfile`, `deploy/docker/Caddyfile`
- `deploy/compose.yaml`, `deploy/orgsyndb.env.example`
- `tests/test_deploy.py`
- README: a new "Container deployment" section; the existing Caddy example moves under "Serve a copy with Caddy". It says that following `main` brings only tested versions, and that following `develop` is for a trial server.
- OpenSpec: new capability `container-deployment`; the change is archived on this branch.

## Testing

- 23 updater tests run against throwaway git repos with a fake build. They cover the first publish, no rebuild without a change, new collection commits, pruning of old releases, a failed collection commit, an app update, a broken app with fallback, an app commit that needs a new image, updates turned off, branch and path settings, PDFs, an unreachable repository, settings errors, `status`, `retry`, and a usage error.
- `docker compose config` passes. `caddy adapt` passes using the official Caddy image, and Caddy served correctly through the symlink and across a swap.
- Full suite on Python 3.14, run on top of `develop`: 815 passed, 306 skipped. The skips are tests that need Hugo, Emacs or Caddy, which aren't installed in the sandbox.
- **The image itself has never been built**, because the sandbox blocks Fedora's package mirrors. The first `docker compose build` is the real test.

## Before relying on it

- Building the image needs internet access. For an offline server, build elsewhere and move the image with `docker save` / `docker load`.

author: fongap
body:
## Evidence and problem
`intake-main-ci.ts` reserves a `CI Evidence` pending status pointing at the short-lived intake run with a 120-second grace period. Once that intake has completed, a later intake may retry an identical head SHA when a long-running Central CI job is still active. Recent Windows CI jobs in `action-worker` lasted well beyond the intake's reservation period, so this is an existing deduplication gap rather than a reason to add another lease system.

## Change
- In the **prepare** job of `run-central-ci-ref` (main branch only), after validating the requested revision and before starting expensive sandbox jobs, write a new pending `CI Evidence` pointing at the **currently running Central CI run**.
- Existing `ciState` checks that run's `queued`/`in_progress` status and will not enqueue another main CI for the same head during its execution.
- Keep `AW_STATUS_TOKEN` mandatory (Commit statuses: Read and write), fail closed if absent, and do **not** fall back to `AW_CONTROL_TOKEN`.
- Add a contract test and changelog entry.

## Scope and limitations
- Does not change CI verdicts or skip required tests.
- Does not introduce another task/lease store, private-repo jobs, paid GitHub features or GitHub token fallback.
- This narrows the post-intake scheduling gap; fully atomic suppression of simultaneous independent entrypoints still requires separate evidence-based analysis.

## Validation
Existing CI, tests, and merge rules on this PR.

author: christopherkarani
body:
Mechanical split of two oversized files in the CLI and MCP HTTP server. No behavior change: whole declarations move into `<Original>+<Topic>.swift` files in the same module. Nothing is renamed, reordered, or reformatted inside a declaration, and doc comments travel with their declarations.

## Files

**`Sources/WaxCLI/WaxCLICommand.swift`** (2147 → 173)

| File | Lines | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `WaxCLICommand.swift` | 173 | `WaxCLI` root, `MCPScope`, `MCP`, `MCP.Serve`, `normalizedKey`, `resolveToolPath`, `ensureToolExists`, `CLIError` |
| `WaxCLICommand+Install.swift` | 579 | `MCP.Install`, `WaxMCPHostRuleWriter`, `WaxMCPAgentPlaybook`, and the private install helpers (skill guidance, skill install per host, redacted snippets) |
| `WaxCLICommand+Doctor.swift` | 560 | `MCP.Doctor`, `lowDiskWarning`, `MCPDoctorSurface`, `MCPVectorHealthDiagnostics`, `MCPSmokeCheckOutput`, `smokeCheckFailureContext`, `extension ProcessRunner { runMCPSmokeCheck }`, and the host registration matrix helpers |
| `WaxCLICommand+Uninstall.swift` | 166 | `MCP.Uninstall` |
| `WaxCLICommand+ProcessRunner.swift` | 140 | `CapturedProcessOutput`, `ProcessRunner` (`run`, `runCaptured`, and their private helpers) |
| `WaxCLICommand+Pathing.swift` | 556 | `MCPInstallRuntime`, `MCPSkillInstall`, `MCPRuntimeValidation`, `Pathing` |

`ProcessRunner.runMCPSmokeCheck` moves into an `extension ProcessRunner` in the Doctor file, next to its only caller. It uses no private `ProcessRunner` members, so it keeps `fileprivate`, and `MCPSmokeCheckOutput` and `smokeCheckFailureContext` stay `private`.

**`Sources/WaxMCPServer/HTTPApp.swift`** (1169 → 655)

| File | Lines | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `HTTPApp.swift` | 655 | `MCPHTTPApplication` actor (unchanged) and `isInitializeRequest` (its only caller is the actor) |
| `HTTPApp+Transport.swift` | 420 | `MCPHTTPServerPipeline`, `MCPHTTPPeerReset`, `MCPHTTPPeerCloseWatch`, `HopResume`, `HTTPHandler` |
| `HTTPApp+RequestPolicy.swift` | 122 | `HTTPAuthPolicy`, `HTTPRequestBodyLimit` |

`MCPHTTPApplication` stays whole at 655 lines. Its session and recovery methods all touch `private` stored state, so splitting the actor would mean widening about ten members. Each new HTTP file repeats the original `#if MCPServer` wrapper and the import header, including the `#if canImport(Darwin)` / `Glibc` block.

## Widened members

- `normalizedKey(_:)` in `WaxCLICommand.swift`: `private` → `internal`. It is used by `Serve`, `Install`, and `Doctor`, which now live in different files.

Nothing else changed access level.

## Move proof

A scratchpad script compares the multiset of non-blank, trimmed lines in the original file (`origin/main`) with the union of the split files. It ignores `import`, `extension X {`, `}`, and `#if`/`#elseif`/`#else`/`#endif` scaffolding, plus `private`/`fileprivate`/`internal` modifiers.

```
WaxCLICommand.swift
original: 1584 content lines; split (6 files): 1584
only in original: none
only in split: none

HTTPApp.swift
original: 869 content lines; split (3 files): 869
only in original: none
only in split: none
```

A stricter sorted-line diff that keeps access modifiers shows only the new imports and `#if` headers, one `extension ProcessRunner {` with its `}`, and `private func normalizedKey` → `func normalizedKey`.

## API diff

`wax-cli` and `wax-mcp` are executable targets with no library product, so `swift package diagnose-api-breaking-changes` does not apply. `git diff origin/main` adds no `public` or `package` declarations. The only `public` matches are existing path strings such as `Resources/skills/public/wax-mcp`.

## Tests

- `swift build -j 4 --build-tests`: passes
- `swift build -j 4 --traits default,MCPServer --product wax-cli`: passes
- `swift build -j 4 --traits default,MCPServer --product wax-mcp`: passes
- `swift test -j 4 --traits MCPServer --filter 'WaxCLITests|wax_mcpTests' --skip WaxMCPProcessTests`: passes (434 tests in 11 suites and 205 tests in 15 suites)
- `node Resources/npm/waxmcp/scripts/launcher-tests.mjs`: 24/25 pass. The one failure (`first-run install-hermes-plugin stages bundled runtime binaries`) also fails on main because no `dist/` runtime is staged.
- `bash Resources/scripts/quality/public_repo_hygiene.sh`: ok

author: mgcronin
body:
Closes #1909

Part of epic #1894. **Stacked on #2083 (#1908, protocol version 3), which is not merged yet.** This branch was cut from `feature/issue-1908-protocol-v3-lap-race`, and this PR's base is that branch so the diff below is #1909's alone. When #2083 merges, GitHub retargets this PR to `main` if the head branch is deleted on merge; if it is not deleted, change the base by hand.

## What changed

The room core (`apps/instance/src/room/core/room.ts`) is now authoritative for a **lap race with items**. A race whose settings carry `lapRace: { laps, items, seed }` runs `@onyourleft/domain`'s `stepRace`, the same step the device predicts with, once per tick on the room's own instants (`tick × frameIntervalMs`). The room's answer is the one that counts (ADR 0028 D-2 rule 4).

**Effort distance is untouched (ADR 0060 D-3.1, D-5.3, D-5.4)**
- Every rider is still re-simulated from reported power through the one physics.
- The grade is read **round the lap** at the effort distance (`before % lapLength`), and drafting reads the effort distance too.
- A frame's `decimetres` stays the **effort** distance and is never the drawn one, so a race offset can never reach a client's correction or the grade it reads.

**Inputs, never outcomes**
- `lane` and `item-use` from a connected seat are admitted only past the last lap-race input sequence admitted on that connection. Replays and stale inputs are dropped.
- Inputs are ignored before the race runs, and `item-use` is ignored with items off.
- **Rate:** one use per tick. The rest of a burst is dropped and **never queued**, because a queued use would fire on the next pick-up by itself.
- A use with nothing held changes nothing.
- An outcome a client claims is already refused by the decoder (#1908); the conformance script sends one and the rider is not closed.

**What a frame carries**
- Each rider's `raceOffsetCentimetres`, `lane`, `held` and `lapsDone`.
- The tick's `itemEvents`. These are read from the race state before and after the step: uses, then hits (a slowing effect starting this tick), then pick-ups, capped at `MAXIMUM_ITEM_EVENTS`. A hit absorbed by a rain cape moves nobody and is not an event.

**Finish order and standings**
- The finish order is the race's own rule (`standings`: finish instant, then drawn distance).
- Standings and time gaps use the drawn distance.

**Rejoin:** a dropped rider is coasted at 0 W (rule 1) and keeps lane, held item and offset through the window. A rejoin resets the input sequence and nothing else.

**Plausibility (rules 2 and 3):** unchanged. A rider is flagged, never ejected.

**Settings:** `settings.ts` gains `lapRace` and refuses a lap race that is a group ride, laps outside 1–100, or a seed outside 0 to 2³²−1. The welcome says `lapRace: { laps, items }` and **never the seed**: a client that knew it would know every draw in advance.

**Both adapters**
- `RoomPlan.lapRace` is passed through `settingsFromPlan`. Reading it from the store is #1910's job; until then only a caller that builds a plan sets it.
- `room-host.ts` passes each tick's item events to a new `onItemEvent` callback. The worker forwards them over IPC, and the router logs a `room-item-event` line.
- `log.ts` gains an `EVENT_KEYS` entry that keeps `room`, `riderId`, `itemEvent` and `item` (each with a value check) and redacts everything else.
- The Durable Object worker-under-test gains `LapConformanceRoom` for `test:workerd`.

`docs/agents/instance.md` gets one paragraph on this.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Where |
|---|---|
| The room's answer is read back from the frame a client decodes, over the real socket | `lap-race-conformance.test.ts`: the self-host adapter (real `ws` on loopback) transcript is decoded. The first frame with a `hit` also carries the `use` of that item, and the **next** frame has the hit rider's `raceOffsetCentimetres` lower. M1 and M16 below |
| Determinism across adapters, byte for byte | Same file: the core reference, the Durable Object under fakes, and the self-host adapter all send identical transcripts. **Also under a real `workerd`**: `conformance.test.ts`'s workerd block, run locally with `pnpm --filter @onyourleft/instance run test:workerd` (13 passed). M3 |
| A use without an item changes nothing; 100 uses in a second are admitted at most at the stated rate | `core/lap-race.test.ts`: *changes nothing in the next frame for a use with nothing held, and never queues it* (byte-identical frames against a twin room for 40 s); *admits at most one use a tick from 100 sent in a second* (exactly one `use` event, then none for 49 s). M4 |

_Requested by **Tony** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01864Pge151bDtPSVqKUZTQ3?thread=cmsg_01864Pge151bDtPSVqKUZTQ37fP9zWsKswY8LVv9368A2g)_

## What

- `examples/hdl_eval_all.py --repair-rounds N` adds an agent loop. After the first generation, each VerilogEval or RTLLM sample is checked with `hdl_bench.tool_feedback`, which compiles the extracted answer on its own with iverilog. A sample fails on a compile error or on a warning the scorer already counts as a failure.
  - A failing sample goes back to the model as a multi-turn chat that includes the tool messages, for up to N rounds.
  - No testbench is involved, so the model never sees expected outputs.
  - One reused vLLM engine (`VllmGen`) serves every round. `vllm_generate` keeps its signature.
  - The first-round generations are saved to `<out>.round0.samples.json`, and the per-round stats go to `repair` in the result.
- `--thinking on|off` passes `enable_thinking` to the chat template. The default is the template's own setting. This replaces the pod-side patch used for the 26B base eval.
- The `tests/test_hdl_train_eval.py` docstring now lists these as item 5. The repair loop is tested with a fake generator, `chat_prompt` with a fake tokenizer, and `tool_feedback` runs when iverilog is installed.

## Why

In the H5 SFT VerilogEval run, about 10 of the 89 failures are compile or lint failures. This loop targets those. It is the open-tool agent piece of the HDL Stage 1 plan.

## Testing

- `pytest helioslm_v5/tests/test_hdl_train_eval.py` gives 7 passed and 2 skipped; the skipped tests need iverilog.
- flake8 is clean.

Template-like academic prose had no shared checks: dashes as connectors, `rather than` framing, clefts, colon chains, filler, closing restatements, one-sentence paragraphs, figurative verbs and placeholder nouns were left to a private author profile. Responses to reviewers were not covered at all.

**Changes**
- `rules.md`: new section *Formulaic prose patterns* (FP1–FP9). Draft writes without them; review reports a pattern as STYLE when it recurs, hides a relation or an active project rule requires it. A single clear occurrence can stay; no authorship inference.
- `rules.md`: new section *Responses to reviewers* (RR1–RR3): verify claims of change against the final manuscript, check what a manuscript edit answers, quote the final version.
- Refinements of existing IDs: B4 (bare numerals, `former`/`latter`), A2 (`-fold`, `divide … by`, `either`), C4, D3, G4 (text inside figures), RC5 (reference series, tick labels), M2 (unobserved limitations), EC2 (exclusions and subsets), L (revision restraint), commas (independent clauses, comma splice, paired commas), numbers (one form per quantity, minus and en dash, decimal point), wording candidates and calibration rows.

**Provenance**

- S-AUTHOR (new): an author's accepted and declined proposals across two manuscripts and revisions; a journal reviewer's independent requests agree with FP7 and FP8.
- S-AUDITS: a check of a response letter that found contradicted claims of removed wording.
- All public examples are synthetic. The sources stay in the private archive.

**Scope and overlap**
- FP items are STYLE checks in the shared corpus and become hard rules only through the opt-in set. T16 now keeps a single `rather than` or em dash.
- Existing IDs were extended rather than duplicated. FP8 complements A1, FP9 complements B4 and FP7 complements C11.

- `python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`: 70 tests OK, 1 skipped (symlink privilege), including a new test for list adds.

author: roboco-app[bot]
body:
Fix the root cause behind the 'quality gate red' bounce family: the shared clone-root dev venv is frozen at the clone-time uv.lock while each task worktree carries the current lockfile. Re-locate by symbol in roboco/services/workspace.py (line refs drift): _DEP_INSTALL_MARKER = ".git/.roboco-dep-install" (~:522); install_dev_deps (~:1981, marker written ~:2030, marker checked ~:2129); worktree .venv -> ../../.venv symlink (~:778-796); ensure_workspace (~:1465); the `uv sync --extra dev` command built at ~:574-592; the healthy-clone path only fetches and runs install_dev_deps on the parked clone root (~:1424-1461), so the lockfile digest (~:500-523) never changes after the first install and the install is skipped forever.

Design choice is yours: compute the digest from the task worktree's actual lockfiles, OR re-sync the clone root to origin's current head before hashing. Weigh that sibling worktrees may carry different lockfile versions, so a naive per-worktree digest could thrash the shared venv. HARD REQUIREMENT: a re-sync must not rip dependencies out from under a concurrently active sibling worktree mid-task — use a staged / copy-then-swap build (or equivalent) plus a lock so concurrent ensure calls serialize.

Tests, next to the existing workspace tests: (1) regression: change the lockfile, re-enter the ensure path, assert the install re-runs and the marker digest changes; (2) after a uv.lock bump on the default branch, the respawned agent's venv installs the newly pinned version (assert via a pinned package version such as fastapi-guard matching the lockfile pin; mock the uv invocation if needed); (3) concurrency: a re-sync while a sibling worktree is active does not break it (the old venv stays usable until the swap). Do NOT fold in the roboco/security.py symptom fixes (tasks 92a48cc0, 1073f708, 590d5d1b). Run make gate before submitting.

body:
## 背景

dotfiles は、macOS / Linux / WSL2 で共通の開発環境を再現するための設定リポジトリです。`bin/claude-ds` は Claude Code を DeepSeek の API で動かすラッパで、自動 compact の位置を公式推奨の 786432 に置いていました。2026-11-03 の実測では、費用の約8割が文脈 10万超の呼び出しから出ており、文脈が大きいまま何百回も呼ぶことが主因でした。この PR は費用を下げる傘ブランチ `ds-cost-down` の孫1です。

## このプルリクエストの目的

自動 compact を、区切りでの自己 compact（200k が目安）を取りこぼしたときの安全網として、実際に効く位置へ置き直します。

## 実装内容

- `bin/claude-ds`: `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` を `233000` に変更
- `bin/README.md` §3.2: 「公式値をそのまま採る」という理由を、実測に合わせて書き直し
- ADR を1本追加: 以前の判断と覆す理由、選んだ値と比べた値、環境変数の意味の出典、サブエージェントに効くか（未確認）と配布後の確かめ方

## レビューで見てほしいところ

- 値を 233000 にした根拠（self-compact の self-compact の閾値 150k（孫2で変更）に区切りを待つ幅を足した位置（発火は約200k）で、機会を奪わない。試算は約15%減）。
- 環境変数の意味は公式の文書から「値そのものの位置で始まる」と読みました。式は明記されていないので、読みが妥当か確認してください。
- サブエージェントに効くかは公式の文書で確認できず、ADR に「未確認」と書き、配布後にログで確かめる手順を残しました。
- 通常の Claude の会話には効きません（この環境変数は `claude-ds` の中にしか無い）。

## テスト結果

`pre-commit run --all-files`、`python3 -m unittest discover -s bin/tests`、`doc-id verify` はすべて緑です。新しい自動テストは設定値と文書の変更のため追加していません。

## 今後の予定

マージ後に人間が `deploy-all.sh` で配ると効きます。孫2 が self-compact の閾値を見直す場合の値の再調整は孫2 側で行います。

author: sinikebe
body:
## What

Five hardening fixes.

**Removed members cannot rejoin.** When the owner removes a member from a shared basket, the invitation link is renewed (`invite_version` + 1). The removed member's old link no longer works. A member who leaves on their own can still come back with the current link. The removal confirmation now says the link changes.

**Failed writes count toward the limits.**
- The per-account write limits (contributions, private recipes, shared baskets) used to bump their counter inside the write transaction, so a write that failed and rolled back erased its own count.
- The attempt is now counted in its own statement before the transaction. A guard (`is_in_transaction`) refuses to count inside one.
- The per-account advisory lock that serializes quota checks stays inside the transaction (`lock_account_writes`).

**Connector reading status is admin-only.**
- `POST /api/v2/connector-stores/{id}/products/status` now requires an administrator.
- Price pages still call `page-refresh`, but each client is limited to 30 calls a minute, counted before any connector code runs.
- A connector's status hook gets 5 seconds before the products are reported `unavailable`.
- In the UI, only administrators see the reading badges and keep polling; other visitors only trigger the refresh.

**Logout clears private data from the device.**
- Signing out removes the account's shared basket copies, their unsent changes, the followed shared basket id, the pending invitation and its product and recipe drafts.
- If unsent changes or drafts would be lost, a confirmation says how many first.
- The personal basket and its settings stay, as before.
- The invitation link is no longer written into the browser's copy of a shared basket. Offline, the page says the link will appear once back online.

**Private recipe page after logout.** The recipe detail is keyed by account too, so a private recipe disappears from the page as soon as the account signs out.

## Checks

- Backend: 245 tests pass on a fresh database. New tests cover:
  - a removed member's old link being refused while the new one differs;
  - refused shared basket changes and refused private recipe writes still reaching the limit;
  - the guard against counting inside a transaction;
  - status being 403 for visitors and 200 for an admin;
  - the per-client page limit running no connector code;
  - a slow status hook reported unavailable.

  `ruff` is clean.
- Frontend: typecheck, lint, build and every suite pass. New tests cover the logout keys (other accounts on the same browser untouched), counting unsent changes and drafts, and the invitation link never being stored.

O **auto-refresh** do cockpit vira **preferência persistida**, ligada por padrão.

author: geezery
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"geezery"} -->
_Requested by **Antti** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U6Qpvu76TLdNoyi6xMfW3Z?thread=cmsg_01U6Qpvu76TLdNoyi6xMfW3Z6q6Er1D9N88mGUfbNcZ964)_

## What and why

With thumbnails on, pictures often went missing: anywhere in the ⌘Tab stack, or a second window of one app. They showed after letting go of ⌘Tab and opening it again. ⌘Tab asked for up to 16 captures at once and the Dock list for 8. ScreenCaptureKit dropped some of them, and a failed one was not tried again until the next ⌘Tab.

Windows' Alt-Tab and taskbar thumbnails just *are there*. This aims for that:

- **Capture only what may have changed** (`PreviewFreshness`). A window is pictured again only when it was active since its last picture, is active now, or changed title or size. A window left in the background keeps its picture, so ⌘Tab usually captures one or two windows instead of 16. The trade-off: a window that changes on its own in the background, such as a video or a chat, shows how it was left.
- **One shared store.** ⌘Tab, the Dock list and Snap Assist share the kept pictures: the last picture of each open window, at most 64, with no two-minute expiry. Pictures are dropped when the window closes, the screen locks or the Mac sleeps.
- **Packed as HEIC** (`PictureCodec`): about 50–80 kB per picture instead of 1.4 MB as a bitmap. A picture is unpacked off the main thread at the size its view needs: 400 px for Dock cards, 640 px for grid tiles, full size for the stack and the peek pane. Unpacked pictures live only while a panel is open. If packing fails, that one picture is kept as a bitmap.
- **Queue** (`CaptureQueue`): at most three captures at a time, and the hovered window or the card stepped to goes first. There is one capture per window, shared by everyone who asks, and its picture is kept even if the list or ⌘Tab that asked has closed.
- **Earlier start.** ⌘Tab loads pictures from the press, not from the draw 150 ms later. The Dock fetches ScreenCaptureKit's window list as the mouse reaches an icon.
- **One retry** after 250 ms with a fresh window list, as a one-shot sleep.
- **Diagnostics.** A failed capture is logged with the app name and error domain/code, never a title. The debug log gets a `previews` line with counts (kept, kB, captured, reused, failed, retried).

Privacy docs updated: SECURITY.md, SCOPE.md, README, wiki Privacy page, llms-full.txt. Two changes are worth reading there: "while ⌘Tab is visible" becomes "when ⌘Tab is pressed", and "up to two minutes, at most 24" becomes "while the window is open, at most 64, packed".

Not built or run here: written without a Mac, so CI is the first compile. To try: turn thumbnails on, ⌘Tab through 10+ windows across several apps, and hover a Dock icon with several windows. Pictures should all be there on the first ⌘Tab after each window has been seen once. Then export the debug log and check the `previews` line.

## Checklist

- [ ] `make test` passes (new suites: `PreviewFreshness`, `CaptureQueue`, `PictureCodec`; CI will tell)
- [x] No third-party dependencies, no networking code, no polling or repeating timers
- [x] New user-facing strings are added to every `Localizable.strings` (none added)
- [ ] Tried with at least one Electron app, a browser and Finder
- [x] No window or tab titles in logs

author: mrmartineau
body:
## ELI5

Orca opens `.mdx` files as Markdown, and plugins are not allowed to recolor Markdown files. So an MDX syntax plugin has no effect today. This change lets a plugin color `.mdx` files in the source view. `.mdx` files still open in the rich Markdown editor.

## What Changed

- **Before:** a plugin syntax that claims `.mdx` is ignored, because `.mdx` maps to the protected `markdown` core language.
- **After:** the plugin's grammar colors `.mdx` in the source view and in diffs.
- **Mechanism:** `.mdx` joins `.jsp` and `.jspf` in the list of extensions a plugin may recolor in `src/renderer/src/store/plugin-syntax-packs.ts`. I renamed the list from `PLUGIN_OVERRIDABLE_STOPGAP_EXTENSIONS` to `PLUGIN_OVERRIDABLE_EXTENSIONS`, because MDX is not a stopgap. `usePluginSyntaxLanguage` only feeds the Monaco language of `MonacoEditor`, `DiffViewer` and `DiffSectionBody`. The rich editor is chosen from the core language (`viewerLanguage` in `editor-panel-render-model.ts`), which stays `markdown`.
- `docs/reference/plugin-syntax.md` names `.mdx` and the source-view trade-off.
- New test: `src/renderer/src/store/plugin-syntax-packs.test.ts`.

## Why

MDX mixes Markdown with JSX and ESM `import`/`export`. The Markdown grammar cannot color those parts. A plugin grammar can (I am writing an MDX one as an Orca plugin), so MDX support can ship as a plugin and the core stays small.

Alternatives I considered:

- **Improve Orca's built-in Markdown grammar for MDX.** This helps everyone with no plugin, but it is a larger change and a product decision.
- **Give `.mdx` its own core language.** Rejected: the rich editor is chosen from `markdown`, so `.mdx` would lose it.

## Linked Issue

None yet. This stays a draft until an issue is filed and linked here.

## Visual Proof

Not attached yet.

- **Before:** with an MDX plugin enabled, `.mdx` source view still uses the Markdown colors.
- **After:** `.mdx` source view uses the plugin's colors; the rich editor is unchanged.

Screenshots will be added before this leaves draft.

## Testing

- [ ] I manually tested these changes locally
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below

Ran locally:

- `pnpm test:node src/renderer/src/store/plugin-syntax-packs.test.ts`: 2 pass. The `.mdx` case fails without the source change.
- `pnpm exec oxlint` and `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on the changed files: clean.
- `pnpm tc:web`: passes.

Not run: full `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`, the running app, Linux, Windows, SSH.

## Risk

**Level:** Low

With a plugin that claims `.mdx` enabled, the `.mdx` source view and diffs use the plugin's Monaco language id instead of `markdown`. Code that checks `language === 'markdown'` then turns off there:

- `[[` document completion (the provider is registered for `markdown` only).
- Markdown comments / annotations (`use-monaco-markdown-annotations.ts`).
- The completion document list set in `use-monaco-editor-decorations.ts`.
- `unicodeHighlight.ambiguousCharacters` turns on (`MonacoEditor.tsx`).

I did not check whether the doc-link decoration controller also turns off.

This is opt-in: it only applies to users who install a plugin that claims `.mdx`. No saved data or settings change. Back-out is a plain revert.

## AI Disclosure

Written with Claude Code (Claude Sonnet 5.5), including the change, the test and this description. The checks above were run by the agent.

## Review

AI code-review summary (from reading the code, not from running the app):

- **Cross-platform:** a lowercase `endsWith('.mdx')` check on the path, with no separator or platform code.
- **SSH / remote:** renderer only, keyed on the file name, so local and remote files behave the same.
- **Agents / integrations:** not affected.
- **Performance:** one extra suffix check when a file opens.
- **Security:** plugin grammars stay data-only under the existing size and time limits. This changes which files they color, not what they can do.
- **UI quality:** no layout change; only token colors.

author: nrb-dev
body:
## Summary

Refs #4355. A cold start of the phone app waited for the account service and the host one step after another. This change removes or overlaps these waits:

- **Server list on the phone.** The encrypted workspace cache keeps the last server list (`~hosts.bin`). At start, the saved servers connect at once. A server connects only when its key is the key that the phone trusts in the keychain. The list of the account service still replaces the copy and removes servers that the account left. Leaving a server removes it from the copy. Sign-out and session expiry delete it. Expected gain: about 2.2 s.
- **Capabilities in the server copy.** The first workspace reads after a start go out with `/compatibility`, as on a reconnect. Old cache files still load (no capabilities); older app versions ignore the field.
- **Early session request.** The first connect of each server asks `POST /v2/remote/sessions/` while the hidden peer page loads. The account service gives the active session again (`startSession`), so the peer asks only for the ticket. A failed early request uses the old path. A failed ticket ends the session, as before.
- **Return hold.** The hold of the other servers after a return to the app ends when the selected server fails, or when Signal reports its host offline.

Not done: a cold-start hold of the other servers. It delays the startup fallback to an online server when the first server is offline (the setup of the reporter), by about 2 to 3 s.

Surfaces: mobile (`apps/mobile`), `packages/team-client` (new `startSession`; `createBootstrap` sends the same requests). PRIVACY.md and the mobile README describe the new copy.

#### Test plan

- [x] Biome on changed files
- [x] Pre-commit typechecks (node, renderer, storybook, api, team-client, mobile)
- [ ] Android cold start: support log time from `Started OpenBot` to `attempt 1 loaded`, before and after
- [ ] iOS cold start with two servers, the first one offline: the app still opens the online server
- [ ] Leave a server, restart the app: the server does not come back
- [ ] Sign out, sign in: no saved server list from before

author: bstoney-yt
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"bstoney-yt"} -->
_Requested by **Brendan**_

## What

She no longer snaps into and out of vehicles. Through an entrance with a door she opens it, climbs in and pulls it shut; getting out she opens it, climbs out and shuts it behind her. The door swings on the vehicle. While this plays she can only look about.

Also in this branch: in a passenger or gunner seat she is drawn in that seat, not the driver's.

## How the original does it (360 code)

- Steps: 0x8229F440 starts with `EnterVehicleOpenDoor` when the entrance's door is there and within 30° of shut (0x8229DD28: cos ≥ 0.866), else `EnterVehicle`. 0x822A5990 moves on at each clip's `Complete`: open door → `EnterVehicle` → `EnterVehicleCloseDoor` if the door stands open (cos ≤ 0.95, 0x822A0958). Exit (0x822A2298): `ExitVehicleOpenDoor` → `ExitVehicle` → `ExitVehicleCloseDoor`, else `ExitVehicle` alone.
- The door is opened and shut by her clips' `opendoor`/`closedoor` events (0x82420208), not by a vehicle clip.
- Door swing (0x824182E8 tick, 0x82418480 pose): even rate, `OpenAngle` over `TimeToOpen`, back over `TimeToClose`, about `AxisOfRotation` in the node's own frame. Field names from the `Door` reflection registration 0x823ECA18. Defaults: axis (0,1,0), 60°, 1.5 s.
- Exit clips play from the exit entrance (0x822A2298 places her there); entry clips from the seat.

## Code

- `m2_engine::vehicle_door`: `Door` records, `Swing`, `Step` chain. `EntranceParams.door` (`DoorName`), `VehicleSeats.doors`, `VehicleSpec::swing_doors`.
- `m2-alpha`: `boarding` (state, a 1 s fallback when no clip plays), `Hijacks::board` plays the steps and doors, `get_out_at`. `--drive --board --seated` takes pictures every 0.25 s.

## Measured (Valiant, `--board --seated`)

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Getting in | instant | 2.08 s: open door 0.50, in 1.03, shut 0.53 |
| Getting out | instant, at the hardpoint | 2.25 s, standing at local (1.72, −0.52), by the door |
| Driver's door | never moves | opens to −60° in 0.26 s, shuts in 0.20 s (front right +60°) |
| First entry frame vs. entrance hardpoint | n/a | 0.08 m |
| First exit frame vs. seated pose | n/a | 0.01 m |

Tests: assets 243, engine 285, alpha 428 pass. fmt and clippy `-D warnings` are clean.

## Follow-up in this PR (second commit)

- The stance and action table's `Target` column now picks clips by the entrance. That gives the tanks their own hatch clips. When she slides over, it picks by the seat she moves to.
- Slide-over: hero.lua's move from the passenger seat to the driver's, and the seat key, play `SeatToSeatTransfer` at the seat she leaves (0x822A6FF0, then 0x822A7198 on `Complete`). On the Valiant from the passenger door, getting in takes 2.75 s including the 0.37 s slide-over.
- Approach: traced. A normal entry has no glide. 0x8229B580 puts her on the vehicle at once and her first clip starts by the entrance, so the jump of up to 0.6 m to it is the original's own. Only a dive-in glides her, 1.2 s over 0x8229F890 and 0x8229FDE8, and the alpha has no dive-in. The invented 0.25 s glide is removed.
- M1A1: the hatch opens 98° and she climbs in over 3.78 s. Her exit clips leave her on the hull. 0x822A2648 rejects that spot, because 0x8229A8D8 fails a stand on a vehicle all round, and the clear-point search (0x822A13D0, 0x8239F440) then takes the first of eight places that fits. The places are turned from the heading by the table at 0x82DE88B8: the front corners first, then the back corners, the sides, behind and ahead. Each lies at the bounding radius plus 1.5 m (0x82B7C10C) from the box's middle. She now lands at the front-right corner, local (5.2, 5.9).

## Not done or unverified

- Clear-point stand-ins: the bounding radius comes from the box's half-diagonal, "fits" means a clear ray at 1.2 m (not the 360's capsule sweep), and that a turn goes towards +x is inferred.
- Doors whose `Type` is not 0 stay shut.
- The M1A1's hatch is left open after she gets out: its exit-close clip has no `closedoor` event.

## Why
Amazon PTD live research for K-Way showed exact categories: `TOTE_BAG` for Nahel shopper, `DUFFEL_BAG` for Sirius duffel, `WAIST_PACK` for Ferimy waist pack. Existing K-Way pilot/generic EAN preview allowlists only `HANDBAG` or `STORAGE_BAG`, causing false category blocks.

## Changes
- Extend strictly validated PTD type enums in `mare-business-capabilities.ts` for the K-Way live canary and **validation-only** generic EAN capability.
- Extend category validation in both generic preview and K-Way pilot, and preview attribute key allowlist for `item_length_width_height`/`compartment` (no new fabricated values).
- Add mock regression tests for all three types covering preview, bounded zero-quantity submission, and unchanged offer price.

## Safety
- Do not publish any SKU with invalid PTD preview; missing origin, manufacturer, materials, product information, GPSR remain missing, never estimated.
- Live seller status and exact EAN no-match gates stay in effect, other marketplaces must be VERIFIED_ABSENT. Existing SKUs, prices, stock and Channable remain untouched.
- This PR enables correct product type selection, **not** a bulk ASIN creation or evidence completion. No Amazon live mutation performed by this PR.

The fallback still honors pause/manual/HOLD, pending or required approvals, process and human-input guards, and never creates a default approval. The new detector_fallback guard is added only to the v1.9 schema roots; published older roots remain frozen.

author: prop
body:
Fixes the two symptoms reported in chat: non-ASCII titles garbled in the player window, and legacy Cyrillic tags needing CP1251/KOI8-R → UTF-8 recovery.

## Diagnosis

**Why text garbles.** Song text enters the DB via `lofty` in `crates/navinamp-library/src/scanner.rs`. Russian MP3s commonly carry ID3v1 or ISO-8859-1-declared ID3v2 frames whose bytes are actually **CP1251** (or KOI8-R). Readers follow the declared Latin-1 encoding, mapping those bytes 1:1 into U+00xx: `Ïåñíÿ î ëþáâè` instead of `Песня о любви`. Every view inherited the mojibake (library, playlist editor, player ticker, OS Now Playing).

**Why the player window looked worst.** Classic `.wsz` skins render the ticker from the skin's bitmap font (`text.bmp`): ~70 cells — a–z, digits, punctuation, `Å Ö Ä`. There are **no Cyrillic glyphs**, and the renderer skipped unmappable chars, so even correct UTF-8 would render as blanks there.

## Changes

### `text.rs` — charset repair (new, +tests)
`repair_tag_text(&str) -> Cow<str>`:
- only Latin-1-mapped text is considered (all chars ≤ U+00FF); proper Unicode and ASCII pass through — the repair is idempotent
- high bytes must be ≥25% of the text's **letters**, which keeps `Motörhead`/`Björk` safe while still repairing the common `DJ … feat. <Russian title>` shape
- candidates: strict **UTF-8** re-decode (fixes UTF-8-bytes-as-Latin-1, `ÐœÐ¾ÑÐºÐ²Ð°` → `Москва`), then **windows-1251** and **KOI8-R** (`encoding_rs`); unigram frequency picks between the codepages, with a small floor for degenerate decodes
- `plausible()` requires **script purity per word** — a token may be Latin or Cyrillic, never both — which rejects accented-Latin false positives (`Été à Zürich`, `Hüsker Dü`) while allowing mixed-language titles
- unit tests: CP1251, KOI8-R, double-encoded UTF-8, long ASCII prefixes, short single-letter words (`Я`, `Ёж`), accented Latin names, proper Unicode, empty, idempotence
- **Known limitation** (documented in the module): text made entirely of accented letters that decodes cleanly under both legacy codepages (`ÄÖÜ …`) is byte-level ambiguous without a language model.

### Scanner — repair at read time
`read_track` repairs title / artist / album_artist / album / genre **before** `album_key` is derived, so new and changed files store UTF-8.

### Schema — one-shot heal for existing libraries
Incremental rescans skip unchanged mtime/size files, so a scan-time fix alone would never heal existing rows. `init` now runs a marker-guarded (`meta.text_charset_repair_v1`) pass over **local** rows: repair the five fields, recompute `album_key`, `UPDATE` changed rows (the existing FTS trigger keeps search in sync), log the repaired count. Runs once per database; remote/Navidrome rows are excluded (server-supplied UTF-8, different trust boundary). Migration test heals `artist ≠ album` with an empty `album_artist` and pins the key to the fresh-scan derivation.

### `SkinText.svelte` — glyph-coverage fallback
If the bitmap font cannot represent the ticker text (any non-space char without a cell, after fold/aliases), that object renders through the existing **HTML text path** (system font, so Cyrillic renders) instead of a canvas with blanks. Coverage for `numbers.bmp` is checked against the *drawn* digits (the classic time strips the colon), so the time/bitrate readouts stay on glyphs.

**Mixed render paths are expected** (review note): the fallback is per object/string, so a Cyrillic title uses the HTML marquee (Verdana, smooth `SCROLL_PX_S` scroll) while an ASCII title in the same classic skin keeps the bitmap marquee (`TICKER_STEP_MS` chunky steps); time and readouts stay on bitmap glyphs. Kept deliberately — forcing the whole ticker to HTML whenever any track is non-ASCII would regress the classic look for the common case.

## Verification

- [x] `cargo test --workspace` — all suites, including new repair + migration tests
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `npm run build`
- [ ] Manual (desktop): scan an album with CP1251-tagged MP3s → library table, playlist editor and player ticker show Cyrillic; UTF-8-as-Latin-1 files too; existing library heals without a rescan on first launch

author: vivmuk
body: ## Why Every web chat minted a new `chat_id`, so Supermemory search always hit an empty `chat-` namespace. Those empty searches are what the dashboard flags. ## What - The chat page stores one visitor id in `localStorage` (`crypto.randomUUID`, or random hex) and sends `visitor_id` on every `/api/chat` turn. After an engagement writes memory it also sends `has_history: true`. - Visitor ids use the same sanitizer as chat ids. A value that sanitizes to empty (`../`, unicode-only, and similar) is ignored. Long values are truncated to 40 characters. Path characters never reach the namespace. - The memory namespace is `visitor-` when a visitor id is present, otherwise the existing `chat-` namespace. A visitor document uses `customId` `visitor--` and `containerTag` set to that namespace, so engagements accumulate instead of overwriting one document. - Recall makes no search request unless this process has already written that namespace, or the client sent `has_history` for a visitor namespace. There is no shared namespace. - `/v1` and MCP still scope by chat id. They pick up the empty-search skip because it lives in `recall()`. ## Tests `python3 -m pytest tests`: **163 passed, 1 skipped**. The skip is pre-existing (`tests/test_agents.py` cannot import `openai`). Supermemory, Venice, and Exa are stubbed. This change does not call the real Supermemory API.

author: gigurra
body:
## Background / Purpose

Live page 3/7 (awb tcl-fcb93a, epic tcl-qo90av "Collab: live page"). Tickets 1 and 2 (#3735 stage listener, #3738 page sources) built the daemon side that serves a page on its own sandboxed origin from an agent's port or worktree files. This PR is the agent-facing core on top of it: the commands an agent uses to show a page to the operator, and the daemon state behind them. The dashboard's Page tab (ticket 4) consumes the snapshot field added here. Drawing, live patches and remote come in later tickets, so this PR has no UI yet.

Steward's requirements for this ticket:
1. A dev server bound only to `::1` is refused, with a hint to start it with `--host 127.0.0.1`. The host proof is IPv4-only by design.
2. Re-showing the same `--name` with a different source kind (port vs static) mints a new origin (new stage page and token). It never swaps the upstream on the same token, so page JS that read static content cannot post it to an origin that now reaches the agent's port.
3. The mount-view gap is tracked as **tcl-kxiqqd**: static sources read through the daemon's view of the filesystem, not the sandbox's deny overlays. It is documented as a known limit and must be resolved before the read-back tickets (5/6).
4. `Origin: null` is admitted by the stage, so the 128-bit token is the real gate. Page tokens go **only to the local dashboard**. That is tighter than "the owning agent and the dashboard": the security review showed that an owner holding its token can curl its own page and read files through the daemon's view (the tcl-kxiqqd gap). So agents see the origin with the token masked (`f-<token>.ui.localhost:PORT`) and act on pages by name. This also keeps the token out of transcripts and clones. It is stated in the docs, the skill and the CLI rules.

## What changed

**Daemon (`pkg/claude/agentd/pages.go`)**
- `POST /v1/pages {target, title?, name?}` shows a page, or updates the caller's page of that name in place. `GET /v1/pages` lists the caller's pages. `DELETE /v1/pages/{name}` closes one. All three are behind `collabRoute` (404 `collab_disabled` with Collab off) and `self.page`, and refuse a human caller (a page belongs to an agent).
- **Own pages only, by construction.** Pages are keyed by (owner agent ID, name), and every route resolves the name within the caller's own pages. Another agent's page cannot be addressed at all, so the same name is just a separate page.
- **Target validation before any dial.** Accepted forms: `:PORT[/path]`, `http://localhost|127.0.0.1:PORT/path`, or a directory or `.html` file. Refused: host names and IPs, `::1` (with the IPv4 hint), `https:`, userinfo, a missing or out-of-range port, the daemon's own ports, and non-plain paths (`//x`, `\`, `#`, controls). A port is then proved once at show time through the existing `dialTarget`: ownership, or the sandbox netns. Nothing listening, or someone else's listener, is refused with the reason plus the IPv4 hint. Static targets must sit inside the agent's **startup directory** (the launch's). The hook-reported edit dir is never used, because the agent steers it with any path it touches. The stage source then re-walks the path with no-follow, dot-name and hardlink rules.
- **Same kind keeps the origin; another kind gets a new one.** A re-show of the same kind calls `setUpstream` plus `notifyReload` on the same token. A kind change closes the old stage page and opens a new token. The public page id stays the same, so the dashboard keeps one tab.
- **Lifecycle.** Retirement closes the agent's pages (hooked in `retireAgentConvWithTransition`), and so does deletion (all three delete paths, before the purge). Pages belong to the agent ID, so they survive reincarnation; only the agent's current conversation can act on them. The operator's close, `DELETE /api/pages/{id}`, queues an operator-authored inbox message `[page <name>] closed`. It quotes no agent-written text.
- **Dashboard event.** The snapshot carries `live_pages` (Collab on, local only), each with a `rev` that increases on every show or update. It is the "page shown/updated" signal for ticket 4. It is classified `denied` in `peer_snapshot_fields.go` and also skipped for unrestricted peers (`isPeerSnapshot`), so tokens never reach any peer. The new dashboard route is listed in `peer_view_routes.go`. Audit rows: `page.show` and `page.close`.
- **In-memory state (a decision).** The ticket says "storage". I kept it in the daemon's memory rather than SQLite. A page is a live origin whose token admits the frame, so keeping tokens off disk means a restart (or close) ends every origin for good. The upstreams can't outlive the daemon anyway. Limits: 8 pages per agent, 64 per daemon.

**Permission:** `self.page` is registered and default-granted with the other `self.*` slugs (`tclaude setup` list), and appears in completion, the countable sudo slugs and the docs.

**CLI (`pkg/claude/agent/page.go`):** `tclaude agent show <target> [--title] [--name] [--json]`, which is short for `tclaude agent page show`, plus `page ls` and `page close <name>`. They are hidden while Collab is off. File targets are made absolute against the caller's cwd. The output prints the source, worktree, origin and rules. Without `--name`, the name comes from the target (`:5173` → `port-5173`, `site/` → `site`, `mock.html` → `mock`).

**MCP: deliberately not added.** The ticket lists MCP, but `tclaude mcp serve` serves only external stewards. An external steward has a synthetic conversation, with no pane and no startup directory, so no page target could ever resolve for it. Advertised tools that always fail would mislead the operator's Config page. I'll add them when a principal that MCP serves has a source.

**Docs and skill:** `docs/live-page.md` (new "Showing a page" section, the token-as-key statement, the mount-view known limit), and `docs/permissions-and-audit.md`. There is a new bundled skill, `agent-page`.

## Tests

Flow tests through the daemon mux (`pages_flow_test.go`), with real loopback dev servers and real stage requests through the dashboard listener:
- show a port page, then update it in place (same id and origin, new upstream served, snapshot rev increases)
- show a static dir and a worktree-relative HTML file; a kind change mints a new origin and the old one returns 404
- `ls`, and close (the token stops admitting; a second close is 404)
- another agent's page: not listed, close is 404, and the same name is a separate page with the owner's page untouched
- slug required (403 naming `self.page`); a human caller is refused
- Collab off: all three routes return 404 `collab_disabled`, and the stage serves nothing
- retire closes only the retiree's pages
- operator close mails the agent, without quoting the agent-written title
- delete closes the agent's pages
- an unrestricted peer's snapshot has no `live_pages` and no token
- a static target in the hook-reported edit dir (outside the startup dir) is refused
- show and ls answers never contain a page token (checked in every show and ls)
- target validation table: host and IP, `::1` hint, https, credentials, missing port, bad ports and paths, outside the worktree, dot-dir, non-HTML file, nothing listening (hint), a foreign listener (refused and never hit), the daemon's port

Locally: `scripts/test.sh ./pkg/claude/agentd/ -run 'TestPage|TestStage|PeerSnapshot|PeerView|Route|Audit|Permission|Sudo'`, plus `./pkg/claude/agent/`, `./pkg/claude/mcpserve/` and `./pkg/claude/setup/`. All pass, except `TestHostRouteLinuxHelperDiscovery`, which fails only in my sandbox (unix-socket path too long in its TMPDIR) and is unrelated.

Not exercised: a real browser (no UI in this PR yet), the netns path end to end (covered by the #3740 CI job for the dial itself), and macOS.

## Reviews

Both by fresh in-harness Claude Code subagents (Agent tool), given only the diff and Background / Purpose.

- **Cold review: done.** Findings:
  1. The MCP tools broke two external-steward tests and can ne

author: untergas
body:
<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
# Review: `wise.py` Data Integrity Risks

## Summary

This PR adds a review-only document, `docs/reviews/wise-py-integrity.md`, that records data-integrity findings in `scripts/wise.py` and requests follow-up changes. No implementation changes, fixes, or new tests are included — the PR is documentation of a review.

The review is based on current `main` (`2f4a9b8`); reproductions were run against an earlier local checkout (`c0ae4a0`), and the relevant implementations were confirmed unchanged in current `main`. The document explicitly scopes out other changes in `main`, such as learner quotation handling.

## Findings documented

The document lists six findings, each with location, requested change, a hint, and acceptance evidence:

1. **High — Overlapping writers can silently lose records.** `Graph.save` replaces both files from a full snapshot with no lock or stale-state check, so two instances loaded before either save can overwrite each other's additions. Requests protecting the full read/modify/write operation or rejecting saves from changed snapshots, with explicit failure instead of silent data loss.
2. **High — Equal merge stamps discard one version arbitrarily.** The merge ordering key (calendar date plus revision counter) can collide for divergent records, and the loader keeps whichever line appears last; the selected record changed when duplicate lines were reversed. Requests detecting and surfacing divergent versions with equal keys, retaining evidence until resolved, and documenting policy for divergent edits with unequal counters.
3. **High — Forced concept addition can replace an occupied ID.** `--force` bypasses similarity detection, including an exact existing concept ID, so an existing concept (with its notes) can be replaced while edges remain attached. Requests rejecting exact concept ID collisions even when forcing, requiring an explicit update or a different ID.
4. **Medium — A symlinked graph directory bypasses file checks.** `Graph.__init__` rejects symlinked `nodes.jsonl` and `edges.jsonl` but not a symlinked `graph/` directory, allowing writes outside the selected state. Requests enforcing the no-symlink boundary for the directory and new persistence files, on both read and write paths.
5. **Medium — Accepted values can crash later commands.** A question with `box=0` is accepted but raises `KeyError: 0` when answered partially; validation also calls `coerce` without retaining its result, so editor-provided strings can pass list-field checks and metadata skips validation. Requests validating domain ranges and stored JSON types, with actionable errors and backward compatibility for legitimate historical records.
6. **Medium — Two file replacements do not form one graph transaction.** Nodes and edges are replaced atomically but independently, so an interruption between them can leave mismatched graph generations (for example, dangling edges). Requests recoverable commit semantics for the graph as a whole, with recovery behavior defined before choosing a mechanism. Noted as following from the sequential replacements; crash injection has not been run.

## Validation context

The document reports a local baseline run of 164 tests (162 passed, two failed: `test_no_git_folder_never_resets_parent_notes` and `test_no_git_project_ignores_parent_folder_notes`), attributed to a Git repository at `/tmp` conflicting with those fixtures' assumptions, and noted as results for `c0ae4a0` rather than a full run of current `main`. Focused reproductions confirmed stale-snapshot overwrite, equal-stamp line-order dependence, forced concept replacement, graph-directory symlink writes, and the invalid-box traceback.

## Scope

This PR contains no fixes and no new test implementations. It only documents the findings and the requested changes.
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

author: zcserei
body:
Fixes DEV-656.

NumberField, TagsInput and MultiSelect validate on a control without a `name`, so Form showed their required and range errors in FormError. The validating control now carries `data-form-name`, and Form uses it when `name` is empty: to file native errors, to focus the control and to clear the error on change. FormData is unchanged.

Typing in one of these fields now clears only that field's error, not the form-level error.

Tests: a new Form browser test covers a required NumberField, an out-of-range NumberField, a required TagsInput and a required MultiSelect. It fails without the fix.

Title: NR-621248: add NGEP DEPLOYMENT_WATCHPOINT entity type

### Relevant information

Registers the NGEP entity type `DEPLOYMENT_WATCHPOINT`, which holds the state of a deployment watchpoint session: the Change Tracking event that triggered it, the GitHub change, the scheduled checkpoint evaluations, the GitHub issue raised on a detected degradation, and the Slack notification target.

author: fredgibbs
body:
Production has not refreshed since Oct 27. Every 10:05 run since Oct 28 ends `mrgather fetch ❌ no file from today for: aa`, and the transform is skipped.

## Why

- The cron runs `update-data.sh -s 202680 -e 202710` with no report list, so the script asked for all five reports: `desr deg as cl aa`.
- Production mrgather (image built 2026-04-10) fetches only the first four. It accepts `aa`, never attempts it, and reports "8 of 8 successful". The applicants table hasn't been refreshed since June 19.
- That went unseen until the I33 fix on Oct 24, which fails a requested report with no file from today. Since then the four reports that download are parsed and then discarded.

## Change

- The default is `desr deg as cl`. The applicants report runs only when it's named: `update-data.sh -s 202680 desr deg as cl aa`.
- ISSUES.md I43 records the evidence, a reproduction, and what remains: mrgather should fetch `aa` or refuse it; one missing report shouldn't skip the tables of the others; skipped steps shouldn't show ✅.

Nothing here is model source, so the deploy rebuilds no bundle.

## Checks

- `testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-data-update-pipeline.R")` passes. A new test pins the default, and it fails with `aa` put back.
- `bash -n scripts/update-data.sh` passes.

Tomorrow's 10:05 cron will pick this up once it's deployed. Until then, a manual run with the four reports named would refresh production today.

author: taktran
body:
`build:package` and `build:umd` only defined `sourcemap: false` for the `staging` and `production` configurations. Nx falls back to a target's default options when it lacks the requested configuration, so `nx build ag-charts-website -c archive` rebuilt the libraries and packed tarballs with sourcemaps enabled. The bundles kept their `//# sourceMappingURL=` comments, even though `.npmignore` drops the `.map` files.

This adds an `archive` configuration with `sourcemap: false` to both targets, matching `production`.

author: paul80nd
body:
## Summary

The fixture check for a kept folder Windows could not seal now passes on Windows. The fault was in the test, not in `regrade.mjs`.

```diff
 test.sh, the unsealed-folder check
   node writes regrade-in.json, its tracePath under $kept     # Git Bash hands node C:/..., so the JSON holds C:/...
-  sed "s|$kept/trace|$unsealed/trace|"                        # matches /tmp/..., so it misses on Windows
+  node -e: set tracePath to "$unsealed/trace/trace.jsonl"     # gets the path in the form node writes
   regrade.mjs reads <unsealed>/home/cwd
```

On Windows the trace stayed on the sealed fixture, which has no `notes.md`, so the grader failed.

## Evidence

- **Before:** on the adopting corpus's laptop, under Git Bash, `sh trials/plugin/fixture/test.sh` printed `FAIL regrade.mjs does not read the workspace of a kept folder Windows could not seal`. The other 46 checks passed.
- **Reproduced on macOS:** with the `sed` pattern changed so it cannot match, the same two lines came out: the `FAIL`, then `regraded 1 case(s): 0 unchanged verdict(s) agree with the tool, 0 disagree; 1 grader definition(s) are new or changed`.
- **After:** on macOS, `sh trials/plugin/fixture/test.sh` prints `every case passed`, and `shellcheck trials/plugin/fixture/test.sh` reports nothing.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** trial-only

Only the fixture changes. `regrade.mjs` and every script the full pass runs are untouched, so the units under way on the laptop are unaffected.

Not done: the fix has not been run on Windows. The laptop is running #898's units, and the fork picks this up at its next sync. No changelog entry or version move, because nothing under `tooling/` or `examples/` changed.

Refs #898

author: amstelwest-lgtm
body: ## Summary An accountant can prepare an IRP6 for an individual / sole practitioner from Work → Tax. Prepare individual IRP6 maps the latest cited tax pack (the same intake as ITR12: IRP5, IT3(b), medical, retirement annuity, travel, practice income and expenses) plus the prior assessment (basic amount), PAYE already withheld, and payments already made. Each figure cites a file id, a full year of books, or a figure the accountant types. A blank is not zero. The draft is `form_code` **IRP6** with `subject` **individual**. Company IRP6 stays `subject` null. That is the Phase 0 unique key, so the two returns do not overwrite each other. The sheet has the same five sections as company IRP6 (taxpayer, estimate, adjustments, credits, result) and periods 1, 2, and 3. Only the accountant can approve a section. The owner cannot. Unresolved queries and missing required sources block Approve. Download is a PDF and CSV capture sheet labelled “Not a SARS return”, for the accountant only. It is not emailed to the client. The gallery shows a second IRP6 face, “Provisional tax return (individual)”, as Ready to prepare. Company IRP6 stays Ready to prepare. ## Form code No new catalog code, and no SQL. `tax_form_catalog` already allows `IRP6`. The foreign key checks the code only. The individual return is a second schema on that code (`taxFormSchema("IRP6", "individual")`), stored with `subject = 'individual'`. Gallery status is the app registry (`galleryId` `IRP6-individual`, status `ready`). The catalog row stays `IRP6` / company / ready. CoS does not need to apply SQL for this PR. ## What the sheet computes - Worked taxable income: employment + practice income + local interest − practice expenses − travel. Medical scheme contributions and retirement annuity contributions are shown and are not subtracted. - Tax on that estimate (or an accountant override) from the signed-off individual rate table for the year of assessment, less the primary rebate. Age 65 adds the secondary rebate. Age 75 adds the secondary and tertiary rebates. If age is not supplied, only the primary rebate is taken off. - Period 1 is half that tax. Periods 2 and 3 are the full-year tax. PAYE already withheld, and payments already made on periods 2 and 3, come off. `rules_year` on the draft is that year of assessment. - The 80% comparison: the estimate as a percent of the worked figure, and 80% of the worked figure in rands. Tables on the sheet, from SARS “Rates of Tax for Individuals” (read 3 November 2026): 2027 as published for 1 March 2026 – 28 February 2027; 2024, 2025, and 2026 share the 2024 brackets (2025 and 2026 are recorded there as no change) and the rebates published for each of those years; 2023 is the previous published table. ## What the sheet does not compute - A rand penalty or interest. - The medical tax credit, or the retirement-annuity cap. - Tax for a year of assessment that has no signed-off table (left blank, and Approve of the result stays blocked). - A partial year of books annualised into practice income. Only a full year already inside the year of assessment is read. - SARS or CIPC login or submit, a ledger write, or a US form. ## Other side? - [ ] Both sides updated - [x] One side does not apply. Add the line below and write the reason after the em dash: Other side: N/A — individual IRP6 is the accountant capture sheet on Work → Tax and the Tax Specialist gallery. The owner home stays the tax card. An owner who opens the shared team pane cannot approve a section or download. No owner-door or owner-home markup change. ## Test plan - [x] `pnpm test:tax-irp6-individual` — 2027 known answer on R555,000 (R116,707.00, period 1 half, PAYE and payments off), 2024–2026 threshold tax nil, 2028 tax left blank, uncited amounts dropped, 80% comparison with no penalty, books full-year practice income, queries and the owner block Approve, CSV and PDF say “Not a SARS return” and cite a file id - [x] `pnpm test:tax-irp6` - [x] `pnpm test:tax-irp6-pdf` — company snapshot unchanged - [x] `pnpm test:tax-form-pipeline` - [x] `pnpm test:tax-itr12` - [x] `pnpm test:tax-specialist-agent` - [x] `pnpm test:tax-specialist-sample` - [x] `pnpm test:tax-deliverable` - [x] `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144 pnpm build:vercel` then `node scripts/za-bundle-leak.mjs` — tax chunk stays off the US path - [ ] `pnpm test:ci` (not run here) Not deployed. No edge redeploy. No migration applied.

author: tj-junhao
body:
Adds value labels, error bars and a connecting line to scatter points.

- `scatter(annotate=True, format=, label_size=, place=)` writes each point's value next to it. `Place.AUTO` tries above, right, below and left, and takes the first position that is clear of marks and other labels. Labels on a fixed side (`ABOVE`, `BELOW`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`) never move. When no position inside the plot is clear and the axis limits are automatic, the limits grow to hold the label. Explicit limits raise `StyleError`.
- `scatter(x_error=(low, high), y_error=(low, high))` draws the series' own error bars in its color, with no palette slot and no legend entry. A NaN end skips one bar.
- `scatter(connect=True)` joins the series' points in input order with a line in the same color. With `by=`, each group is joined separately.
- Adds a `Place` enum, a corpus module `point_labels` in three themes, Rust and Python tests, and skill and README entries.

body:
## Ce face acest PR

Ecranul de bucătărie sună o dată când o comandă încă nepregătită trece de 20 de minute. Ospătarul vede vârsta comenzii colorată, cu aceleași praguri ca în bucătărie.

## Tip

- [x] Funcționalitate nouă (fără schimbări pe server)

## Ce se schimbă

- **`src/lib/orderAge.ts`** e regula unică pentru vârsta comenzii pe ecranele de staff:
  - `ageLevel`: 10 minute = atenție, 20 = întârziată;
  - un pickup programat în viitor e calm, iar după ora promisă vârsta se măsoară de la ea. Sunt aceleași reguli ca `urgencyAnchor` / `isScheduledPickupAhead`.
- **Bucătărie:**
  - o comandă `new` / `confirmed` / `preparing` care trece de 20 de minute sună O dată, cu un ton diferit de „comandă nouă” (440 Hz / 450 ms față de 880 Hz);
  - comenzile deja întârziate la deschiderea ecranului nu sună: cardul lor e deja roșu, iar un reload nu are voie să facă zgomot;
  - verificarea rulează și la 10 s, fiindcă pragul se trece fără niciun eveniment;
  - `takeNewlyLate` ține minte comenzile alertate și le uită pe cele ieșite din bucătărie, ca setul să nu crească la nesfârșit.
- **Ospătar:** vârsta apare în ambră sau roșu, cu textul „întârziată” la 20 de minute, ca semnalul să nu fie doar culoare. Culoarea dispare după „Servit”.

## Testare

- [x] Teste noi:
  - OA1–OA4 (`src/lib/__tests__/orderAge.test.ts`): pragurile, pickup-ul, filtrul de status, o singură alertă per comandă;
  - KA1–KA2 (`src/components/__tests__/kitchenLateAlert.test.tsx`, pagina întreagă cu timere false): tăcere la deschidere, un singur sunet la trecerea pragului, comanda gata nu sună;
  - WA1–WA2 (`WaiterOrderCard.test.tsx`): pragurile pe cardul ospătarului, fără culoare după „Servit”.
- Mutațiile sunt notate în antetul fiecărui test, de pildă:
  - fără baseline → sună la deschidere;
  - fără intervalul de 10 s → pragul nu sună;
  - fără `alerted` → sună la fiecare 10 s;
  - fără filtrul de status → comenzile gata sună.
- Local nu există `node_modules`, deci Vitest și tsc rulează prima oară în CI.

## Risc

- [x] **Low:** doar ecranele de staff, fără migrații.
- Sunetul folosește contextul audio existent (`staffAudio`). Pe o tabletă proaspăt deschisă rămâne mut până la prima atingere, cu bannerul existent „Pornește sunetul”.

## Pentru bridge

- [x] Nu afectează bridge

- [ ] CI a trecut (lint, typecheck, tests, build)

- [x] Documentația actualizată (bullet nou în CLAUDE.md)

author: klucdesire-tech
body:
## Ce que ça change

Les données qui identifient une personne ne partent plus en clair vers l'IA.

- **Une seule porte vers l'IA :** tous les envois passent par `_llm_call`. Ses sortants sont pseudonymisés : une valeur identifiante devient un jeton `⟦P12⟧`. La réponse est remise en clair au retour : l'utilisateur voit ses données, le fournisseur jamais.
- **Repérage à la lecture de chaque fichier** (`confidentialite.py`), pour toutes les sources : fichier, lien, DHIS2, jeux enregistrés, architecte.
  - Par le nom de la colonne : nom, prénom, téléphone, e-mail, adresse, matricule, numéro de dossier ou de patient, date de naissance.
  - Par le contenu : e-mails, téléphones, noms et prénoms, texte libre qui change à chaque ligne.
- **Le calcul tourne sur les vraies valeurs :** le code écrit par l'IA avec un jeton est remis en clair avant de s'exécuter.
- **Registre par utilisateur :** un résumé d'analyse envoyé plus tard, depuis une autre requête, est protégé aussi.

## Ce qui part encore vers l'IA

Les noms de colonnes, les catégories (district, sexe, tranche d'âge), les nombres, les dates qui n'identifient personne, et les libellés d'indicateurs. Les masquer empêcherait Adifa’ d'analyser.

## Vérifications

- **Fuites mesurées sur les 10 fichiers de démonstration,** sans réseau, sur les vrais parcours (chat avec affichage de lignes, puis synthèse d'analyse). Avant : 25 codes patients et 25 matricules envoyés. Après : 0. Aucun faux positif : dates, périodes, catégories et libellés restent lisibles.
- **Vraie IA sur 120 patients fictifs :** 0 identifiant envoyé en 3 appels. Réponse juste (patient au CD4 le plus bas, son district et son téléphone, 10 patients sous 250), en clair pour l'utilisateur.
- **21 tests :** repérage, 11 pièges à ne pas masquer, aller-retour, isolation entre utilisateurs, 50 000 noms, et chat de bout en bout.
- Suite complète, sans les tests du chat : 902 passent, 51 ignorés. Tests du chat rapide et DSML : 7 passent.

## Limites

- **Le repérage est une règle, pas une garantie.** Il peut manquer un identifiant :
  - un code numérique de moins de 6 chiffres, laissé en clair pour ne pas le confondre avec un effectif ;
  - une colonne de prénoms seuls ;
  - un nom sans mot clé dans une colonne peu variée.
- **La réidentification par recoupement n'est pas traitée :** un âge, un district et un sexe rares peuvent désigner une personne.
- **Les données de santé agrégées partent toujours vers DeepSeek :** effectifs, moyennes, catégories. Pour de vraies données TA-MOH, la règle reste de ne pas utiliser l'IA.
