author: emadshaaban92
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"emadshaaban92"} -->
_Requested by **Emad** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01NvNweHQCNYXbRxuUSFdtfJ?thread=cmsg_01NvNweHQCNYXbRxuUSFdtfJKXxM4a9AXS2dfeyoXHEBvk)_

## What

When a change sets an attribute with an expression (the third kind in `AshQuick.Audit.Row.given/2`), that attribute's `changes` entry now also has `expr`, stored as text:

```elixir
count: %{from: 0, to: 6, expr: "count + 5"}
```

On an unversioned resource `from` is what the actor loaded and can be stale. `count + 5` is true no matter what `from` was. Rebased on #130. It also shows up beside `from_unknown: true` on a bulk update by query.

## Wrapper findings (point 2)

I printed `changeset.atomics` in `after_batch` on Postgres with `Example.Test.FileTally` (`file_objects`; `byte_size` required, `min: 0`):

| change | what `after_batch` sees |
|---|---|
| `byte_size + 1` | `required!(type(type(if byte_size + 1 < 0 do error(Ash.Error.Changes.InvalidChanges, [message: "must be greater than or equal to %{min}", vars: %{min: 0}]) else byte_size + 1 end, Ash.Type.Integer, [min: 0]), Ash.Type.Integer, [min: 0]), %{name: :byte_size, resource: Example.Test.FileTally})` |
| `fragment("length(?)", key)` | the same wrappers around `fragment("length(?)", key)` |
| `key <> ".pdf"` (string) | `if string_trim(key <> ".pdf") == "" do nil else string_trim(key <> ".pdf") end` |

On ETS, a required attribute whose expression can come to nil gets `if is_nil(type(...)) do error(Ash.Error.Changes.Required, ...) else ... end`. With `min`/`max`, `count + 1` turns into a `cond` with a branch per constraint. A `string` with `max_length` folds the empty check into that same `cond`. An expression with no constraints that cannot come to nil (`byte_size + 1` without `min`) arrives clean.

Peeling those layers apart by shape would be fragile, so the expression is kept at an earlier point. `Audit.Change` is the last change, and it now records the expressions in `batch_change/3` and `atomic/3`. At that point the action's changes have run and Ash has filled in `^arg`/`^actor`/`^atomic_ref`, but the required and constraint checks haven't been added yet. Two wrappers are still there and are undone at render time:
- `Ash.Type.String.cast_atomic`'s `if string_trim(x) == "" do nil else string_trim(x) end`. Only the layers that the attribute's `trim?`/`allow_empty?` say Ash added are removed.
- the `type(value, T, constraints)` that `^atomic_ref` adds. It is removed only when `T` and `constraints` exactly match an attribute's own.

If an atomic was set by a change that runs after the audit change, `after_batch`'s copy is used as it stands. The kept copy is removed from the context before the changeset is handed on, because it can hold a secret the same way `atomics` can.

## Secrets

- A sensitive attribute's `expr` is `"**redacted**"`.
- **Ash folds literal-only subexpressions.** `count + (1 + ^arg(:bonus))` with `bonus: 4242` reaches the data layer as `count + 4243`, a value derived from the secret that no equality check would catch. So once the action is given a sensitive argument (non-nil, not in `record_sensitive`), **every** literal in its expressions is redacted: `count + **redacted**`. Atoms that aren't booleans, and nil, are kept.
- Otherwise a literal is redacted when it equals a sensitive attribute's value, or is a string that contains one at least 4 characters long. A shorter secret is matched only as a whole literal, so a PIN like `"nt"` doesn't wipe `count + 1`. The values checked are on either side: `changeset.data`, `attributes`, and literal `atomics`. That covers `^atomic_ref(:pin)` and pinned record fields. Example: `name <> "/" <> **redacted**`.
- A `fragment`'s SQL is kept and its value arguments are walked. The fragment renders from `extra.original`, which `Ash.Filter.map/2` doesn't reach, so that is handled separately.
- Backstop: if any secret of 4+ characters still appears in the rendered string, for example inside an `exists` the walk doesn't enter, the whole `expr` becomes `"**redacted**"`.
- The marker renders unquoted, so it doesn't read as a string literal.
- This hides how a value was built, not the value. Known and left as is: a numeric secret of 4+ digits also redacts an expression where its digits happen to appear inside another number (fails safe). On `:sign` (`name <> "/" <> ^atomic_ref(:pin)`), `name.to` still holds the PIN, because redaction works per attribute. The docs say so.

## Scope

The three-way split in `Row.given/2` now goes through one `kind/3`, shared by `given/2` and `changes`. Inputs and update defaults that Ash turned into expressions don't get an `expr`, and neither does a versioned resource's counter. Since #130 the lock sets that counter by an expression (`if <written values changed> do version + 1 else version end`) that repeats every other expression the write set, sensitive ones included. It runs after `Audit.Change`, so it's treated like an update default: no `expr`, and read off the record into `attributes`.

## Rendering

The text is `inspect(expr, limit: :infinity, printable_limit: :infinity)` with Ash's forced line breaks collapsed. Ash prints `left op right` without parentheses, so every operand that is itself an operator gets wrapped: `(count + 1) * 2` would otherwise read `count + 1 * 2`. That also shows `<>`'s right associativity, as in `name <> ("/" <> **redacted**)`. A 120-character pinned string comes out whole. Pinned values render as Elixir writes them: `Decimal.new("1.50")`, `~U[2026-11-03 10:00:00Z]`, `~D[...]`, `Money.new(:USD, "12.50")`. The moduledoc says this can change between Ash versions.

## Tests

- Library: 735 passed. Example (Postgres): 494 passed. `mix format` is clean in both. `mix credo` at the root has no issues. `example/` has no credo dependency, so I ran the root credo on the new example files, and it's clean.
- Red-green. I broke each guard on purpose and confirmed these tests fail:
  - redaction walk off → "a sensitive argument in an expression never appears in the entry", "a secret another attribute's expression reads is redacted there too", "a bulk update by query keeps its expression beside an unknown `from`"
  - equality-only redaction (no fold rule) → the sensitive-argument test and the bulk test, which store `count + 4243`
  - scope check off → "an input the type cast to an expression…", "an update default keeps no expression"
  - kept copy unused (render `after_batch`'s atomics) → "an expression reads as written, without the checks Ash wraps it in" (library) and the example's "an expression is recorded as written, beside what it came to"
  - string unwrap off → the as-written test and the `^atomic_ref` test
  - sensitive-attribute check off → "a sensitive expression is redacted, and not recorded as input"
  - `^atomic_ref` type unwrap off → the `^atomic_ref` test
  - backstop off → "a secret where the walk does not reach takes the whole expression with it"
  - versioned counter clause off → "a versioned resource's counter keeps no expression, and is recorded as set"
  - short-secret threshold set back to 1 → "a short secret is not looked for inside other text"
  - grouping off → "an expression keeps its grouping", the `^atomic_ref` test and "an expression Ash has not resolved is walked all the same"
  - line joining off → "an expression renders on one line, whole…"
  - element-wise list walk off → "an expression Ash has not resolved is walked all the same"

## Docs

- `Audit.Change` moduledoc: "Atomic writes" and "Secrets".
- README: a new bullet in the list of things to know, now six.
- CHANGELOG: Unreleased → Features.

`Row.changes/3` became `changes/4`. It's internal, since `Row` is `@moduledoc false`.

author: jerotire
body:
## Description

Adds Dependabot, so new versions of GOV.UK Frontend, the build and test tools, and our GitHub Actions arrive as pull requests that CI tests. This is the start of the automated update cycle: later PRs deploy what merges to NonProd, then release it to Prod.

The page doesn't change: the build is byte-identical to `main`'s.

**Dependabot** (`.github/dependabot.yml`)

- npm is checked daily and GitHub Actions weekly, both at 07:00 London time.
- A version is only proposed once it's 7 days old (`cooldown`). Compromised npm releases are usually pulled within days, and quick follow-up patches have time to settle. Cooldown doesn't apply to security updates, which are now enabled in the repo settings, so those arrive as soon as an advisory is published.
- Commit messages are set up for release-please, which a later PR adds:
  - `fix(deps)` for `govuk-frontend`, which gets released, one PR per version;
  - `chore(deps-dev)` for the build and test tools, grouped into one PR, which doesn't get released;
  - `ci` for GitHub Actions, grouped into one PR.

**`govuk-frontend` is now in `dependencies`**

Everything was in `devDependencies`, since nothing from `node_modules` runs in the browser. But `govuk-frontend`'s CSS, fonts and crest are inlined into the page, so a bump to it changes what users see. Moving it is what gives its bumps the `fix` prefix. It's still 6.6.0 with the same integrity hash; the lockfile only loses its `"dev": true`. Nothing in our build or the shared workflows omits devDependencies, so the move only changes how Dependabot labels its bumps.

**Artefacts on `main` are kept for 30 days**

`nodejs-build` defaults to 3 days, which overrides the repo's 30-day setting. Artefacts built on `main` are now kept for 30 days, the most the org allows. PR builds keep 3 days, as nobody should deploy those.

**README**

A new "Keeping dependencies up to date" section covers the schedule, the cooldown, and which commit types get released. There's also a CI status badge for `main` under the title.

**After merge**

Dependabot only reads its config from `main`, so this can't be checked until it merges. Expect a first batch of PRs at 07:00 the next morning for anything behind, and actions on the following Monday. Config errors show under Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot.

Every Dependabot PR needs two approvals under the org ruleset, like any other PR.

Related issue: N/A

## Before submitting (or marking as "ready for review")

- [x] Does the pull request title follow the [conventional commit](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) specification?
- [x] Have you performed a self-review of the code
- [ ] Have you have added tests that prove the fix or feature is effective and working
- [x] Did you make sure to update any documentation relating to this change?

author: mztechnology97
body:
PR 3 and 4 of the plan to keep shapes and components inside one product. They are combined because one needs the other. The owner's requirement: "Bisogna evitare in tutti i modi conflitti con altri prodotti".

## How a product recognises its pieces
New module `farm/products/shapes.py`.
- **By geometry, per product:** an object in a product's 3MFs is a piece of that product when its fingerprint matches one of the product's own shapes. Objects without a measured mesh are matched by name.
- **Nothing written on shared objects:** the same 3MF can serve several products, each reading it with its own shapes, and a re-saved 3MF keeps its pieces.
- **Ready plates:** a plate is ready for a product when every object is one of its pieces or set aside as "non fa parte".
- **Where it is used:** `plates_for` (the `/farm/products` list and Seller Hub), Cosa stampare, Accoda, dispatch, and the product sheet. On the sheet, confirmed and proposed now mean ready or not ready for that product.
- **Legacy fallbacks:**
  - components without a product (from before the migration) still read `farm_plate_yields.shape_id` and confirmed plates;
  - a shape with no geometry yet falls back to the old link on the object until the first Salva (marked as a shortcut).

## Writes stay inside the product
- **Salva:** puts the piece's geometry on one of the product's shapes.
- **Non fa parte:** takes the geometry off.
- **Shape names:** reused only within the product, and only with the same geometry (#58's rule, now per product).
- **Merges:** shape and component merges only within one product; otherwise 409.
- **Adding a component to a product:** whether through create/update, Aggiungi, set/kit or a colour variant, the component becomes the product's own, together with its shapes. An unowned shape takes the geometries found in the product's 3MFs. A component of another product gets 409.
- **Removing:** Togli and parts removed by an update always retire the component.
- **API:** `GET /shapes` and `GET /components` accept `?project_id`. Components and shapes now report `project_id` (an addition to the contract). `POST /shapes` accepts `project_id`.

## Tests
- **New non-interference test:** `test_nothing_done_on_one_product_changes_another`. The Set di 2 and the Set di 5 use the same 3MF. On one of them the test runs:
  - Salva and Non fa parte;
  - Rimetti, set → kit → set, and renaming a shape;
  - Stessa forma (shape merge), plus a merge into the other product's shape (refused);
  - disable/enable, Togli on every part, a re-saved 3MF with renamed objects, and Rimuovi.

  After each action the other product's sheet, pieces, shapes and components are identical, and `/farm/checks/isolation` ends ok.
- **Updated tests:** the ones that shared components or shapes on purpose now expect 409. The plan fixture uses a colour variant instead of a second product with the same component. "Assemblaggio" with different geometry gets 409 within a product; across products each product gets its own shape.
- **Results:** `pytest -k farm` 150 passed; ruff check (only the 3 old B905); ruff format clean on the new code.

To be installed together with PR 5 (frontend) and followed by `POST /farm/migrations/isolate-products`, after the dry-run report.

body:
## Summary

`init --embed` now pins `.github/workflows/tripcord.yml` at `6a1279565e9e41e9dec163e6bedf07f2647a2c67` (`main@6a12795`). `tripcord-pr.yml` at that commit pins the composite action at `8b33b1b5a69c686b611b43a475da9658fe44614d`, which has the `base` input and the embed check, so a repository that runs the generated workflow compares a pull request with its base. The documented caller examples pin the same workflow files. This repository's own workflows already call that action, so those pins stay. Golden fixtures for TC-CFG-016 are regenerated.

This is the third re-pin (#43 item 27). No tags, releases, or Marketplace changes.

## Release gate

`TRIPCORD_RELEASE_GATE=1` `TestReleaseGatePinnedActionHasEmbedCheck` passes. Both pins reach an action with the `base` input and `internal/embedded`.

`TestReleaseGateHookSubcommand` still fails until hook mode lands. The claude, cursor, and copilot wiring run `tripcord hook`, and this build has no `hook` subcommand.

## Pin contract

- `@main`, `@v1`, `@v1.2.3`, and `@release` in docs or the README are pins. They fail the 40-character sha check. This tree has none of those refs.
- Every `uses` pin of this repository's action or reusable workflow needs a `# main@<short>` comment that is a prefix of the full sha.
- `runningInCI` is captured at package init, before `TestMain` sets `CI=true` and unsets `GITHUB_ACTIONS`. A shallow clone or a directory that is not a git checkout fails the git half of `TestPinsHaveEmbedCheck` only when the process was started with `CI` or `GITHUB_ACTIONS` set. Outside CI those cases skip. A non-shallow CI checkout that is missing the recorded minimum still fails.
- `TestVetAndTestFetchesFullHistory` keeps the `vet and test` job at `fetch-depth: 0`. No other job's fetch depth changed. `e2e perf budget` runs `go test ./cmd/tripcord` with a filter that does not include this test, so its depth-1 checkout does not fail it.

## Tests

- `go test -race ./cmd/tripcord ./internal/embedded ./internal/githubaction`
- `TRIPCORD_RELEASE_GATE=1 go test ./cmd/tripcord -run '^TestReleaseGatePinnedActionHasEmbedCheck$'` (pass)
- `TRIPCORD_RELEASE_GATE=1 go test ./cmd/tripcord -run '^TestReleaseGateHookSubcommand$'` (fail, missing `hook` subcommand)

body:
## What changed

For an agent with a persona, the SessionStart startup contract and the managed protocol block (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md) told Claude Code to hold `gingugu board watch` under `Monitor` all session and re-arm it at every 30 minute expiry. A `Monitor` expiry is itself a model turn on the session's whole context, so a session left open keeps re-arming it with nothing on the board.

Measured from local transcripts: four sessions left open overnight made 173 calls and read 49.6M tokens between midnight and 10:30, up to ~490k context per wake, with an empty board.

Now:
- The contract (`session_start.py.tmpl` and the repo's copy) says board mail arrives with the next prompt and forbids the watcher.
- `rules_protocol.md.tmpl`: `### Board watcher` becomes `### Board mail`, with the same rule. The CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md blocks are refreshed to match.
- `gingugu --help`, plus the `board_watch` and `board_hook` docstrings, no longer point Claude Code at `Monitor`.
- `gingugu board watch` itself is unchanged. Codex's `--exec 'codex queue ...'` sidecar wakes only when a post arrives.

**Upgrading:** run `gingugu init --force` in each repo that has a gingugu SessionStart hook, because each repo keeps its own copy. Then restart open Claude Code sessions.

author: cluelessuk
body:
## What
An allowlist entry can declare the host ports its pods publish: protocol, host port and container port per mapping. Default deny. Nothing enforces it yet; later PRs in this stack do.

## Why
A host port publishes a pod on the node's own address. Today only the chart's admission policy refuses host ports, and the router gets its 443 through namespace exemptions rather than its allowlist entry. This gives the allowlist one default-deny place to grant a host port, so the router, and any operator workload such as a metrics collector, gets its port the same way.

## Why is this the best solution?
- Per workload, not per container: port mappings belong to the pod's sandbox, which all its containers share.
- The node's own service ports (inventory, etcd, Kubernetes API, credential release, join endpoint, kubelet) are refused when the document is parsed. A document that would let a pod answer as the node is never accepted, so no enforcement point has to catch it.
- A grant needs every container's launch pinned, as secrets and egress do. Otherwise the control plane picks what runs behind the port.

## Review focus
- The refused node service ports in `nodeServicePorts`.
- A node reading a served document drops host ports it cannot validate, keeping the entry, so the entry publishes nothing.
- Skim: decoder plumbing and docs.

author: alaskantuna
body:
## Summary

Fixes two small faults on the reply paths, both older than the shared pipeline.

```diff
 /ask failure send
-  interaction.editReply(...)                 # throws InteractionNotReplied before defer, so the user sees nothing
+  deferred || replied ? editReply : reply    # the same form /stats uses, ephemeral
 asksAboutReplies(text)
+  strip <...> tokens first                   # <:replies:123> no longer offers the replies tool
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** a turn failing before `deferReply` sent no error. `<:replies:123>` counted as asking about replies.
  **After:** `sends a pre-defer failure through reply on /ask`, and new `replyIntent` cases for emoji, mentions and a real question, pass. They failed before the fix.
- **Second review:** approved. It traced every `/ask` failure path, and both of its deliberate breakages failed tests.
- **Known limit:** `<...>` stripping also removes bracketed words such as `<replies>`. Those cases are rare, and a miss only withholds an optional tool.
- **Also found, not changed:** `resolveMediaUrl` can throw before the `try` on `/ask`, which sends no reply.

## Merge Danger

author: carlosbonetti
body:
## Summary

`get_workflow_run(id, user=...)` skipped its owner check when the run had no project, so any signed-in user got the run. With a user given, a run without a project is now refused with a 404. Calls without a user behave as before.

## Motivation

Found while surveying duplication for #1021. `get_workflow_run` outer-joins `Project` and checked `user is not None and project is not None and project.user_id != user.id`. A run with `project_id = NULL` (the column is nullable in `lib/models/workflow_run.py`) passed that check for every user. The sibling checks refuse in that case: `_verify_workflow_run_ownership` in `lib/services/feedback_service.py` and `check_file_access` in `lib/services/files/service.py` both inner-join `Project`, so a missing project means no row and a 404.

The only caller that passes `user=` is `cancel_workflow_run_endpoint` (`POST /api/workflow-runs/{id}/cancel`), so the bug let any signed-in user cancel a project-less run.

## What Changed

- `lib/services/workflow_runs/service.py`: when a user is given and the run has no project, raise 404 "Workflow run not found"; otherwise 403 on owner mismatch, as before.
- New `tests/integration/workflow_runs/test_get_workflow_run_owner.py`: owner gets the run, stranger gets 403, a user asking for a project-less run gets 404 (this one failed before the fix with `DID NOT RAISE`), and an internal call with no user still gets a project-less run.

**Why 404 rather than 403:** it matches the siblings. Their inner join turns "no owning project" into "not found", and they only use 403 for a project that exists but belongs to someone else (or to no user).

**Callers checked:**
- `cancel_workflow_run_endpoint`: the one `user=` caller; now refuses project-less runs.
- `get_workflow_run` / `get_workflow_raw_state` routes and the MCP `get_workflow_run` tool (`lib/api/mcp/tools/workflows.py`): call without `user=` and authorize through `get_project_access(str(run.project_id), ...)`. Unchanged.
- `_end_workflow_run` in the same service: no user, still loads project-less runs (and raises its own `ValueError` for them). Unchanged.

**"Project row gone":** not reachable. `workflow_runs.project_id` is `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so deleting a project deletes its runs. The NULL `project_id` case is the one that is tested.

## How It Was Verified

- New integration test failed before the fix and passes after.
- `uv run ruff format .`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run mypy .` (0 errors), `uv run pytest tests/unit` (2697 passed), plus `tests/integration/test_feedback_project_access.py`.

## Open Questions

- These owner-only checks (`get_workflow_run` with `user=`, `_verify_workflow_run_ownership`, `check_file_access`) don't honour admin or share-link access the way `get_project_access` in `lib/services/projects/service.py` does. That means, for example, an admin with write-level access to a shared project can't cancel its runs. Left alone here; worth deciding whether the cancel endpoint should go through `get_project_access(..., required_level=AccessLevel.WRITE)` like the gate-approval endpoint next to it.

## Risks and Mitigations

- A client that cancelled a project-less run as a regular user now gets a 404. No user-facing flow creates runs without a project, so this should affect no one legitimately.

author: bowo-prasetyo
body:
Two changes, both prompted by a real chat with `Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-q4f32_1`.

## 1. Personas correct the user and stay consistent

The model said four times that LLMs have no feelings. Then the user summarized it wrongly ("So, the AI does have the actual emotions too…"), and the model answered **"That's correct! The AI does have the actual emotions…"**. Small models tend to agree with whatever the user says, and only the Precise persona told the model to correct mistakes.

| Persona | Added |
|---|---|
| Friendly, Writer, Coder, Brainstorm | "If the user says something that isn't correct, gently correct it instead of agreeing." · "Stay consistent with what you said earlier in the conversation." |
| Precise | "Stay consistent with what you said earlier in the conversation." It already says "if it is wrong, correct it politely". |
| Custom | Unchanged (the user's own text) |

The prompts stay at 6–7 lines, since small models follow short instructions better. A 1.5B model will still slip sometimes; this makes pushing back the default rather than an exception.

## 2. "A new version of the app is available"

In the same report the toolbar still showed **Docs / Upload**, which #11 removed. The tab was running the version from before the latest deploy.

- **Why the service worker can't catch this:** it only updates when `sw.js` itself changes, and most deploys don't touch it.
- **What the app does instead:** it fingerprints its own files (`index.html`, the `.js` modules, `sw.js`, CSS) when it starts, then checks again **every 30 minutes** and **when the tab comes back into view** (at most every 5 minutes). If anything changed, a bar under the status line says *"A new version of the app is available."* with **Reload** and a dismiss **×**.
- **Reload:** saves the chat on screen first. While a reply is streaming it's disabled ("Reload after this reply").
- **Offline or failed checks** change nothing.
- **The check also refreshes the service worker's saved copies**, because its fetch goes through the network-first handler. So Reload gets the new files even on a slow connection, where the 4-second timeout would otherwise serve the old copy.
- `window.webllmCheckForUpdate()` runs a check right away (used by the tests).

This also prevents a subtler issue: a long-open tab restarting its worker after a deploy, and so mixing old and new code.

## Tests (87 pass, ~58 s)

- **`unit/personas.spec.js`:** built-in prompts stay at 8 lines or fewer, every one has the consistency line and a "correct the user" line, and lookup falls back to the default.
- **`e2e/update.spec.js`:**
  - No banner when nothing changed
  - A "deploy" (a changed `personas.js`) shows the banner, and Reload brings in the new file
  - Dismissing works; offline checks change nothing
  - With the **service worker active**, Reload gets the new version and the saved offline copy is refreshed too
- **Regression checks:** removing the correction line from Friendly → 1 failed; never announcing the update → 3 failed.

## Not tested

How much the new prompt lines actually reduce agreeing on a real 1.5B model. That needs real chats. The CI tests only check that the lines are present.

## The change

`parse_int_list` (and the two helpers that share it) expanded ranges with `list(range())`. A span larger than `sys.maxsize` raises a bare `OverflowError` instead of the `ValueError` already used for unparsable tokens (`'1-'`, `'abc'`). Guard the cardinality and raise `ValueError` with the offending token.

Fixes #725.

## The backstory

I send small Python library fixes when I find an unclaimed report with a clear contract mismatch. This one was sitting open: a documented range string that cannot be returned as a list escaped the parser's error type. Huge single values and small spans at huge endpoints are unchanged.

body:
**Author: Sage** (Claude Code, in-game agent)

David: "we also need to build the Anthropic API version of Dewey this morning." Goldy's brief is req_e673b1425d0f. One commit, `851277fc`, on `main` (9e499a13).

## What it is
An `anthropic` provider, chosen with `ORBITAL_ASSISTANT_PROVIDER=anthropic`, behind the same `AssistantProvider` interface as Claude Code (`provider.server.ts`). The figures gate, redaction and the analytics events don't change; the provider is the only new part.

- **Messages API with streaming** (`@anthropic-ai/sdk` 1.4.0, a new dependency):
  - the model is `claude-sonnet-5-5` unless `ORBITAL_ANTHROPIC_MODEL` says otherwise;
  - effort is `medium`, with adaptive thinking (the model's default);
  - the server-side refusal fallback (`fallbacks: "default"`) is on for the models that take it.
  
  I checked the model ID, the SDK calls and the error classes against the Claude API reference and the installed SDK's own types, not from memory.
- **Our tools and nothing else:** `TOOLS` from `tools/definitions.ts`, with no server tools and no MCP. Each call runs in this process through the tool server's own `callTool`, with this answer's query token, as the fake-lookups provider already does. So a lookup is checked and limited exactly as under Claude Code.
- **The loop:** `tool_use` → `tool_result` until the turn ends. Each assistant turn goes back whole, thinking and fallback blocks included, and all of a turn's results go back in one message.
  - A tool that isn't ours gets an error result and is never run.
  - A tool call cut off at `max_tokens`, or in a declined turn, is never run.
- **Limits:** at most 8 model calls an answer, 2 minutes for the whole answer, and the player's stop aborts the request in flight.
- **The key:** read from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` alone and passed to the client explicitly. That turns off the SDK's other ways of finding credentials (`ant` login profiles on disk among them), so nothing is read from the home folder (David's rule). It's never logged, never in an error, and never sent to the browser.
- **Errors**, each with a fixed message; the API's own text is never passed on:

  | Error | Kind | The panel shows |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 401 or 403 | `signed_out` | offline |
  | No key | `missing` | offline |
  | 429 | `rate_limited` (new) | "unavailable" |
  | 529 | `overloaded` (new) | "unavailable" |
  | A timeout | `timeout` | "took too long" |

- **The panel:** on the API, availability means a key is set; there's no Claude Code probe. The offline message reads "Dewey's terminal is offline on this machine: it needs an Anthropic API key", with the hint "Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the game server's environment, then restart the game." Plot, please check that copy.
- **Alma** follows Dewey onto the API, with no tools (`ORBITAL_ALMA_PROVIDER=claude` keeps her on Claude Code, and `scripted` turns her off; `ORBITAL_ALMA_ANTHROPIC_MODEL` sets her model alone). Her two fixed failure lists gain `unavailable:rate_limited` and `unavailable:overloaded`, appended.
- **Docs:** `docs/dewey-setup.md` gains an "On the Claude API" section.

## Checks
- It typechecks, `format:check` passes, and `src/assistant`, `src/alma` and `src/game` pass 458 of 458.
- **New tests** (`anthropicApi.server.test.ts`), against a stand-in for the API stream:
  - what's sent: our rules, the fenced message, our tools only, effort and fallback;
  - streamed text;
  - the tool loop, with the assistant turn echoed back and the results in one message;
  - an unknown tool, and a tool's own error;
  - no run after `max_tokens` or a refusal;
  - the 8-call cap;
  - each error kind, never in the API's words;
  - no key;
  - the player's stop;
  - the timeout;
  - email redaction;
  - one answer through `ask` and the figures gate, where `{{a1}}` is filled in and the lookup is shown.
- **Alma's engine choice** is pinned in `alma.test.ts`.
- **Not yet run:** a real-model run (it needs a key and the light baton), and Probe's short red-team pass once it runs.
- **One thing I saw and couldn't explain:** in two runs back to back, three to five tests in `tools.test.ts` failed under `--maxWorkers=4`, and I didn't capture the error. In 13 runs since, on this branch and on `main`, all passed, including the same command. This PR doesn't touch `tools/`. I'm noting it in case it comes back.

Reviewers: Audit, and Frank or Chart.

body:
## What changed

- **`web/readers/fcit_stats.py`:** `read_stats` turns Fantacalcio.it's statistics page into one `SeasonStatsPayload`.
  - Each player's ID and club come from his profile link.
  - The reader checks each column it reads by its title, so a column that changes meaning makes the page unreadable rather than misread.
  - The fantamedia, penalties saved and red cards aren't read.
  - `0,0` means no average, and appearances are the rated ones.
  - A bad row is left out with its reason; players come out in ID order.
- **Name resolution (`domains/players/resolve.py`):**
  - an initial no longer stands in for another player's whole name;
  - hyphens split names, so "MILINKOVIC V" finds "Milinkovic-Savic V.";
  - surnames written as two words meet joined ones, so "DEL PRATO E" finds "Delprato".
- **Reading list and source registry:** the statistics page comes first for season figures.
- **Tests:** a synthetic statistics page in `tests/collect_pages.py`, and two optional checks on the owner's saved real pages.

## Why

mvp-roles task 2 (R1.1, R1.2, R1.3, R1.6, R7.2). The saved-page check found a real bug. Once every listed player is known, an outlet's initial paired with another player's whole name: "SKORUPSKI L" matched both Skorupski and Libra. Only 45% of a round page's names resolved, which would have broken lineups for every role. Now 96.6% resolve and none ambiguously. The rest are players outside the official list, whom the statistics page doesn't show.

## How it was checked

- **Tests written first and seen failing:**
  - `tests/unit/roles/test_read_stats.py`: 12 cases;
  - P1 in `tests/property/roles/test_read_stats.py`;
  - `tests/unit/xy/test_resolve.py::test_an_initial_never_stands_for_a_whole_name` and `::test_the_two_sites_spellings_meet`;
  - `tests/unit/test_sources_config.py::test_statistics_page_listed_first`.
- **On the saved real pages:** the statistics page reads all 603 players with no problems, covering 20 clubs, each with a keeper. Reading it takes 0.5 s. The names check fails without the resolver fix and passes with it.
- **`make check`:** 19 of 19 pass; 568 tests; coverage 98.1% of lines and 93.5% of branches.

## Known gaps

- "ANGUISSA A" still can't find "Zambo Anguissa". From the words alone, Zambo could be a first name that contradicts the initial, so he has no outlet views until a player-alias table exists.
- The collector doesn't read the page yet; that's task 3.

## Definition of Done

- [x] Tests first, red then green
- [x] `make check` green
- [x] tasks.md lists the requirement IDs and tests, and is ticked
- [x] Reading list and source registry updated
- [x] Conventional Commits, own branch

body:
Last round of bug fixes drafted together under single PR, enjoy!

Release **0.11.118**. This branch starts from `main` at 1cdc45a and combines #40 and #41, which it replaces. It also takes in #44, #45, #46, #47, #48 and #49, which were merged into it. Every branch was merged as it was, so its history is intact.

| Source | Package | Version |
|---|---|---|
| #40 | LogNextChar | **1.4.0** |
| #41 | Ultimate Mail Mod | **7.0.1-ck13 + 7.0.1-ck14** (needs hub 0.4.34) |
| #44, #47, #48, #49 | zBag | **5.07-ck21** |
| direct, #45, #46 | Global Bank / Chrome extension | **1.6.7 / 1.3.7** |
| aa25dc6 | Kit / hub | **0.11.118 / 0.4.34** |

## LogNextChar 1.4.0

- **Modern login screens.** The server, character, account, character create, settings and dialog screens get a flat dark look in the style of rom weakauras' options window, with Cherry's Bar's icons.
  - **Modern look**, first in the settings panel, switches back to the game's own look at once, without a reload. `modern_ui = false` in `config.lua` does the same. Modern is the default, also when an older `config.lua` has no `modern_ui` line.
  - Character select shows name, classes with levels and zone, or the red delete timer. With Global Bank it also shows a coin beside the gold, Arcane Transmutor charges and the last save date. Lists are only as long as their contents.
  - Server select has cropped 3:2 flags and a character count. The settings panel is at the left edge, the server list at the right edge, and Settings, Back and Exit Game are at the bottom right. The panel and list anchor only to the screen, because the client re-anchors dependents recursively (`CUiLayout::ResetAnchors`) and a loop would never end.
  - Settings use smaller check boxes under group headings.
  - Fixed: Tab between the two boxes of a two-entry dialog. Its script didn't compile.
- **Numbered characters.**
  - The character screen numbers the characters from 1.
  - **Edit character order** adds up/down arrows (or Shift+Up/Down), saved per server.
  - Next and Prev show the number they log into: a big cyan number under the name.
  - CampNext's next, prev and index (`/lnc <number>`) follow these numbers. `ChangeChar(n)` keeps the game's slot (`slot` mode).
- **Prev fix.** The number's `SetTextColor` doesn't exist on a client FontString (its colour is `SetColor`). That stopped `OnLoad`, so Prev did nothing (`Unknown mode: nil`). `OnLoad` now registers its events first and sets each button up on its own.
- **Slow way back after a logout.** The client clears its character list, waits 3 s, reconnects and only then loads the list. CampNext now waits for `UPDATE_CHARACTER_SELECT_LIST` for up to 120 s, then has 15 s to switch. A list without the character it left cancels instead of switching. Steps and failure reasons go to `LOGCHAR_TRAIL` and `LOGCHAR_FAILED`, chat reports a failure once after the next login, and `/lnc probe` lists the steps.
- The account line says `Loginxml 1.4.0` when the game has no account name. Gameforge launcher logins give `TNTLogin`.
- Built in `Interface/loginxml/template/skin.lua` (first in `loginxml.toc`) and 25 TGAs in `Interface/loginxml/media/`, drawn by `tools/build_login_skin.py` plus Cherry's Bar icons.
- Tests: `tests/login_ui.py` runs the real login screen in a stand-in client that offers only the methods the client has, from its `uilua*.cpp` tables. It reports anchor loops and replays the client's way back with the list arriving after 4.5, 14 and 40 s. Also `tests/test_login_look.py` and the slot tests in `tests/test_lognextchar.py`. In-game checks: G35 to G47.

## Ultimate Mail Mod 7.0.1-ck13 and ck14

- **Modern mail window**, opened at the mailbox by default. **Classic mail window** in `/umm`, or `/umm ui classic|modern`, switches at the next mailbox without Reload UI.
- **Load time:** only `Modern/Loader.lua` and `Modern/Modern.xml` (bare frames, 23 KB) load with the game. The rest (about 150 KB of Lua) loads at the first mailbox. A load error falls back to the classic window and is reported once (`/umm x`).
- **Inbox:** Gold / Items / Unread chips, a From switch and search. Tick all sits beside From and Take all beside the search. The bottom row is Delete emptied, Delete, Return. Lists **never read a mail**, because reading cuts a mail to 3 days. Take skips C.O.D. and gold past 999,999,999.
- **Compose:**
  - One name per Send, as many mails as needed: long text goes in numbered parts, and up to 10 items on **+** each get their own mail.
  - The box beside C.O.D. is the gold for the name in To, with two preset buttons. C.O.D. is off at every start and changes only on a click.
  - **Use inbox gold** / **Extra gold mails** take each inbox gold mail just before sending, so 7 gold caps can go to 7 characters in one Send.
  - The subject fills in from the first item or gold amount.
- **Mass send:** a bag grid with rounded slots, click, Ctrl-click, drag-box and name-search marking, and Send / Send safely / Send fast with `/umm` pacing. Categories are 36 one-click boxes with item icons, in two rows under the bag grid (they replace the category list).
- **Activity:** this session's sends, totals and the 20 last-mailed names. Kept in memory only.
- **Settings:** **Mail window scale** (0.70 to 1.50, `/umm scale`; drawn at 1.2× at scale 1), **Open name list by itself** (`/umm namelist`), Recent/History/Use last per server (`UMMConfig.RecentByServer`), and Ctrl+Backspace in every box.
- **Layout fix:** `Modern.xml` frames had no `<Size>`, so the client resized them to their parent. That left the tabs dead after one click and drew bars across the screen.
- **ck13:** recently sent names first in the classic Compose, **Use last** on Mass Send Items, To kept across tabs.
- Packaging: minimum hub **0.4.34**. `LICENSE-ModernWindow.txt` (UMM only) credits the WeakAuras textures (GPL v2), Cherry's Studio Panel Assets (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0) and Fira Sans (OFL 1.1). The combined `LICENSE.txt` is unchanged.
- Tests: `tests/test_umm_modern.py`, `tests/rom_layout.lua` (follows `CUiLayout::SetScale`), plus compose, history and shortcut tests. In-game checks: UM1 to UM27.

## zBag 5.07-ck21

- **Item shop next to bank (zBag)** (`zBag_VAR.bankshopside`): with one bank and bank tab 6 on, slots 201-300 go into their own box on the right of the bank, and the bank search moves under it. *Lock resize* moved to the *Hide default backpack* row.
- **Next to bag (zBag)**: with one bag and *Show equipment slots* on, the 21 equipment slots go into their own box attached to the bag's right side, in two columns while the bag is shorter than 21 rows and one column when taller. The bag then ends after its last row of slots.
- **Stats** tick beside the bag search:
  - A single-stat mana stone shows its stat's short name (*str*, *stam*, *patt*…) in a per-stat colour.
  - A stone with 2 to 6 stats shows *2x* to *6x*.
  - The code is in the new `zBag/zBagKitStats.lua`, listed in the hub manifest.
- Slot numbers follow the font size setting and no longer flash big on mouseover.
- Earlier commits had rewritten `zBag.lua`, `zBagTmpl.xml`, `zBagB.lua` and `zBagB.xml` with LF endings. e08255c and #48 restore their original endings, so the diff shows only the real changes. #48 also rewords five code comments; no code changes.
- Tests: `tests/test_zbag_shop_side.py`, `tests/test_zbag_eq_side.py`, `tests/test_zbag_slot_font.py`, `tests/test_zbag_stat_prefix.py`. In-game checks: Z2 to Z5.

## Global Bank 1.6.7 / extension 1.3.7

- **Character transfer tracking:**
  - A content script on `https://<language>.runesofmagic.gameforge.com/charactertransfer` reads the planned transfers and the characters the form offers. It reads page text only, never account names, e-mail addresses or links, and never clicks or sends anything.
  - Each transfer shows as a plate on the Characters page, `Xfer › server › time registered`. Hovering it counts down to the weekly maintenance (default Thursday 09

Prepared 4 control+candidate decks at 1/2fF with exactly one model-include difference, generator and fail-closed tests, and a dry-run-by-default Python runner reusing no-overwrite RAW/LOG/SHA archiver. **All four new v3_4 decks UNRUN; original v3_3 results and source unchanged.** The model is an engineering timing surrogate, not TI silicon or a safety proof. Must evaluate common 0–220us metrics, pre-fault <=1mV, both full320us, all ten gates.

3. OEM YAGEO/KEMET exact part `A720V477M2R5APE003` (https://yageogroup.com/download/specsheet/A720V477M2R5APE003) lists **H MAX 2.1mm**, vs the repository's 1.9mm distributor nominal. Corrected candidate source and bank JSON, all 15 C100-C114 mechanical records, KiCad provisional footprint descriptive data and full placement-board notes. Original BOM supplier candidate and mechanical Fab remains unverified. Preserved frozen v3 manifest source/JSON SHA256, full tests.

4. Reclassified `cout_bank_path` 0.2688mOhm 2oz/100C independent-lane result as an **illustrative scenario, not a rigorous lower bound** on unrouted shared PCB; corrected scientifically unjustified claim that existing 42.76mVpp ripple must be a lower bound when distributed ESR changes. author: fhyq-dong
body:
## Summary

Adds a `network.bind_host` setting so the HTTP API can listen on `127.0.0.1` only. The default stays `0.0.0.0`, so nothing changes for existing setups.

- **Why a setting, not a flag:** the user service always launches `server start --managed-service`, so a CLI flag would never reach a service-managed server.
- **Why only two values:** local CLI commands, `surge connect`, and the extension all dial `127.0.0.1:<port>`. Binding to any other address (a LAN IP, `::1`) would lock them out, so validation accepts `0.0.0.0` or `127.0.0.1`. An invalid value rolls back to the default with the usual config warning. If local discovery later follows the bind address, the check can be relaxed.

#642 lists a configurable bind address as follow-up work; this is that piece.

```bash
surge config Network.bind_host 127.0.0.1   # then restart Surge
```

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./...`
- [x] New tests: `serverBindHost` default/override, `bindServerListener` binds to the configured host, and `Settings.Validate` keeps `127.0.0.1` and resets an unreachable address.
- [x] Manual, Windows 11: with `bind_host = 127.0.0.1`, `surge server start` listens only on `127.0.0.1`. `/health` answers on loopback and the LAN address refuses the connection. `surge config Network.bind_host 192.168.1.10` is rejected.

author: ismail-benali
body:
## Summary

This Draft PR implements the server-side content-safety gateway and governed-learning foundation for Issue #37. It connects the main React content-writing surfaces to the scan gateway and adds dataset/model lifecycle RPCs. It remains unmerged and is not production-ready.

### Server gateway and database boundary
- Authenticated Edge Function verifies JWT, derives role/account standing server-side, enforces operation/field allowlists, bounded payloads, trusted contexts, exact-origin CORS, and 90-second actor/operation/payload-bound one-time tokens.
- Private SQL draft contains token storage/consumption, text-field guards, SECURITY INVOKER write RPCs, scan audit events, and private learning registries.
- Fixed text projection coverage for `community_attestations.dialect_region` and `role_promotion_requests.dialect_region`, with pgTAP assertions.
- Governance-trigger notifications now receive narrowly scoped internal audit tokens; sender-less system notices remain supported for trusted maintenance paths. There is no general trigger bypass.

### Client write-path integration
- Added `src/lib/contentGateway.ts`: scan first, then call the matching SECURITY INVOKER RPC. There is deliberately no direct-REST fallback.
- Routed new proposals, rapid-review corrections, per-draft synchronization, editorial decisions (including bulk approval), community attestations, profile text changes, promotion requests/decisions, admin governance changes, messages, and moderation reports/resolutions through the gateway.
- Signup no longer copies unscanned profile text into user-editable Auth metadata. When signup has no session, the profile is completed after sign-in through the scanned profile flow.
- Kept only non-content metadata writes direct: message read/ack timestamps and avatar/public-listing metadata. Text projections exclude these fields.
- Added four client gateway contract tests: scan-before-RPC ordering, fail-closed scan errors, review/block decisions, and no direct-write retry after RPC failure. These are adapter tests, not full browser E2E coverage.

### Governed learning lifecycle
- Added service-role-only dataset freezing with exact train/validation/test membership, approved/consented/licensed candidate checks, and cross-split source-group/contributor leakage prevention.
- Dataset fingerprints are computed server-side from source digests and the split manifest.
- Added versioned domain-specific release policies (no default policy is seeded), persisted evaluation runs with policy-versioned release gates, model candidate registration, independent release reviews, activation, and rollback records.
- Linguistic releases require one independent approval; content-safety releases require two distinct approvals. Submitters cannot approve their own model release.


### Validation status
- Latest completed application checks: TypeScript passed, 64 unit tests passed, production build passed.
- Latest completed Edge Function checks: both function type checks and the Edge Function type checks passed.
- CI #387 rebuilt the isolated database successfully but pgTAP failed on a malformed SQL test delimiter and sender-less governance notification handling. Both defects have been corrected on the current HEAD.
- CI #388 is running the corrected isolated database rebuild and pgTAP suite. Do not treat database tests as passed until that run completes.
- No browser-level integration test against a non-production Supabase project has been completed. The connected Supabase account currently exposes one active project and no development branches; a dedicated branch requires explicit cost approval.
- No measured shadow-mode precision/recall/FPR/FNR/latency results exist yet. The database defaults to shadow; a real measurement run requires a reviewed non-production policy and a labelled sample set.

### Explicitly not done
- No SQL migration was applied to any remote database.
- No Edge Function deployed and no secrets configured.
- No Supabase production schema, RLS, data, or auth settings changed.
- No merge, production release, or deployment.
- No dataset is automatically assembled, no model is trained, and no model is auto-promoted. No reviewed release policy is installed by default.

### Required before completion
1. Pass CI #388, including isolated database reset and all pgTAP tests.
2. Obtain approval for a dedicated Supabase development branch, then run browser-level integration coverage for every write surface and direct REST bypass.
3. Review the non-production Darija/Arabizi policy with native-speaking editors; do not activate an unreviewed lexical ruleset.
4. Run shadow mode on consented, labelled examples and report precision/recall/FPR/FNR plus p50/p95 scan latency before any enforcement approval.

See `docs/algorithms/SERVER-GATEWAY-IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md` for implementation boundaries and remaining blockers.

author: wendy926
dargmuesli
body:
Each Docker job builds the image twice, once for the smoke test and once to push, and the second build normally reuses the first one's cache. The Dockerfile seeds skew protection from `ghcr.io/maevsi/vibetype:latest`, which each build resolved again. When a `main` run pushed a new `:latest` in between, the second build started from scratch and took about 10 minutes instead of about 10 seconds. The concurrency group from #2478 prevents this on release branches, but pull request runs are in their own group and were still affected, as #2478's own build showed.

A new job resolves `:latest` to its digest once per run and passes it to both builds as `SKEW_PROTECTION_SOURCE_IMAGE`, so they always share the same source image. The job runs in parallel with the dry release and adds no time to the run. This PR's own CI run checks the case without a release, where the `RELEASE_NAME` line of the build arguments is empty.

_Requested by **Andrei** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_019SRGSmcMjSFXhQQVHqXLi9?thread=cmsg_019SRGSmcMjSFXhQQVHqXLi9A4D4GhqbU6tixcAzDWD2Mp)_

Andrei: "the column of light above the player characters works great but now it is not visible enough with the mountains in the background." He chose brighter on mountains, but measured: "calculate how much of the beam is shown against the mountain background". He also chose to count that share by the beam's light. After trying it in the preview, he asked for the plains too: "Let us start with x1.5 against plains (vs x2.0 against mountains)". The ruling is Q329 in `docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`, items 1 to 3.

## What changed

- **What is behind each beam.** Each beam measures how much of its light stands over each terrain of the map's ground, wherever its figure stands.
  - It samples 5 points across the beam and 24 up it.
  - Each point counts for as much light as the beam gives there, so the bright lower part counts for more than the faint top.
  - Whatever is not over the ground stands off the map.
- **How bright that makes it.**
  - Over mountains: twice as bright.
  - Over plains: 1.5 times as bright.
  - Over forest and off the map: as today.
  - Over mixed ground, each terrain counts for its share, rounded to twentieths.
- **What gets brighter.** Only the beam's light and its white core. The dark edge is unchanged.
- **When it is measured.** Whenever the beam is drawn and sized. A walking figure's beam is out anyway, and it comes back measured where the figure arrived.

Code:
- `PLAYER_BEAM_GROUND`, `groundOf`, `beamOverGround` and `beamStrength` in `apps/web/src/render/sceneModel.ts`, with tests.
- `insidePolygon` in `apps/web/src/render/geometry.ts`.
- In `apps/web/src/render/pixi/renderer.ts`, `beamLight` gives each point's weight and `sizeBeams` measures each beam and redraws it.

## Anything beyond what was asked?

No. The beam's colour, width, height, edge, fade while walking and the rings are as they were. A beam with only forest or the sky behind it looks exactly as today. No rule, number, map or rulebook word changed.

## Checks

- Typecheck is clean.
- All 915 tests pass (10 new).
- Checked in the game: a hero on the mountains now has a beam that shows clearly over the rock, and a hero on the plains at the forest's edge is brighter by its plains share.

Obsidian's plugin review flagged `src/ui/renderBoard.ts:1135`: "This assertion is unnecessary since it does not change the type of the expression." The review checks with TypeScript 6, where an `input` listener's event is already an `InputEvent`. TypeScript 5.9 types it as `Event`, so the cast was needed locally and our lint passed.

- **TypeScript:** `^5.6.0` → `~6.0.3`. Limited to 6.0.x because `typescript-eslint` 8.x supports TypeScript below 6.1 (not 6.1 or the TypeScript 7 rewrite yet). `tsconfig.json` needed no changes.
- **Search box:** `(event as InputEvent).isComposing` → `event.isComposing`.

With this, our lint reports what the review reports. With TypeScript 6 and the cast still in place, `npm run lint` failed on exactly that line.

## Testing

- `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, the shortcut tests, `npm run harness` and `npm run package` all pass with TypeScript 6.0.3.
- The built `main.js` is byte-for-byte the same as the 1.3.0 release, because types are stripped, so nothing users run changes. No version bump or release notes, and no native retest.

The review's CSS warnings (`clip-path`, `display: contents`) are left as they are. Its browser-support data marks both as partial in every Chrome version, for limits that don't apply here: shapes in external SVGs, and buttons or table-like roles. We use `inset(50%)` on screen-reader-only text, and `display: contents` only on plain `div` wrappers.

body:
## 问题与改动

纯度最大不动点仍逐轮重建名字集合并扫描函数体。含非纯叶子的长调用链每轮只降级一层，与声明顺序无关；基线组件从 64 → 128 → 256 函数时，JIT 约 1.95 → 7.67 → 30.59 ms，显示重复扫描成本。

保留小模块和短链扫描。至少 256 个函数、四轮后仍收缩且非空时，先确认后续短尾是否稳定；仍有传播才用本次 Compute 专属的反向调用图。按函数体记录有效状态，按名字计活跃 provider；名字的最后一个 provider 失效时才通知调用者，每个函数体最多失效一次。

复用只读候选集合的稳定哈希槽位作为名字节点，避免重复建索引。图存活期间不修改原表；结果需要移除名字时重建结果表。保留纯递归 SCC（没有非纯来源时）、同名 provider 聚合、重复边、缺失/无体/NoInlining callee 的保守行为；每次 Compute 重算。可投机最小不动点保持原样，不混淆两种递归边界。

## 性能与范围

测量基线 `db2c3cd165951085097460c444dad4786756f5b6`；最终验证 base `3ba8f1738189c6f46aedd8be8d8d565e2be4992b` 仅新增 xtask Git 读取失败回退修复，optimizer 源码未变。Head `a1dfc116a15506edae91a9773f379fd97b17e04c`。

两侧 optimizer 均由同一固定 VM、唯一隔离上游 driver 构建，相同 SDK/字节码，仅目标包不同；独立快照补齐相同的 workspace 依赖声明。程序/driver 目录没有部署依赖遮盖。组件含夹具创建和 Compute：一组预热、六组交替 A/B，每进程两次预热、12 样本。

| 非纯叶子调用链组件 | JIT 前 → 后 (ms) | interp 前 → 后 (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 256 函数 | 29.704 → 1.585 (-94.7%) | 72.705 → 3.449 (-95.3%) |
| 512 函数 | 117.511 → 2.866 (-97.6%) | 287.095 → 6.833 (-97.6%) |

控制覆盖 16/64/128/256 函数：浅扇出、全部局部非纯、全纯、短链旁独立纯函数/纯调用者，以及确认后仍有少量传播的短尾。最终控制最大约 +3.4%（16 函数 JIT 全纯，约 +0.005 ms）；不保证所有微场景更快。

初版重复名字索引导致短尾控制慢约 11%–30%；稳定槽位复用及短尾确认减少该成本。64/128 函数仍有固定图成本，依据控制结果将建图范围限制为至少 256 函数。所有不利原型数据均保留，不混入最终收益。

完整源码编译固定 VM/driver/SDK，仅 optimizer 不同，每次 release/no-incremental/jobs1，一组预热、六组交替配对，同时记录 wall 与子进程 user+sys CPU。所有 zpkg/zsym SHA256 一致；合成非纯程序输出 caught，全纯程序输出 1。

| 工作负载 | JIT wall 前 → 后 (ms) | interp wall 前 → 后 (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 合成 128 函数非纯链（不建图控制） | 898.59 → 897.84 (-0.1%) | 611.51 → 616.38 (+0.8%) |
| 合成 512 函数非纯链 | 1052.50 → 946.06 (-10.1%) | 1010.69 → 733.50 (-27.4%) |
| 合成 512 函数全纯链控制 | 907.38 → 903.00 (-0.5%) | 723.02 → 720.77 (-0.3%) |
| 仓库真实 z42c.semantics 模块 | 2739.89 → 2750.18 (+0.4%) | 3339.98 → 3345.05 (+0.2%) |

CPU 结果与 wall 接近。收益集中在大模块的长非纯依赖传播，真实模块没有明确收益，**不主张通用编译提速**。原始数据、全部不利原型、固定环境哈希见本轮 outputs/compiler-purity-demotion-samples.json 与 compiler-purity-demotion-compile-samples.json。

author: nezhinskiy
body:
## What and why

LiveBridge can now update itself and its Claude Code mod from **Settings > Updates**, the menu bar menu, or a notification. An install starts **only when you click Install**. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-11-02-in-app-update-design.md`. Plan: `docs/plans/2026-11-02-in-app-update.md`. ADR: `docs/adr/0002*`.

- **Settings** shows the running version, a **Check for updates** button, and **Check for updates automatically**. That option is on by default and off for a build from source (`LBSourceBuild`). An automatic check runs at most once a day, and each release is announced only once.
- **Install** (`Updater`, an actor behind an injected `UpdateEnvironment`) runs these steps:
  1. Requires a signed-in `gh`.
  2. Downloads the image from the release's asset host (capped size and timeouts).
  3. Runs `gh attestation verify`, pinned to `getLiveBridge/LiveBridge`, the `release.yml` signer workflow, `refs/tags/vX.Y.Z` and GitHub-hosted runners. The attested digest must equal the image's SHA-256. There is no path that skips this.
  4. Mounts the image read-only and checks the app inside: bundle id, version equal to the release (it refuses a version not newer than the running one), minimum macOS, `codesign --verify --deep --strict` and the CDHash.
  5. Stages the app in `/Applications` and re-checks the CDHash before the swap.
  6. Waits while a voice request is open.
  7. Updates the mod with `claude plugin marketplace update` and `claude plugin update`. It never passes `-y` and never answers a prompt, then checks the result in `plugin list --json`.
  8. Stops the call and waits once more.
  9. Swaps the app atomically (`renamex_np` with `RENAME_SWAP`) and writes `updates/record.json`.
  10. Relaunches: a positional-argument `sh` helper retries `open` until the installed app's executable runs. This works around a LaunchServices -600/-609 race in which `open` can still exit 0.
- **Marketplace:** it now pins the mod to the release tag (`git-subdir`), so the mod you install belongs to the app.
- **Socket:** `UnixHTTPServer` retries the bind while the old instance quits, and its stop removes only its own socket (inode check).
- **Docs:** the README with its six translations, the site, SECURITY.md, the architecture overview, CONTRIBUTING (release steps) and the CHANGELOG are updated. They say only what the code enforces.

Base is `dev` (not `main`), following the agreed flow: PRs go into `dev`, and the release goes to `main` later.

## How it was tested

- **Swift tests:** `swift test` passes 278 tests. New suites: AppVersion, Release, UpdateProblem, UpdatePolicy, UpdateState, UpdateRecord, Updater (fake environment), DownloadRules, UpdateBundleCheck and RelaunchScript (with real `pgrep`/`open` stand-ins), plus the registry and socket changes.
- **`scripts/check.sh`:** every step passes except `node --test app/Tests/AudioJSTests`. On Node 24 that step fails on a directory argument; the separate PR into dev fixes it. With `*.test.mjs` the step passes 10/10.
- **Manual end-to-end run on macOS 27:** a 0.1.1 debug build announced the real v0.1.2 release, then downloaded it, verified the attestation, staged it, updated the mod to 0.1.2, swapped and reopened as 0.1.2. The first two runs found the relaunch race, which the last two commits fix.
- **Reviews:** a spec review plus a security review, per-wave reviews, and a final whole-branch review. The final review found no Critical issues. Its one Important finding, a swap failure after the mod update that went unreported, is fixed in 8041c54.

**Not observable yet:** the "updated" notice and the cleanup of the staged copy after a relaunch. They run in the new version, so they can only be seen once a release that contains the updater exists.

**For reviewers:**
- The new RelaunchScript tests sign a copy of `/bin/sleep` ad hoc at test time, so CI must allow `codesign`.
- Known minors are deferred deliberately, for example an older `gh` reads as a failed attestation (it fails safe), and a failed automatic check still counts as the day's check.

## Checklist

- [x] `scripts/check.sh` passed, except the Node 24 AudioJS step described above, which is fixed separately.
- [x] The docs that describe this behaviour changed in the same pull request.
- [x] No wire change.
- [x] No personal data in code, fixtures, logs or screenshots.

author: bcavnvidia
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> This PR cherry-picks #4746 into `release/v2.0`. It does not apply cleanly, so the conflicts are resolved by hand as described below.

On `v2.0`, `forge-dpu-agent` skips re-rendering HBN unless one of Core's two config versions changes or a hash of a hand-picked set of top-level response fields changes. That hash leaves out `tenant_interfaces`, so a change to an interface's `vpc_prefixes`, `vpc_peer_prefixes` or `vpc_peer_vnis` never reaches a DPU that is already running. Creating a VPC prefix or changing a peering bumps neither version, so DPUs that rendered earlier keep a stale FNN VPC-isolation ACL and drop their hosts' traffic to the new prefix until `forge-dpu-agent` restarts (#8535).

#4746 replaces the hand-picked hash with a fingerprint of the whole response. It removes only the fields that cannot affect HBN rendering and sorts collections whose order does not matter, so any rendered input, including new or nested ones, triggers an apply by default. Only the DPU agent changes.

## Related issues


## Type of Change
- [x] **Fix** - Bug fixes

## Breaking Changes
- [ ] **This PR contains breaking changes**

## Testing
- [x] Unit tests added/updated

## Additional Notes
* The conflicts come from `main_loop.rs` changes on `main` that predate #4746 and are not on `v2.0` (the visibility refactor, IPv6 BGP health, per-interface routing-profile hashing). Each conflicting hunk takes #4746's side.
* `use_admin_network_changed` and `ManagedHostNetworkConfig.loopback_ip_v6` do not exist on `v2.0`, so the line that clears the former, the test case that sets it, and the fixture field for the latter are dropped.
* #4314's IPv6-unicast health test arrived with the conflict context and is dropped, because `v2.0` does not have the function it tests.
* On `v2.0`, the fields the fingerprint excludes are either handled outside the HBN skip (DHCP and NTP, extension services, link health, the pinger type) or not read by the agent at all (`astra_config`, `enable_dhcp`, `deprecated_deny_prefixes`, the instance payload).
* `traffic_intercept_config` still exists on `v2.0`. The fingerprint now covers it in full, where the old hash covered a subset of its fields.

author: yadaniyil
body:
A review of the whole app, with four small fixes and new tests. One commit per fix.

## What was broken, and the fix

**1. A recording could be lost for good.** While a recording was turned into text, it sat in the temporary folder. It only moved to `unsent.m4a` if the work failed with an error. If iOS ended the app halfway, the recording was gone and the app never offered it again. This can happen with a long recording in the background: after the time limit, after a phone call, or after the shortcut's 25 second cap ("The text will be in the app when it is ready"). For example, a 10 minute recording with Parakeet takes about 36 seconds, which is more than iOS gives in the background. Also, the background time had no expiration handler, and Apple's docs say the app is then killed.
- Fix: the recording moves to Application Support before the work starts (`UnsentRecording`). A recording still there at the next launch waits for another try, like a failed one. Background time is now asked for before the microphone stops, and it is ended when it runs out, so iOS suspends the app and doesn't kill it.

**2. Coming back to the app could wipe the user's clipboard.** A result copied in the background is copied again when the app comes to the front, because iOS can ignore the first write. That only checked the age (2 minutes). So: dictate, paste, copy a link in Safari, open Open Dictation, and the link was replaced.
- Fix: it also checks the clipboard's change count, and only copies again if nothing was copied since (`ClipboardRetry`).

**3. The model download could carry on over mobile data.** The first download only starts by itself on Wi-Fi. But once iOS stopped it (as when the user leaves to set up the shortcut), it carried on by itself on any network. What is left can be hundreds of MB.
- Fix: it carries on only on Wi-Fi or the like. Otherwise the "Try again" button stays.

**4. ElevenLabs could put sound tags in the text.** ElevenLabs can write sounds like "(laughter)" or "(footsteps)" into the transcript, and the app never set `tag_audio_events`. ElevenLabs' docs list the field but don't state its default. Two other docs say it is on. Sending `false` is harmless either way.

## Tests added

- `UnsentRecordingTests`: a recording leaves the temporary folder, one left over at launch waits for another try, a newer failure replaces the older one, a retry that fails again keeps it, and the file keeps its old path for existing installs.
- `ClipboardRetryTests`: copy again when fresh and unchanged; never after a newer copy; never when old.
- `FirstModelDownloadTests`: three new tests for carrying on (on Wi-Fi, not on mobile data, not once something else can listen).
- `ElevenLabsTranscriberTests`: the new field is sent.
- `HistoryStoreTests` (new, it had none): order, the limit of 30, a relaunch, removing, clearing, an unreadable file.
- `MultipartFormTests` (new): the exact upload layout, and the sound is sent byte for byte.

## What I ran, and what I could not

There is no Xcode or iOS SDK in this cloud box. So I checked what I could on Linux with Swift 6.3, in a scratch package outside the repo. It copies the Foundation-only files and uses small stand-ins for UIKit, Network, os, ActivityKit, AVFoundation and the two model libraries.
- **96 tests in 18 suites pass**: all the new ones, plus the existing store, model preparation, turn-taking, OpenAI and ElevenLabs network, rewriter, archive and token tests.
- I undid each fix in turn, and its test failed every time.
- `DictationController.swift` type-checks in Swift 6 mode. I checked it with each plausible SDK signature of `beginBackgroundTask`'s expiration handler.

Not run:
- **The app was not built with the iOS SDK, and the tests did not run on iOS.** Please run the README's test command before merging.
- Tests that need AVFoundation, SwiftUI or word counting (stopwatch, stats, tutorials, onboarding pages) did not run on Linux. I didn't change that code.
- Nothing was tried on an iPhone. Two things are worth checking there: (a) a long Parakeet recording that stops on the time limit while another app is in front, then open the app; (b) the clipboard case above.

## Review notes: top remaining problems, most serious first

1. **The Live Activity's stop button can start a recording.** It runs the same toggle intent as the shortcut. If the app dies while recording, the Live Activity stays. Tapping its stop button then starts a new recording with the microphone on. A stop-only intent would fix it, but it needs testing on a device. (`OpenDictationWidgets/DictationLiveActivity.swift:73`, `:119`)
2. **Only one failed recording is kept.** A second failure replaces the first without a word, though the card says it is "still saved". This was the same before this PR. (`UnsentRecording.keepForRetry`)
3. **Long transcriptions in the background still stop.** They no longer lose the recording, but they can't finish until the app is opened. iOS 26's `BGContinuedProcessingTask` is made for this case.
4. **Two models can be in memory at once.** A download's last step loads its model outside the one-at-a-time queue, so it can overlap a dictation with the other model. (`OneAtATime.swift:25`)
5. **The style step cuts long dictations.** `max_output_tokens` is 2048, about 1,500 English words and fewer in Ukrainian. Past that, the plain text is copied with a note. (`OpenAIRewriter.swift:29`)
6. **An unreadable saved file counts as empty, and the next save replaces it.** This applies to the Recent list and the stats. (`HistoryStore.swift:21`, `Stats/DictationLog.swift:66`)
7. **Audio edge cases:** nothing handles a media services reset during a recording, and Bluetooth microphones are never used (no `.allowBluetoothHFP`, so AirPods users talk into the phone). (`AudioRecorder.swift`)
8. **Small one:** "Throw it away" still works during a retry. (`UnsentRecordingCard.swift:18`)

`HANDOFF.md` is a working note in case this session ran out of time. Delete it before merging.

author: waloid24
body:
## Summary
`string_util.h` and `orset_driver.h` use fixed-width integer types without directly including <cstdint>. They currently rely on transitive includes from other standard-library headers.

This no longer compiles with libstdc++ 15, which reduced transitive inclusion of <stdint.h> and <cstdint>:
https://gcc.gnu.org/gcc-15/porting_to.html#header-dependency-changes.

## Reproduction
The affected translation units were compiled with the same Clang 15 frontend while selecting different libstdc++ header versions:
| Translation unit   | libstdc++ 13 | libstdc++ 15 |
|--------------------|--------------|--------------|
| `string_util.cpp`  | Pass         | Fail         |
| `orset_driver.cpp` | Pass         | Fail         |

Compiling with libstdc++ 15 while explicitly pre-including <cstdint> makes both translation units pass. The existing CI job passes because its Ubuntu 24.04 Clang environment uses a standard-library configuration where the definitions are still transitively available:
https://github.com/cmu-db/bustub/actions/runs/40272396352/job/121407819779

## Outcome
Add the required includes so the headers are self-contained and compile across standard-library versions. The code now builds consistently across libstdc++ versions.

author: eduardopin
body:
A session that stops for a handoff while a background shell or sub-agent is still running gets switched today anyway: the `/clear` drops the task's result, two switches of the same session can race, and the watcher's limits lag the squad in use (handoff at 80%, ceiling 600k, 40 sub-sessions, 3 orchestrators). The switch now waits for background tasks, claims each session once, seals the handoff it hands to the pickup and backs off cleanly; the watcher's thresholds match the squad. Wake-up of stuck sessions, per-repository orchestrator slots and the README/CLAUDE.md numbers stay out of this change.

## Before and after

| Resource | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Switch with a background shell running | `/clear` goes out at once; the shell's result is lost | Waits up to `SQUAD_SWITCH_WAIT` (600 s) for it to come back |
| Switch with a background sub-agent running | `/clear` goes out at once | Waits up to `SQUAD_SWITCH_WAIT_AGENT` (2,400 s); past the deadline it keeps waiting only while the session is busy or herdr is silent, up to `SQUAD_SWITCH_BUSY` (1,800 s) more |
| Two switches for one session | Both can type into the pane | One claim per session: `switches/<session>.claim`, created with `O_EXCL`; the second switch gives up |
| Handoff handed to the pickup | Read-only copy checked by sha256 | Same, plus an optional task note appended to the sealed copy, and the copy's own sha256 rechecked right before `/clear-pickup` |
| Task that returns after the handoff | Ignored | The watcher asks for the handoff to be rewritten with the result, then switches once |
| Switch that gives up before `/clear` (session woke up, pane changed) | Watcher never hears back | Rearms the watcher so the next Stop decides again |
| `/clear` that does not switch the session (dialog open) | Switch gives up silently | Sends Escape when the pane is idle; never while it is working |
| Handoff threshold | Context ≥ 80% of the window, or reread ≥ 60% above a floor of 50–80% by burn | Context ≥ 90%, or reread ≥ 60% above a floor of 70–90% by burn |
| Dispatch limits | Ceiling 600k, 40 sub-sessions, 3 orchestrators, `ORCH_HERE` 120k | Ceiling 800k, 60 sub-sessions, 6 orchestrators, `ORCH_HERE` 500k |
| `session_context.py` report | 80% / 50–80% | Same thresholds as the watcher |

## Resources created

None. No cloud or infrastructure resource; the only new on-disk state is `~/.claude/squad/switches/<session>.claim` and `~/.claude/squad/watch/<session>.switch-note.md`, both local and per session.

## Resources deleted

None. Nothing is removed; the old defaults are still reachable through the same environment variables.

## State and flow

### State

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Stop: handoff written
    Stop --> Claimed: switches/session.claim (O_EXCL)
    Stop --> [*]: claim exists, second switch gives up
    Claimed --> Waiting: background shell or sub-agent alive
    Claimed --> Clearing: no live task
    Waiting --> Clearing: task returned, handoff rechecked
    Waiting --> Rearmed: session woke up or pane changed
    Waiting --> Clearing: deadline plus SQUAD_SWITCH_BUSY passed
    Clearing --> Pickup: session id changed after /clear
    Clearing --> Escaped: session id unchanged and pane idle
    Pickup --> [*]: /clear-pickup on sealed copy, sha256 rechecked
    Escaped --> [*]
    Rearmed --> [*]: watcher decides on next Stop
```

### Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as squad-watch.py
    participant S as squad-switch.py
    participant H as herdr pane
    W->>W: Stop: record live background tasks, write switch note
    W->>S: spawn (pane, session, handoff, sha256, note)
    S->>S: claim, then wait if a task is alive
    S->>H: agent status until idle
    S->>S: seal copy (handoff + note), recheck sha256
    S->>H: /clear
    S->>H: /clear-pickup pickup copy
    S-->>W: rearm on give-up before /clear
```

## Functions created and deleted

| Function | File | Change | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claim_path`, `claim` | `hooks/squad-switch.py` | Created | One switch per session through an `O_EXCL` claim file |
| `read_note` | `hooks/squad-switch.py` | Created | Reads the task note only from `watch/<id>.switch-note.md`, strict path match |
| `wait` | `hooks/squad-switch.py` | Created | Scheduled wait for a background task, with deadline and busy margin |
| `watch`, `rearm` | `hooks/squad-switch.py` | Created | Hands the watcher a synthetic Stop when the switch gives up before `/clear` |
| `sealed_copy` | `hooks/squad-switch.py` | Changed | Appends the note to the sealed copy and returns the copy's sha256 |
| `running`, `news_after`, `spawn`, `here`, `switch_note` | `hooks/squad-watch.py` | Created | Live background tasks at Stop, news after the handoff, spawning the switch or the wait |
| `test_cut_between_70_and_90_percent`, `test_context_at_70_with_low_burn_is_not_handoff_time` | `tests/test_watch.py` | Created | Replace the 50–80% tests of the same cases, renamed for the new thresholds |
| `test_cut_between_50_and_80_percent`, `test_context_at_50_with_low_burn_is_not_handoff_time` | `tests/test_watch.py` | Deleted | Renamed and re-pointed to 70–90% (above); no case dropped |
| 10 new `test_*` (background wait, rewrite on return, Escape, slot, owner request, rearm, herdr failure and silence, claim, orchestrator defaults) | `tests/test_watch.py` | Created | Cover each new switch and threshold path |

## Cost

| Resource | Assumption | $/month |
|---|---|---|
| None | Local hooks only, no cloud resource | 0.00 |
| **Total** | | **0.00** |

Not estimated: nothing.

## Risk analysis

| | |
|---|---|
| Risk of applying | A switch can now sit up to 2,400 + 1,800 s on a stuck sub-agent before going out; the higher limits let a session grow to 90% of its window before the handoff. Both match the squad already running this code. When the claim is created and the `/clear` is then refused, the session is left without a switch (inherited behaviour; card 5354f946, squad-wake, resolves it). |
| Risk of not applying | Background results keep being lost on switch, double switches stay possible, and the public watcher hands off and denies dispatches earlier than the squad it documents |
| Blast radius | Every herdr-hosted Claude Code session using the squad hooks on one machine; no remote state |
| Rollback | Revert the merge commit. The new state files (`*.claim`, `*.switch-note.md`) are inert without the new code and can be deleted; the old thresholds can also be restored by environment variable without a revert |

## Practices applied

| Practice | Source | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Line-by-line parity with the source squad, reviewed independently | Card scope; `CONTRIBUTING.md` | `hooks/squad-switch.py`, `hooks/squad-watch.py` |
| Read-once sealed copy checked by sha256, opened without following symlinks; note path matched strictly | `SECURITY.md` (switch sends a read-only copy verified by SHA-256) | `hooks/squad-switch.py` `sealed_copy`, `read_note` |
| Exclusive file creation for the claim | `SECURITY.md`, no "most recent file" lookups | `hooks/squad-switch.py` `claim` |
| A hook change comes with a test that fails without it | PR template checklist | `tests/test_watch.py` |
| New environment variables documented | PR template checklist | `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/watcher.md` |

## Scans

| Tool | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Lint | `python -m py_compile hooks/*.py skills/session-context/scripts/session_context.py` (the CI compile step) | Pass |
| Semgrep | Not run: the repository has no Semgrep configuration or CI step | Not run |
| Trivy | Not run: no container image, lockfile or IaC in the diff | Not run |
| Secrets (gitleaks) | `gitleaks detect --log-opts="origin/beta..HEAD" --redact` | Pass, no leaks found |

## Tests

| Suite | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Watcher | `python3 tests/test_watch.py` on a7ab89b | 49 passed, 0 failed (beta 39); two tests renamed for the new thresholds, none dropped |
| OMP bridge | `python3 tests/test_watch_
