## Summary

- Applies the layout table of a-novel-kit/stack#1026: each file sits in the deepest directory that holds every route using it, and `src/lib` keeps only what the whole app shares. A URL now leads to its code by walking up from its directory.
- No rendered change: files move, imports follow, and tests move with the code they cover.

## What moved and why

- **Route files hold their server code.** `lib/server/auth/account-route.ts`, `authentication-route.ts`, `authorize.ts` and `shell-layout.ts` were each one route's code under a route-named module; they are now `(app)/account/+page.server.ts`, `(app)/(home)/+page.server.ts`, `(app)/authorize/+page.server.ts` and `(app)/+layout.server.ts`, with their tests beside them as `page.server.test.ts`. The health probe lives in `healthcheck/+server.ts` and its test drives `GET`, status code included.
- **The email-link family shares its code in its group.** The three `ext/` pages already shared a screen in `ext/(short-code)`; their load and submit, link parsing and page-data types join it as `short-code.server.ts`, `short-code-link.server.ts` and `short-code.ts`.
- **No route group without a route.** `(app)/(access)` and `(app)/(authentication)` held no page. The access boundary is a shared component (`src/lib/ui/AccessBoundary.svelte`), the error page's screen sits beside `+error.svelte` as `error-screen.svelte`, and the login dialog's panel is a part of the shell screen, `(app)/authentication-panel.svelte`, whose controller joins the shell's `controller.svelte.ts`.
- **The shell owns its helpers.** The menu and dialog URL codecs, the rail preference, the action-data reader and the account display served only `(app)`, so they sit beside it; `account-action.ts` sits beside the account page.
- `logout.ts` stays in `src/lib/server/auth`: the logout endpoint and the account page's logout action share it. The request suite moves unchanged to `src/routes/request.test.ts`, the root of the routes it drives.

## Breaking changes

None.

body:
Search Console, the last six weeks:

```
week of 21 Sep       159 impressions   position 82    0 clicks
week of 12 Oct     1,521               position 59    0
week of 19 Oct    18,478               position 53   10
week of 26 Oct    10,345               position 50   13
```

Indexing is fixed and the site is now being shown and not read. Underneath that average are
two different businesses:

```
"allison rub"                         position 14    CTR  67%
"quigley law firm"                    position 13    CTR  50%
"national injury help"                position 12    CTR 100%

"wrongful death lawyer los angeles"   position 81   210 impressions   0 clicks
"los angeles motorcycle accident..."  position 79   184              0
"chicago personal injury law firm"    position 88    88              0
```

The volume is on city-and-practice rankings nobody clicks. What converts is a firm's own
name, where we sit one notch below the page. The titles on those three profiles already
lead with the firm name, so neither gap is an on-page problem. Both are authority, and
authority is slow.

So this takes the road the site is actually built for. The directory holds a measurement
of 1,388 firms that nobody else holds, and the thing most likely to quote it is a language
model. Today there is nothing here written for one.

## /llms.txt

Generated from the collection at build time rather than written once, so it cannot drift
from what the site says.

It leads with scope instead of with numbers, because the mistake a model makes with a
directory is reporting a figure without its denominator. These 1,388 firms are not a sample
of American law firms: every one cleared an eligibility gate before being published, so the
median of 50 is the median of this directory. The closing section says so and prints the
accurate sentence beside the inaccurate one.

```
"50 is the median score across the 1,388 firms published on Law Firm Listings"   accurate
"The average US law firm scores 50"                                              not
```

Firms are not enumerated. There are 1,388 of them with a page and a sitemap entry each, and
a list here would be a worse copy of the sitemap. The 28 research guides are listed with
their summaries, because those are the pages that carry findings.

## /data/directory.json

The thing no single page can be: the shape of all 1,388 firms at once.

Every count is three-way.

```
yes             the firms where we read the thing
no              the firms where we looked and it was not there
unestablished   the firms where nobody looked, or nobody could
```

`of_those_read` is the percentage over the first two only. A directory that reports two
columns turns "we could not check" into "they do not have it", and the number that comes
out is wrong in the flattering direction. Scoring here already refuses that trade, because
a sub-factor with no source leaves the denominator rather than costing a firm points, and a
published statistic has to keep the same promise.

```
names at least one attorney        1,008 yes    380 no      0 unestablished
states a fee model                   779        609         0
publishes a readable case result     606        745        37
publishes its own mark             1,310         78         0
```

It is deliberately not the per-firm JSON under `/api/`. That one belongs to the panel, it
carries a firm's subscription, and robots.txt disallows it for a reason worth keeping:
1,388 files repeating what 1,388 pages already say are a waste of a crawl budget. This is
one file saying something none of those pages says.

## evidence

The same honesty pointed at us. Every sub-factor in the directory by the kind of source
behind it:

```
observed              9,691
places                4,155
firm                  4,050
ahrefs                2,770
no queryable source   1,585
registry                633
no roster published      529
pending                 132
```

1,585 against 633. That is a fact about American public records rather than about law
firms, and it is the whole reason pillar A averages 17% of its maximum while pillar C
averages 83%. It belongs in the open next to the scores it holds down.

## Checks

1,632 pages. Nine guards passing, `check_reminders` among them: it was on an unmerged
branch when the first pass ran here and landed on main while this was being written.

Three numbers were wrong in the first draft and are not in this one. `fee_model`,
`results_published` and the Google rating each came back 100% on the first pass, which is
never a finding and always a broken test: the fields are always present, and the absence
lives in a sentinel value or a nested flag. The rating really is universal, because a
verified Google Business Profile is a condition of being listed, so it moved to `scope`
where it describes the sample rather than pretending to describe the profession.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

# And the first study built on it

The dataset above is the substrate for the research pieces, so the second half of this pull
request is one. It takes **item 2 off the ranked backlog**, carried since 2026-10-19 and
unwritten through two runs.

`/guides/does-a-medical-malpractice-page-mean-anything/`

Target: **"how to choose a medical malpractice lawyer", 450/mo US, CPC $3.00**, with
`how to choose a good medical malpractice lawyer` at 30/mo beside it. This is the
per-practice fork the criminal defense run predicted on 2026-10-05 and called "worth a run
each". Full keyword notes, including what was checked and rejected, are in the backlog row.

## The finding

Every page ranking for that query opens with the same instruction: find a firm that handles
medical malpractice, not a general injury firm. The people giving the advice are law firms.
Testing it needs a lot of firms at once, and we hold 1,113 whose own primary practice is
personal injury.

The raw split reads as the advice vindicated:

```
                              rare page     no rare page
median LFL score                     57               47
median organic traffic              895              176
median named attorneys                5                2
median areas published                7                4
```

That last row undoes the three above it. These are not firms that chose a hard specialism.
They are firms with more pages, and one of the pages they have is this one.

## The control, which is the piece

Hold breadth constant. Inside each band of firms publishing the same number of areas,
compare the ones carrying a rarer page against the ones carrying neither:

```
areas   n rare   n not   score rare   score not
    2       15      39           37          39
    3       15      70           42          40
    4       26      84         47.5        48.5
    5       47     155           49          54
    6      111      62           54        54.5
```

**Four of the five bands go the same way or against.** The widest gap in the table runs
against the advice. Bands with fewer than eight firms on a side are not shown.

Worth recording what this does not implicate: `score.py` reads `practices[]` only to pick a
cohort (line 399) and never scores how many there are. The raw gap is not our own arithmetic
paying for pages. It is breadth standing in for firm size, and size is what the scale sees.

## Falsification, fifth consecutive hold

```
mean Google rating    4.85 rare    4.89 no rare
```

The group publishing fewer pages is the higher one. Fifth time a study here has set what
firms publish beside what clients said and found the second one flat.

## A false sentence the build could not see

A draft caption called the highlighted pair "the areas fewest firms publish" while the chart
directly beneath it showed **workers' compensation at 455 sitting below medical malpractice
at 524**. Every figure recomputed correctly and every check passed.

The published page says the pair is chosen by the kind of claim,

author: shatim-ops
body:
## Зачем

#777 стал менять `.github/workflows/ci.yml` только после открытия, и авторевью Qwen не пришло: `qwen-review.yml` срабатывал на `opened` и `ready_for_review`. Решение владельца 03.11 (чат «1.7 — релиз», опрос, вариант 1), уточнение #578: `synchronize`, и ревью приходит само, только если push меняет чувствительный путь. Оно заменяет решение владельца от 24.10 («сессия пишет `/qwen review` после каждого пуша, workflow не меняется»); запись — в `process-handoff.md`.

## Что

- **`.github/workflows/qwen-review.yml`.** В `pull_request_target` добавлен `synchronize`. Скрипт получает `ACTION`, `BEFORE`, `AFTER` из события через `env`, как требуют правила workflow: текст события — через `env`. Код PR по-прежнему не исполняется, `pull_request_target` работает на ветке по умолчанию, SHA читаются только git-ом как данные.
- **`.github/scripts/qwen-review.sh`.**
  - Отбор путей вынесен в функцию `sensitive` — тот же список sensitivePaths.
  - На `synchronize` проверяется пересечение путей push (`before..after`) и путей PR (`base...head`). Если влить в ветку `main`, где менялся `.github/`, это не PR-ный путь и ревью не зовёт.
  - Если SHA некорректен, равен нулю или git его не получил (force-push поверх ушедшего коммита), отбор идёт по diff PR, как при открытии.
- **`qwen_review_scope_test.sh`.** Семь новых случаев с подменёнными git и gh:
  - push добавил `.github/` — ревью;
  - push в чувствительный PR без чувствительных путей — нет;
  - влитый `main` с правкой `.github/` — нет;
  - push в код согласия — ревью;
  - нулевой `BEFORE` — по diff PR;
  - прежний SHA не получен — по diff PR, для нечувствительного и для чувствительного PR.
- **`internal/workflows`.**
  - `TestWorkflows_QwenReviewsOnOpening` требует `synchronize` и передачу `ACTION`, `BEFORE`, `AFTER` через `env`.
  - `TestWorkflows_QwenReviewScope` требует отбор по пересечению (`comm -12 …`).
- **Документы.** Строка в `release-plan.md` (блок A, хозяин — Процесс) и запись о замене решения от 24.10 в `process-handoff.md`. `CLAUDE.md` не трогал: его фраза «приходит само только на PR, который трогает…» остаётся верной, а правила меняет только владелец.

## Проверка

- `bash .github/scripts/qwen_review_scope_test.sh` — 19 ok.
- `go test ./internal/workflows/ ./internal/testrules/ ./internal/repolayout/` — ok.
- shellcheck 0.10 той же командой, что в CI (`install.sh internal/bootstrap/install.sh .github/scripts/*.sh`) — ok.
- Новые проверки краснеют на старом коде. На `qwen-review.sh` из `main` случай «push в чувствительный PR без чувствительных путей» даёт review вместо skip, и `TestWorkflows_QwenReviewScope` падает. На старом `qwen-review.yml` `TestWorkflows_QwenReviewsOnOpening` падает без `synchronize`.

PR трогает `.github/`, поэтому Qwen придёт сам, на `opened`.

author: silvertree2010
body:
## What and why

Fixes #5363

### Cause

The PostScript interpreter stopped every file after a fixed 50,000,000 operations (`MAX_OPS`), whatever the file's size. A large valid EPS that draws many objects through prolog procedures appears to need more than that, so the import was cut off with "the program runs too long".

### Fix

The budget is now set per program when the interpreter is created: 50,000,000 operations plus 64 for each byte of the program. A program of a few kilobytes keeps about the old limit. A 141 MB file gets about 9 billion operations, so a large untrusted file can now run far longer before it is stopped. This change lets untrusted files do more work, so it needs a maintainer's sign-off before merge.

### Not changed

The separate object cap `MAX_NODES` (1 << 20) in `crates/eps/src/import/graphics.rs` is unchanged. A file with more objects than that still loses the extra objects, and no warning is shown.

## How it was tested

- Regression test `import::tests::a_large_file_with_many_objects_reads_to_its_end` was added. It fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p vectorcraft-eps --lib a_large_file_with_many_objects_reads_to_its_end`). The test models the failing shape with a synthetic file.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.
- The attached reproduction file (#5363) was not run against the fix.

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, brands, layers, wasm).
- [ ] No panics in shipped code: no `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!` or
      `unimplemented!` outside tests, and no unchecked indexing on data from files, parameters or
      messages. Errors are returned as `Result` and shown to the user
      ([why and how](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/main/docs/development.md#robustness-vectorcraft-never-crashes)).
- [ ] Clean-room: nothing copied from Adobe products or GPL/AGPL code ([AGENTS.md](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/main/AGENTS.md)).
- [ ] Every new asset has a row in `ASSETS.md`.

author: huntharo
body:
## Summary

Cancelled arrow/box drags could still save on release, another pointer could replace an active stroke, and delayed saves could replace a newer selection or record into the next capture's session. Concurrent history requests could replay one entry twice, discard a rejected entry, or reach capture-level history while an editor replay was busy.

- Give canvas draw, box, raster and selection gestures one discriminated owner with the initiating pointer, live payload and interaction token. Terminal events detach that owner before persistence; the render draft remains a snapshot.
- Keep newer canvas/panel/keyboard selection intent and raster preview ownership through deferred completions. Key the editor session by capture ID.
- Admit one history request through reconciliation and replay. Cancel open gestures, wait for released writes, let newer interactions supersede a waiting request, and retain failed replay entries for retry. Unmount prevents a deferred history request from dispatching.
- Preserve the existing coalescing rules and in-place stroke sampling. Pointer movement stays local.

Multi-layer replay checkpoints acknowledged steps against one exact operation and direction. A direct retry resumes at the first unacknowledged step, preserving completed restores and local ID-chain updates. Before a new edit or reverse replay crosses a partial operation, split its acknowledged prefix into completed history and retain its unfinished suffix on the original stack, then retire the cursor. A new edit therefore keeps the partial redo's persisted changes undoable before clearing future history; reverse replay handles the completed piece before reaching older entries. Both directions remain available to editor controls and the Edit-menu bridge when either piece exists, even with an otherwise empty stack. Coalescing ownership is cleared at this boundary. An interrupted batch becomes separate history entries only when the operator changes direction or makes another edit; ordinary batches and direct retries retain their grouping. Replays remain non-atomic, and an unacknowledged live-ID conflict still fails.

The branch also carries the byte-identical `quit-reentry.test.ts` fixture from [PR #792](https://github.com/pwrdrvr/PwrSnap/pull/792), commit `703542ccc90402bfdd2b98b7c416a084f7c99ade`. The [failing CI job](https://github.com/pwrdrvr/PwrSnap/actions/runs/41688271204/job/126100029437) raced its real 20 ms fail-safe against the model's event-loop settlement. Selective fake deadlines preserve real `setImmediate` dispatch, advance time only after the pre-deadline assertion, and restore timers after each test. This is the already-validated deterministic fixture port so this independently based branch passes the same test; runtime shutdown code is unchanged.

## Screenshots

Not applicable to these lifecycle changes; static layout is unchanged.

## Screen recording

The reproduction uses contrived editor fixtures, synthetic pointer events and deferred dispatch replies. Native headed E2E was not run locally.

## How was this tested?

The [initial test-only commit bd74028a](https://github.com/pwrdrvr/PwrSnap/commit/bd74028a) adds 38 behavioral cases before the production fix. The [followup test-only commit 4ff7b490](https://github.com/pwrdrvr/PwrSnap/commit/4ff7b490) adds 8 partial-replay cases with schema-valid nodes and strict live-ID conflicts.

The [admission test-only commit 918a2d1f](https://github.com/pwrdrvr/PwrSnap/commit/918a2d1f) adds 6 regressions before the latest production change. The final set adds 2 empty-stack keyboard-admission cases and 2 geometry ID-chain cases; all 10 fail against unchanged `5bbfe058`. They cover a partial redo followed by a new edit, reverse history that previously invalidated its cursor, the symmetric partial-undo path, and preserved recovery with real live-ID conflict semantics.

| Validation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New tests against unchanged audited production `c849f1d` | **28 failed, 38 passed** across 2 files |
| Complete editor + Edit-menu bridge suites before the final raster cleanup and retry followup | **57 files, 854 tests passed** |
| Partial-replay tests against `0f00e8b3` before the followup fix | **7 failed, 1 passed** |
| Partial-replay tests after the followup fix | **8 passed** |
| Final draw/gesture + undo + coalescing suites at `4224d7a9` | **3 files, 95 tests passed** |
| `pnpm lint` at `4224d7a9`, including typecheck, syntax/typed lint and policy checks | **Passed** |
| Deterministic quit fixture port at `5bbfe058` | **12 tests passed**, single worker; relevant syntax lint and diff check passed |
| Ported fixture equality with `703542c` | **Identical blob `7e25130d60f013d5720d82b81da9c648230ce88d`** |
| Admission regressions against unchanged `5bbfe058` | **10 failed** |
| Bounded editor/undo/coalescing/Edit-menu run with final production source | **4 files, 126 tests passed** before type-only fixture guards; all **18 partial-replay tests passed** after those guards |
| `pnpm lint` at `60a37585`, including typecheck, syntax/typed lint and policy checks | **Passed** |

Covered interleavings include cancellation/lost capture/window blur, another pointer's events, press/move/release before paint, release outside the canvas, delayed saves followed by a new gesture or panel selection, stale refetch selection, capture switch/unmount, open-gesture history, pending-save history, concurrent replay, failure/retry, and cleanup of only the failed raster commit's own preview. All existing coalescing tests pass.

Partial-replay cases cover multi-delete undo, multi-create redo, replace in both directions with a failure during restore or removal, replay after a complete reverse cycle, a tagged push after partial failure inside an open bracket, and a genuine live-ID conflict that must fail on every retry. The transient restore failure and live-ID conflict both return `insert_failed`; no error code is treated as success.

The complete suite used `--maxWorkers=4 --testTimeout=15000` after shared-host load exceeded 60 and existing dynamic-import tests hit the default five-second deadline. Repository timeout defaults and act-warning guards are unchanged. The final focused run used one worker and default deadlines.

A broader renderer run before the final cleanup passed 3,484 tests and failed the unrelated RegionSelector case “a forwarded Esc right after a keydown step-back is swallowed”; that case passed in isolation. The known unchanged-base Library adapter formatter fixture failure (`formatters.monthShort.format is not a function`) was excluded and is coordinated separately.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

At the test-only commit:
```sh
pnpm test --project desktop-renderer --maxWorkers=1 --testTimeout=15000 \
  apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/features/editor/__tests__/editor-draw-tool \
  apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/features/editor/__tests__/useUndoRedo.test.ts
```

Complete editor and bridge suites:
```sh
pnpm test --project desktop-renderer --maxWorkers=4 --testTimeout=15000 \
  apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/features/editor \
  apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/lib/__tests__/editMenuBridge.test.tsx
```

Final focused suites:

author: fatherlinux
body:
## Summary

Two changes to `security.yml:container-scan`, coupled because the first is what makes the second safe.

**The health check no longer publishes a port.** It published `127.0.0.1:8019` on the runner and curled it. 8019 is the production gateway's port on a real machine, so on a self-hosted runner a CI job would either fail to bind or — production mid-restart — take the port production was about to reclaim. A test must not be able to do that, and picking a different port only narrows the window. It now publishes nothing and probes from a sibling container sharing the server's network namespace, using the image under test so no extra pull is needed.

That is strictly more correct where this already worked: a published port can be answered by anything else listening on the runner, so this gate could have gone green without the built image ever starting. Sharing the namespace makes it impossible to be talking to anything but the container just built — and "a wrong clean" is the defect the security-gateway profile says matters most.

**The runner is chosen by expression.** `vars.FAST_RUNNER_LABEL` for a pull request whose head repo is this repo, GitHub-hosted for everything else.

- A **fork** PR never reaches our hardware. Structural, not a setting a reviewer can click past to see whether CI goes green.
- `push`, `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` stay GitHub-hosted, so every verdict on `main` comes from a clean machine with no persistent layer cache. The self-hosted runner can make a PR pass that should not; it can never build the image we publish.
- The label lives in a repository **variable**, so no hostname is in this repo, and clearing that one variable moves every job back with no commit and no review. That is the kill switch for an offline runner — otherwise a required check never reports and every PR blocks silently.

With `FAST_RUNNER_LABEL` unset, every job runs exactly where it runs today. That is deliberate: this PR is being tested on GitHub-hosted runners first, because `main` and fork PRs depend on that path.

## Gatehouse: the self-hosted runner HIGH

`SKIP=gatehouse` / `SKIP=gatehouse-range`, answered here per CONTRIBUTING.

The finding is that PR-controlled code executes on a self-hosted runner and a contributor with branch-write access could compromise it or persist on a non-ephemeral host. That is the accepted central risk of the change rather than a defect in it, and the mitigations are exactly the three the suggestion asks for. Measured on the host today, not asserted:

- **Ephemeral** — the runner registers with `--ephemeral`, takes one job and de-registers; the container is `--rm`. Confirmed registering and going `online` with labels `self-hosted,Linux,X64,...`. Persistence across jobs is limited to the image layer cache, which is the point of the exercise; a poisoned cache can only produce a false PR pass, never a published image, because `main` and releases build on GitHub-hosted runners.
- **Isolated** — rootless podman container under a dedicated unprivileged user with no sudo and no group shared with production, inside a systemd slice capped at 12 of 16 cores and 32 GB. Verified the cap binds from a *cold* slice start (`cpu.max 1200000 100000`, `memory.max` 32 GB, `cpu.weight 50`), not merely that systemd accepted it. Inner containers share the runner container's network namespace, so nothing a job starts binds a port on the host — verified by publishing 8019 inside the runner while watching the host, which stayed at exactly one listener (production's) throughout.
- **No sensitive host or network access** — the only credential the container gets is a GitHub App key scoped to `administration:write` on this one repository. No registry credential and no production secret: `container.yml` (Quay/GHCR push) and the Gatehouse workflows (API keys) stay GitHub-hosted precisely so that stays true. The runner also does not join the internal `crunchtools` podman network, so a job cannot reach other services.

One thing that verification turned up rather than confirmed: the runner user *could* read production's `/srv` databases, which are mode 644. A job cannot — it is inside a container that mounts no part of `/srv` — but the second step was open, so the unit now carries `InaccessiblePaths=/var/srv /srv`, verified denied from inside the sandbox. The 644 databases are a separate production-hygiene item, not this PR's.

Branch-write access on this repository is two people. A fork PR never lands there.

## Test plan

- [x] YAML parses; `runs-on` expression resolves
- [x] Trentina's image builds inside the runner container (2m11s cold, 7s with the layer cache warm)
- [x] `/health` answers through the sibling-container probe: `{"status":"ok","classifier":"loaded","profiles":1,"pending_pins":0}`
- [x] The host's 8019 listener count is unchanged throughout a runner job
- [ ] This PR's own `container-scan` passes on a GitHub-hosted runner (the path `main` and forks use)
- [ ] Then, with `FAST_RUNNER_LABEL` set, the same job passes on the self-hosted runner
- [ ] A fork PR lands on `ubuntu-latest`

## Why

Decision 101 (03/11/2026): sharing by link leaves the Tisty app completely. Tisty Share moves to its own repository, Folio by Tisty, and Tisty keeps only its own key. The removal goes in small PRs; this is the second one, after #556.

## What this PR removes (backend only, `app/src-tauri`)

- `sharing.rs` with its in-memory test server (`sharing_here.rs`) and tests: the Share client, the `sharing::ON` switch, uploads, pictures, revocations sent to the server and the share refusal codes.

The `tisty://` scheme stays: `tisty://open` still opens local files. `tisty-share-proto` stays (with `mint`) for the app's own keys, phrase, certificates, cloud seal and parcels, and for the signing-name check. author: danswett
body:
Part of #459 (P0, CI throughput), item 2. Part of #357. PR B (caching) follows separately.

**Security-sensitive** (AGENTS.md rule 5): this changes when code scanning runs and adds a job with `pull-requests: read`. An independent security review runs on the final head.

## What changed
### `codeql.yml`: per-language analysis on pull requests
- **The new `languages` job:**
  - **Main pushes and the weekly schedule** get all three languages, unconditionally.
  - **A pull request:** the job lists the PR's changed files through the API, including a renamed file's old path, and picks a language for each kind of change:
    - **csharp:** `*.cs`, `*.csproj`, `*.cshtml`, `*.razor`, `*.props`, `*.targets`, `*.sln`, `*.slnx`, `Directory.*`, `nuget.config`, `global.json`.
    - **javascript-typescript:** `*.js`/`mjs`/`cjs`/`jsx`/`ts`/`mts`/`cts`/`tsx`/`html`/`htm`/`vue`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `tsconfig*.json`, and anything under `pwa/`.
    - **actions:** anything under `.github/`, and any `action.yml`/`action.yaml`.
- **Fail-safe:** these cases analyse **all three**:
  - a change to `codeql.yml` itself;
  - an empty file list;
  - 3000 files or more, where the API's list may be incomplete.

  **A failed listing fails the job** (bash `-e` with `pipefail`) rather than reading as "nothing to analyse".
- **`analyze`** takes its matrix from that output. It's skipped only when the list is `[]`, which happens for a docs-only PR. The run summary says what was analysed and what was left out.
- **Permissions:** the new job has only `pull-requests: read` and no checkout. `analyze` keeps `contents: read` and `security-events: write`.

### Concurrency: CodeQL, Dependencies and Workflow lint
All three now use #431's grouping:
- **Pull requests:** `<workflow>-pr-<number>`, and a newer push cancels the older run.
- **Every other run:** `<workflow>-<run_id>`, and it's never cancelled.

**What that changes for CodeQL:** its old group was `codeql-<ref>`, which put main's pushes and the weekly run in one group. GitHub keeps only one pending run per group, so a burst of merges could silently drop a main analysis. Now every main commit is analysed.

Dependencies and Workflow lint run only on pull requests, so for them only the group name changes.

## Code scanning stays truthful
- **A skipped language uploads nothing.** On the PR, code scanning's own CodeQL check then reports that configuration as not found: "Code scanning cannot determine the alerts introduced by this pull request, because N configuration(s) present on refs/heads/main was not found". So the check **never claims a skipped language has no alerts**. There's no false "no alerts", because no empty SARIF is uploaded.
- **No stale-alert closure:** alerts close only when a later analysis of the same category on the same ref lacks them. Main's runs still upload every category, and a PR's partial analysis touches only the PR's own ref.
- **Analysed languages still block:** the check still compares them with main and fails on new high or critical alerts as before.

## Safety invariants (#459)
- **main runs every suite before publish:** unchanged. This PR doesn't touch `ci.yml`, and CodeQL on main analyses all languages on every push, now including pushes that the old shared group would have displaced.
- **a non-draft PR runs everything the selector picks at ring 1:** unchanged. The selector and `ci.yml` aren't touched. CodeQL's catalog entry stays `select: always`: the workflow runs on every PR and picks languages itself, and the catalog comment says so.
- **quality-gate covers every job:** unchanged. `quality-gate` is in `ci.yml` (#443), which isn't touched, and CodeQL was never one of its jobs.
- **no test is skipped:** no test suite changes. Only the CodeQL languages a PR doesn't touch are skipped, and they're reported as not found, as above.

## Measured
Taken from the last 60 successful runs of each workflow, using job wall times.
- **CodeQL per PR push:** `csharp` averages 2.88 min, `javascript-typescript` 1.27 and `actions` 0.76: 3 jobs and about 4.9 runner-minutes.
- **Dependencies** takes 0.68 runner-minutes over 2 jobs, and **Workflow lint** 0.24 over 1. They're unchanged except that superseded runs are cancelled.

Applying the new picker to the files of the last 40 merged PRs:

| PR kind | count | CodeQL jobs | runner-min (avg) |
|---|---|---|---|
| .NET only | 21 | 3 → 2 (`languages` + csharp) | 4.9 → ~3.0 |
| PWA/JS only | 10 | 3 → 2 | 4.9 → ~1.4 |
| workflows only | 4 | 3 → 2 | 4.9 → ~0.9 |
| docs only | 3 | 3 → 1 (`languages` only) | 4.9 → ~0.1 |
| two or three languages | 2 | 3 → 3 or 4 | about the same |
| **all 40** | | **3.00 → 2.00 per push** | **4.91 → 2.23 per push** |

CodeQL's wall time per PR is bounded by its slowest language, at most about 3 min. That stays the same or improves; the gain is mostly runner-minutes and queue slots. This PR changes `codeql.yml`, so its own run analyses all three (the fail-safe rule). Its CodeQL run therefore doesn't show the saving.

## Verified locally
- **The `languages` script** ran in Git Bash with `-eo pipefail`, with a stubbed `gh`:

  | Changed files | Languages picked |
  |---|---|
  | docs only | `[]` |
  | `.cs` + `.csproj` | `["csharp"]` |
  | `Directory.Build.props` | `["csharp"]` |
  | `pwa/*.mjs` + lockfile | `["javascript-typescript"]` |
  | `pwa/*.css` | `["javascript-typescript"]` |
  | a workflow | `["actions"]` |
  | `codeql.yml` | all three |
  | a mixed change | all three |
  | a deleted `.cs` | `["csharp"]` |
  | an empty list | all three |

  A failing `gh` exits 1 with no output.
- **On a push event**, it picks all three.
- **actionlint 1.7.12 with shellcheck 0.11.0:** no findings.
- **zizmor 1.32.0** (regular persona, online audits): no findings.
- **`dotnet test tests/AgentBridge.Quality.Tests`:** 67 passed (catalog edit).

author: useofscript
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"useofscript"} -->
_Requested by **Script** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01MZyFA193MjgETYsRHvQwdf?thread=cmsg_01MZyFA193MjgETYsRHvQwdfHg2ZgN3DhT6GqDD2yBKSMZ)_

## Why
Kermit's answer about the Lyreto bridge was: "u js needa have the roblox code stuff for it to work". Lyreto already has a **Roblox Game Bridge** (lyreto.com/developers/bridge): a server ModuleScript (`LyretoBridge`) plus a key from the Lyreto server's settings. The module sends player chat to `POST https://lyreto.com/api/bridge/v1/messages`, long-polls `GET /api/bridge/v1/messages` for channel messages, and shows them as "[Lyreto] name: message" through a small LocalScript.

I read the module line by line (I didn't run Lyreto's code here) and filled in every engine piece it uses that Guts&Bolts didn't have yet.

## Engine
- **Luau:** generalized `for _, v in list do` loops and `if … then … else …` values are rewritten into plain Lua (`__gb_iter` helper in the prelude).
- **TextService:FilterStringAsync** goes through our chat filter. The result has `GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync`, `GetChatForUserAsync` and `GetNonChatStringForUserAsync`.
- **RunService:IsServer / IsClient / IsStudio / IsRunning**, **game.JobId** (each server gets its own ID; "" in Studio, like Roblox), `table.clear`, and `typeof(secret) == "Secret"`.
- **StarterGui:SetCore("ChatMakeSystemMessage")** shows a line in that player's own chat. **TextChatService.ChatVersion** reads `LegacyChatService`, so scripts written for both chat systems use SetCore. `DisplaySystemMessage` called from a LocalScript now shows only on that computer; before, on the host it went to everyone.
- **IsDescendantOf(workspace)** is false for things in the service folders (ServerScriptService, ReplicatedStorage…), like Roblox. The module refuses to start if it thinks it's in the Workspace.
- **Where LocalScripts run:** they don't run inside ServerScriptService or ServerStorage (the module keeps its client there as a template). A LocalScript put in StarterPlayerScripts during a game waits for the next player instead of running at once, which avoids double lines on the host.
- StarterPlayer always has a StarterPlayerScripts folder, and `player:FindFirstChildOfClass("PlayerGui")` finds the PlayerGui.

## Website server
- Web requests wait up to 25 s for an answer (was 10 s), because Lyreto's bridge holds a request open while it waits for messages.
- When a game has web requests off, the error now starts with "HTTP requests are not enabled", like Roblox's. Roblox-style scripts look for those words.

The C++ server can't make web requests at all, so nothing changes there.

## Checks
- New `tests/RobloxChatBridgeTests.cpp`: the Luau rewrites, a typed module in ServerScriptService with a LocalScript template, and each new API. Passes.
- All 36 ctest tests pass and all 304 worker tests pass. Player, Studio and the servers build.

## What Lyreto still needs (for Script to ask Kermit)
1. **Accept a Secret as the key**, the Roblox way: `LyretoBridge.Start({ ApiKey = HttpService:GetSecret("LyretoKey") })`, using `apiKey:AddPrefix("Bearer ")` for the Authorization header when `typeof(apiKey) == "Secret"`. On Guts&Bolts anyone can host a game, so a key typed into a script could be read by a host. Secrets stay on the Guts&Bolts server. This also works on Roblox (Roblox has secrets too).
2. **Know when messages come from a Guts&Bolts game:** those requests carry `X-GutsAndBolts-Game`, `X-GutsAndBolts-Server` and `X-GutsAndBolts-Host` headers. The `robloxUserId` field will hold a Guts&Bolts user ID, so Lyreto shouldn't look up a Roblox profile for it. A "GUTS&BOLTS" tag instead of "ROBLOX" would fit.

## Problem
Running the multi-shop mode from the deploy compose files (for example a public demo on Dokploy) didn't work by setting variables: the `shopnex` service hardcoded `TENANCY_MODE: single` and never mentioned `OPEN_SIGNUP` or `ROOT_DOMAIN`. Values set in the platform's Environment tab only fill `${...}` placeholders in the compose file, so none of them reached the container; the login page kept saying "Ask a shop owner to invite you". The only way was to edit the compose file.

In `deploy/docker-compose.yml`, `deploy/docker-compose.dokploy.yml` and `deploy/dokploy-template/docker-compose.yml`:

```yaml
TENANCY_MODE: ${TENANCY_MODE:-single}
OPEN_SIGNUP: ${OPEN_SIGNUP:-false}
ROOT_DOMAIN: ${ROOT_DOMAIN:-}
```

The defaults are the old behaviour (single shop, invitation-only, no root domain), so existing installs don't change.

body:
## Summary
Our Seguridad client, mocks and fake seed were written against an early Prism mock. An audit of G7's real backend (`Modulo-de-Seguridad-Backend`, branch `develop`) and its public discovery document showed that real tokens were rejected and several request/response shapes differed. This PR aligns the client with the real contract so `MODULES_MODE=http` can run against `https://g7-auth-service.onrender.com/api/v1`.

## Changes
- **Issuer**: configurable via `SECURITY_EXPECTED_ISSUER` (default `auth-service`); production value `https://g7-auth-service.onrender.com/api/v1/auth` (from `/auth/.well-known/openid-configuration`).
- **Request fields**: login `{correo, contrasena}`, MFA verify `{challengeToken, codigo}`, resend `{correo}`.
- **Registration**: always sends `correo, contrasena, nombres, apellidos, celular (+51 + 9 digits), aceptaTerminos, canalOrigen=CHATBOT`; reads `{id, estado}`; 422 `POLITICA_INCUMPLIDA` returns one row per rule `{campo, mensaje, regla, esperado}`. Inbound phone accepts `^(\+51)?[0-9]{9}$` and is normalized to `+51`.
- **Responses**: addresses read `direcciones`; password policy exposes the real Spanish fields and keeps the English aliases; profile document from `tipoDocumento`/`documentoEnmascarado`.
- **Errors**: 403 `PASSWORD_CADUCADA`, 401 `OTP_INTENTOS_AGOTADOS`, 401 `CODIGO_INVALIDO` (with `intentosRestantes`); `OTP_EXPIRADO` is exposed as 410 `CODIGO_VENCIDO`.
- **Security**: the client no longer sends `client_secret` as a header on every request; only `POST /auth/token` uses it. A missing secret now only disables introspection instead of breaking the whole client (customer endpoints are public or use the holder token).
- **Introspection** sends the service Bearer token.
- Respx mocks and the fake seed follow the real contract.

## What

`GET /api/tasks` takes `updated_before` (ISO time, exclusive): only tasks whose last event is earlier. With `from_date` it lists exactly the runs one bucket of `GET /api/stats/timeseries` counts.

## Why

The redesigned Overview opens the runs behind a chart bar. `from_date` compares the task's last event (the time the chart counts it at), but `to_date` compares its first event, so a run that started before the bucket and ended after it would be listed under the wrong bar. There was no upper bound on the last event. This is the one backend gap for the Overview (PR 6); everything else it shows is served by T6's endpoints.

## Tests

`tests/unit/test_routes_updated_before.py`: exclusive bound (store), one bucket's list equals the timeseries count for that bucket, a long-running task is not listed under the bucket it started in, naive datetimes are UTC, combined with `within`.

Mutation: `<` to `<=` fails 2 tests.

`ruff`, `mypy --strict` on `store.py` and `routes.py`: clean. Changelog fragment included.

author: florentrvl
body:
## Problem

Nexus workspaces show the **Async Error Caught** overlay with:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '_leaflet_pos')
  at _getMapPanePos → _getNewPixelOrigin → _move → _onZoomTransitionEnd
```

Reported in ForvisMazarsAI/bob#1622.

## Root cause

Leaflet 1.9.4 `_animateZoom` schedules `_onZoomTransitionEnd` with an **uncancellable** `setTimeout(…, 250)`. That works around browsers that don't fire `transitionend`. `map.remove()` deletes `_mapPane` but cannot clear that timer. If a map is torn down within ~250 ms of an animated zoom, the timer still runs `_move` → `_getMapPanePos(undefined)` and throws. Things that tear a map down mid-zoom: navigating away, a Strict Mode remount, switching layout/dataset, a `fitBounds`/`flyTo` that is still animating, or a zoom +/- click.

The existing `safeInvalidateMapsLeafletSize` guard only covers `invalidateSize`, not this path.

## Fix

- New `guardMapsLeafletZoomTeardown(map)` in `maps/lib/leaflet-map.ts`. It wraps the instance's `_onZoomTransitionEnd` so the late callback becomes a no-op once `_mapPane` is gone. On a live map it delegates to Leaflet unchanged. It is idempotent.
- Installed on every Nexus Leaflet map: `createMapsLeaflet`, which covers `MapsFeedCanvas` and all feed/layout maps, and `MapsPresenceMap`.

## Tests

New `leaflet-map-zoom-teardown.test.ts` (jsdom, real Leaflet):
- reproduces the `_leaflet_pos` throw **without** the guard (remove mid-zoom, then advance timers);
- no throw with the guard;
- on a live map the zoom still completes (`getZoom() === 3`, `zoomend` fired once);
- the guard is idempotent.

Checks:
- `pnpm exec vitest run`: the 4 new tests pass. The set of failing tests is identical with and without this change. The 45 failures already on `main` include the 6 `maps-feed-canvas.test.ts` tests that fail with "invariant expected app router to be mounted".
- `pnpm typecheck` and eslint on the touched files: clean.
- `make check`: passes (core, marketplace, Nexus build).

author: iskandr
body:
## Summary
ORFdata becomes a core dependency, so `pip install varcode` can annotate noncanonical ORFs without an extra. `extra_orfs` now uses whatever ORFdata data is installed: a missing catalogue triggers a warning instead of an error. Version 11.6.0: a minor release, because it changes the install requirements.

Part of #640 (the ORF half of the dependency consolidation; the RNA/pysam and Biotite items stay open). Closes #612.

## Why
#640 asks for ordinary `pip install varcode` to cover the common ORF capabilities. Every ORFdata release since 0.43 requires `pandas>=3,<4` and `pyensembl>=2.32.3`. A core dependency therefore also raises Varcode's floors, which is what #612 requested.

With ORFdata always installed, `extra_orfs="all"` on a genome whose catalogues or chain files are not all installed used to raise `NotInstalledError` from deep inside annotation. A plain install should degrade gracefully instead.

## What changed
- `requirements.txt`: adds `orfdata>=0.44.0,<1`; raises to `pandas>=3.0.0,<4.0.0` and `pyensembl>=2.32.3`. The 0.44 floor is the release with the `orfdata setup` / `data fetch` CLI the new warning tells users to run.
- `pyproject.toml`: the `orf` and `uorf` extras stay, empty, so `pip install 'varcode[orf]'` keeps working.
- `varcode/extra_orfs.py`: `_place_installed` first calls `orfdata.extra_orfs(genome, evidence)`. On `NotInstalledError`, it re-places using only the selected catalogues for the genome's species that are installed (bundled, downloaded or built) and are on the genome's assembly or have a downloaded lift to it. If none qualifies, the genome gets no extra ORFs. Either way it warns with ORFdata's message, which names the install command. Results are cached per genome, so the warning and the placement happen once.
- The `ImportError` guards for a missing ORFdata are removed from `extra_orfs`, `orf`, `uorf` and `proteome`, and tests no longer `importorskip("orfdata")`.
- CI: drops the Python 3.11 + pandas 2 job, and the sdist install no longer requests the `uorf` extra.
- Docs: removes the `varcode[orf]` install steps and the `orfdata[data,build-data]` extras, which ORFdata no longer has. The getting-started dependency section now lists the new floors, and the ORF guide describes the fallback instead of "fails with the command".

## Behavior change
- A pandas 2 environment can no longer install this version; pip will upgrade pandas, or refuse if something pins pandas<3.
- `extra_orfs` with missing ORFdata data now warns and annotates with what is installed; before, it raised.

## Testing
- `./lint.sh` (ruff and mypy) is clean.
- With ORFdata 0.48.1, the version CI installs: 355 passed across the ORF suites (`test_extra_orfs`, `test_uorf`, `test_proteome`, `test_cli_reference_orfs`, `test_common_transcript_orfs`, `test_non_aug_orfs`, `test_orf_reference_dna`, `test_orf_serialization`, `test_species_genetic_codes`, `test_start_loss_details`). Also 291 passed across the documentation-example, source-distribution, native-reference and extra-ORF tests.
- Two new tests in `test_extra_orfs.py` cover the fallback. With the bundled catalogue installed but others missing, it warns, places only `bundled`, and does not re-warn or re-place on a second call. With nothing installed, it warns, and the effects match plain `variant.effects()`.
- `mkdocs build --strict` passes.
- I'm relying on CI for the full matrix.

author: devikae
body:
## 다이어그램
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as PostService / CommentService 등 11곳
    participant O as search_outbox
    participant P as SearchOutboxProcessor (@Scheduled)
    participant S as post / comment (원문)
    participant X as search_index_state
    participant D as search_document
    W->>O: 원문 변경과 같은 트랜잭션에 INSERT (Propagation.MANDATORY)
    P->>O: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED + lease, attempts+1
    P->>X: 게시글 상태 행 잠금 (ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE)
    alt 이벤트 버전 < applied_version
        P->>O: DONE (오래된 이벤트 무시)
    else
        P->>S: 현재 원문 재조회
        alt 비공개·삭제
            P->>D: 게시글·댓글 문서 삭제
            P->>X: tombstone (id·버전만)
        else 공개
            P->>D: 해당 원문 문서 교체
            P->>X: applied_version 갱신
        end
        P->>O: DONE (한 트랜잭션)
    end
```

## 무엇을 바꿨나
IKA-5 2단계(IKA-10)와 평가 실행기(IKA-9)를 하나의 PR로 묶었다. 사용자 요청으로 snowthing PR 수를 줄였고, IKA-7(#51) 위에 쌓았다.

정합성(설계 017 D6): 게시글·카풀·장터·댓글의 생성·수정·삭제와 장터 관리 상태 변경, 모두 11곳에서 원문 변경과 같은 트랜잭션에 `search_outbox`를 기록한다. 처리기는 이벤트 내용 대신 현재 원문을 다시 읽어 인덱스를 맞춘다. 원문 버전이 `applied_version`보다 낮은 이벤트는 버리고, 삭제는 원문을 보관하지 않는 tombstone으로 남겨 역순 이벤트가 문서를 되살리지 못하게 했다. 실패는 지수 백오프로 5회까지 재시도한 뒤 FAILED로 분리하고, 관리자 API로 다시 처리할 수 있다. 매일 대조해 어긋난 인덱스를 다시 큐에 넣고, 재인덱싱은 id 순서 체크포인트로 원문별 교체를 해서 검색 중단 없이 진행된다.

평가(IKA-9): 근거 검색 API에 평가용 선택 파라미터 `createdBefore`, `excludePostPublicId`를 추가했다. `scripts/evaluate-evidence-search.py`는 저장소 밖의 사람 검토 평가 자료(JSONL)로 Recall@k를 n/N 형태로, 지연 P50/P95와 함께 계산한다. 질문 원문은 출력하지 않는다.

결정과 이유
- outbox 기록은 명시적인 서비스 호출로 했다. 댓글 소프트 삭제가 JPQL 일괄 UPDATE라 엔티티 콜백이 돌지 않는다. AFTER_COMMIT 비동기 방식은 커밋 뒤 프로세스가 죽으면 이벤트를 잃는다. 새 쓰기 경로에서 호출을 빠뜨리면 매일 대조로만 잡힌다는 대가가 있다.
- 같은 버전 이벤트도 다시 처리한다. 댓글 소프트 삭제는 `version`을 올리지 않는데, 기존 낙관적 락 동작을 바꾸지 않으려고 그대로 두었다.
- 처리는 이벤트마다 READ COMMITTED 한 트랜잭션이다. 게시글 단위 상태 행을 잠가 직렬화하고, 잠금 순서는 게시글 상태 → 댓글 상태(id 순)로 고정했다.
- 계획에 없던 컬럼 `search_index_state.document_count`를 추가했다. 이게 없으면 대조에서 구간 하나가 빠진 경우를 찾지 못한다.
- 설계 D6의 "새 세대 생성 후 전환·롤백" 대신 원문별 교체 + 체크포인트로 구현했다. 이 차이는 문서 05에 적었다. 기존 `/rebuild`는 `search_index_state`를 갱신하지 않아 deprecated로 표시했다.

## 검증
- `./gradlew test --rerun` (전용 테스트 DB): 534개 중 실패 0, 기존 제외 1. 브랜치 직후 기준 실행에서 나온 1건 실패(`ProfileImageSecurityIntegrationTest` 503)는 새 DB에 `request_budget_window`가 아직 없어서 생긴 환경 문제였고, 이후 실행에서 통과했다.
- 장애 테스트: 중복 처리, 역순 버전, 삭제 후 오래된 upsert(부활 없음), 예외 주입 → 백오프 1/2/4/8초 → FAILED → 재처리, 작업자 중단 후 lease 만료 재처리, 숨김·복구·차단 전환 시 게시글·댓글 문서와 근거 조회 404, 인덱스를 일부러 훼손한 뒤 대조로 복구, 체크포인트 재개 중 검색 유지, 새 엔드포인트 401/403.
- 반영 지연 (**로컬 측정, 운영 아님**): 한 게시글을 0~300ms 간격으로 100번 수정. 측정은 `processed_at − created_at`, 앱과 DB가 같은 Windows 11 호스트(Docker MySQL 8.0.46, Java 21), 간격별 1회 실행.

| 폴링 간격 | N | P50 | P95 | 최대 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000ms | 100 | 444.6ms | 939.8ms | 1017.7ms |
| 200ms | 100 | 106.1ms | 197.6ms | 233.4ms |

- 평가 실행기: 로컬 앱과 직접 넣은 데이터로 동작만 확인했다(측정 아님). 실제 평가 수치는 사람 검토 정답이 필요해 아직 없다(`04_evaluation.md` §5).
- Spotless: worktree에서 JGit 문제로 일반 복제본에서 통과시켰다. 마이그레이션 028은 임시 스키마에서 검증 스크립트를 통과했고, 두 번 더 실행해도 성공했으며, `validate`로 앱이 기동한다.
- 운영 마이그레이션·배포는 하지 않았다.

## 리뷰 포인트
- **머지되어 운영에 반영되면 027·028이 적용되고 처리기가 켜진다.** 배포 뒤 `POST /api/v1/admin/search/reconcile`을 한 번 실행해야 한다. 이전 이미지가 서비스하던 동안의 변경은 대조로만 반영된다.
- 분산 스케줄러 잠금이 없어서 인스턴스마다 폴링과 대조를 한다. 결과는 정확하지만 작업이 중복된다.
- 댓글이 아주 많은 게시글은 게시글 이벤트 하나의 트랜잭션이 길어진다.

Closes IKA-10
Closes IKA-9

author: davidsoto31
body:
## Problema
Una marcación hecha después de medianoche solo se asignaba al turno de ayer si ese turno **cruzaba la medianoche por horario** (ej. 21:40–06:00). Con un turno como **14:00–22:00** y horas extra hasta las **00:30**, la salida se tomaba como una marcación **del día nuevo**:
- Si ese día tenía turno, la salida quedaba como su **entrada**. Ayer quedaba sin salida (alerta "Sin marcar salida" y extras sin liquidar) y el turno de hoy quedaba corrido ("salida a almuerzo" al llegar).
- Si ese día no tenía turno, el kiosco no le dejaba marcar la salida.

## Solución
Si ayer el colaborador marcó entrada y todavía no marcó salida, una marcación después de medianoche es **de ayer** cuando:
- llega dentro de las **6 horas** siguientes a la salida programada de ayer, y
- hoy **no** tiene un turno que empiece en las **2 horas** siguientes (para no confundirla con una entrada temprana de hoy).

Aplica al kiosco con conexión, sin conexión y a la marcación manual. Las extras de esa noche se calculan con las reglas de siempre. La alerta **"Turno sin cerrar"** pasa de 5 a **6 horas** después de la salida programada, para coincidir con ese margen. Los turnos de noche siguen igual.

## Prueba (marcaciones con su hora real, vía sincronización del kiosco)
- **Turno 14–22, sale a las 00:30, hoy turno a las 14:00:** la salida queda en el día anterior con **2 h 30 min de extra nocturna**, y la entrada de hoy va en su propio día.
- **Ayer sin salida, marca a las 03:30, hoy turno a las 05:00:** se toma como **entrada de hoy** (empieza en menos de 2 h).
- **Ayer sin salida, marca a las 04:30** (6 h 30 min después): no se asigna a ayer.
- **Turno de noche 21:40–06:00:** sin cambios.

body:
This is the backend step that the editor's Knowledge section needs (ADR 0038 build rows 10 and 11, part `editor-and-elsewhere` of software#525). It does two things:

- `FactoryModel.knowledge_sources` is now typed as a name or a `KnowledgeSourceEntry` object. `internal/factorymodel` already kept object entries, and until now the contract said they couldn't exist.
- goald renders the editor's "What agents see" preview through the same Go code that builds a run's Knowledge section.

## What changed

- `domain.IndexKnowledge` (`internal/core/domain/knowledge_section.go`) is now the only builder of a Knowledge index. It picks the sources that apply to the run, uses each entry's readWhen or else the snapshot's, lists the sources with no snapshot as not synced yet, adds the memory, and returns nothing for an agent that may not read files. The gateway's `knowledgeOf` calls it with the snapshot pinned on the claim.
- `GET /v1/orgs/{org}/factories/{factory}/draft/knowledge-preview?agent=&station=&lane=&work_type=` (`getDraftKnowledgePreview`, scope `factory:read`) answers `{section}`. It calls `domain.IndexKnowledge` with each source's current snapshot and takes the top folders from the source's files. The endpoint description says that a run uses the snapshot its claim pinned, so a run may see a different snapshot than the preview.
- `authoring.Service.DraftLine` reads the draft's `domain.Line`, including its knowledge and memory.yaml. A draft whose references are broken still has a line. It returns `*ParseError` (409 yaml-invalid) when factory.yaml doesn't parse or doesn't satisfy the schema.
- I added `lane` to the spec's `station` and `work_type` parameters, because `appliesTo` can also name lanes.

## Acceptance criteria

- knowledge_sources is typed as a name or an object, and both read and write keep the entries unchanged: met. `TestAPI_DraftModelKnowledgeEntryObjects` passes.
- The preview lists the sources that apply with their readWhen, file count and top folders, lists the unsynced ones and the memory, and leaves out sources that don't apply to the agent: met. `TestAPI_DraftKnowledgePreview` passes.
- The refusals work (404 agent-not-found, 409 yaml-invalid), a viewer may read the preview, and the section is empty for an agent that may not read files: met. `TestAPI_DraftKnowledgePreviewRefusals` passes. `testdata/access.golden` shows 200 for a viewer.
- The gateway and the handler share one builder: met. The gateway's knowledge tests pass without changes (`go test -run 'TestBundle_Knowledge' ./internal/gateway`), and `TestKnowledgeIndex_SectionOfAnAgentsRun` passes.
- The generated code is regenerated and committed, and `task gen:check` passes: met. One correction to the spec: the docs site has no generated API reference page for `task docs:gen` to write. `apps/docs/src/pages/openapi.yaml.ts` serves the contract directly. `task docs:gen` regenerated only the change map, and `task docs:check` passes.

## Checks run

- The spec's verification commands for api, gateway, domain and factorymodel: pass.
- `go test -race` for internal/api, authoring, gateway, core/domain and factorymodel: pass.
- `task gen:check`, `task lint` (0 issues), `task docs:check`: pass.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web run typecheck` and `pnpm --dir packages/api-client run typecheck`: pass.
- Not run: `task check:changed` (the station runs it) and the integration tests (this change touches no SQL and no adapter).

## Disagreements between repository rules

`.claude/rules/contracts.md` says a branch never regenerates `docs/engineering/change-map.md`. AGENTS.md (amended 2026-10-29) says to run `task docs:gen` and commit the result. I followed AGENTS.md and edited entry file 368.

author: asuresh8
body:
## What changes for a reader

Before: `troubleshooting.md` said only "a limit of the OCI front" for exit 2, quoted no OCI message, had no entry for the build-node cache refusals, and described exit 3 as only a wrong self-test answer. After: two new blocks, "OCI front" and "Build-node cache", quote each message with its cause and fix, and the exit 2 and exit 3 rows name them. A missing or unwritable cache directory is now documented as exit 3 with no restart. No code, flag or message changes.

## Walk

- `crates/tierstore/docs/troubleshooting.md` exit table: row 2 points at the OCI prefix/certificate/key refusals and the cache budget refusal (both `InvalidFlags`, exit 2 per `exit_status` in `server/cli.rs`); row 3 adds the unusable cache directory and cache-check failure (`LocalTierFailure`, exit 3).
- "OCI front": messages from `server/oci/tls.rs`, `server/oci/mod.rs` (prefix rules), `server/cli.rs` (both-or-neither TLS flags), and the runtime handshake lines from `server/oci/listener.rs`. Notes that read and bind failures exit 1 (`is_invalid_flags`), the rest exit 2. The 10 second handshake limit is `OCI_HANDSHAKE` in `server/cli.rs`.
- "Build-node cache": the budget message from `server/cache_cli.rs`, the two `refusing to start` messages and the three check names from `server/local_cache/selfcheck.rs`.

## Compatibility and failure modes

Docs only; B8 does not apply (no format touched), so there is no cross-release test. Measured by reading the cited sources; the messages are copied from the format strings, not run.

## Tests

None added or changed: no behaviour changes (T5 not applicable). CI coverage is unaffected.

author: hstecher
body:
GWS migration to github.


AI summary
```
The first GitHub build (702da78) left six BuildRequires unpinned, and the flat rpm-repo (el8+el9 together) resolved two of them to EL9 packages in an EL8 build: timeProbe-devel-1.1.16-3.git.712092b.el9 and tdct-2.18.6-5.el9. That build only produced a correct IOC by luck.

Pin every BuildRequires to the exact NVR that build resolved, using the .el8 build of the same version where it had picked .el9. asyn-devel and streamdevice-devel carry no dist tag in rpm-repo, so they are pinned without %{?dist}.

tdct needs the pin even though nothing in gws compiles against it: the pipeline installs gemini-ade before reading the spec, and gemini-ade pulls tdct.el9. The pin makes dnf builddep downgrade it to .el8.

Verified with a local ./gemini-rtsw-ci/build_rpm.sh --el 8:
- BUILD DEPENDENCY VERSIONS: every -devel resolves to .el8 (or no-dist).
- gws-mk-IOC is byte-identical to the 702da78 CI build.
- Against the last GitLab build gws_mk-1.1-1.el8 (2025-04-02): 12/15 files byte-identical; db/gwsTop.db and gwsSadTop.db differ only in the generation-timestamp line; in gws-mk-IOC, 140/144 functions and all data sections (.rodata .data .dynsym .dynstr .rela.plt) are identical, same NEEDED libs (EPICS 7.0.7). The rest is C-runtime startup code and annobin notes from a newer EL8 gcc (8.5.0-29/30 vs 8.5.0-24/26). RPM Requires and scriptlets are identical.

Co-Authored-By: Claude
```

Until `MONETIZATION_SIGNING_KEY` is set on the protected `release` environment, the release workflow signs nothing and builds keep this bundled file. ## One-time steps for the owner key 1. On your computer, create an Ed25519 key. The commands are in `plugins/plugin-valhalla-copybot/MONETIZATION_KEY.md`. They print only the public key. 2. Store the private key offline. Add the same PEM as the GitHub Actions secret `MONETIZATION_SIGNING_KEY` on an environment named `release`, with your review required before use. 3. Replace the public key in `extension/trust.js` and `src/monetization-trust.ts`, run `scripts/sign-monetization.mjs`, and commit the new signature. 4. body:
## Product Updates

- [ ] Highlight — list the entry UUID(s), or say that the entry is being drafted before this PR receives a number.
- [x] Other — give the concise user-visible change that belongs in the durable disposition.
- [ ] Omit — give the concrete reason this has no announcement value.

Proposed disposition (`other` / `hardening`, draft pending review): Settings → Authentication gains a Login Policy card to switch off password and/or passkey sign-in for non-admins, enforcing IdP-only login. Platform admins stay exempt as the recovery path. Full entry prose will be authored in `product-updates/dispositions/pr-<number>.json` after this PR opens.

Closes #567

## Summary

Implements gobifrost/bifrost#567 per the maintainer's direction (admin exemption, no hidden break-glass page). Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-sso-only-enforcement-design.md`.

- Global `password_login_enabled` / `passkey_login_enabled` policy on `OAuthLoginPreference` (system_configs, no migration; old rows decode to open).
- Server-side 403 gates: `/auth/login`, `/auth/mfa/login`, `/auth/mfa/verify`, `/auth/register`, `/auth/register-from-invite` (password variant), `PUT /profile/password`, passkey authenticate/register options+verify. First-run bootstrap bypasses; device flow untouched; CLI direct password grant is covered by the `/auth/login` gate.
- Guard rails: enabling requires a fully-configured SSO provider; last provider cannot be removed while enforced (409); deleting the default-SSO provider preserves enforcement flags.
- `GET /auth/status` returns real flag values; Login page collapses disabled methods into a visible Platform Admin Sign-In expander; Settings Login Policy card with locked-on admin-exempt notice.
- Sessions are not auto-revoked on flip (documented manual `revoke-all` / `admin/revoke-user` follow-up); existing rate limiters and audit paths reused.

Validation: `quality api` clean; 85 backend unit (incl. contract/dto tripwires) + 31 backend e2e green; client `tsc`, ESLint, vitest 8/8; Playwright `sso-only-login`, `preferred-sso`, `sso-settings-acceptance` (4 passed). `pr-preflight` green except a pre-existing host-missing-`jsonschema` leg, which passes inside the API image (44/44).

Adds simulator specs that update a TRMNL X from older releases to this firmware.

- Stable (the newest tag below this version, v1.8.18 today): updates through the modem on 5 GHz and on 2.4 GHz and keeps its access token.
- The release before stable (v1.8.17 today, which most new X are unboxed on): the same two updates, a retry a day after a failed update, the charger replug out of shipment mode (#695), and a USB flash of this firmware that keeps shipment mode.
- Adds `rake "firmware:build_release[<tag>]"`, which builds a tag's TRMNL_X into `spec/tmp/releases/`. CI builds both releases after the PlatformIO caches are saved and caches them per pair of tags.
- `portal_enable_verbose_logging` accepts a 302, which older captive portals answer instead of 404.
- `ProvisionedX` takes an `image:`, as 1.8.17 reads past the end of a BMP smaller than the panel.

Validated on the sim with `NO_CACHE=1`: 7 examples green. Two are `:smoke`, so CI runs them.

The previous architecture assigned future connected execution to a Python gateway and treated an EA as optional. This documentation-only design makes a fixed, reviewed EA the sole connected broker mutator, with Python proposals and deterministic backend reservations. The implemented Python simulator remains the reference.

Updates the canonical architecture and operating documents; adds ADR-001, a complete observation → candidate → risk → EA → reconciliation → advisor → learning trace, protocol/storage ownership, lost-acknowledgment sequence, state/action matrix, deployment/restore design, migration map and milestone acceptance criteria. Canonical order is now finish M1 → M2A intent/EA protocol → M2B fixed EA execution → M2C deterministic safety → M2D connected PAPER acceptance → M3 baseline/replay → M4 AI/advisor → M5 unattended PAPER → M6 capped LIVE → M7 controlled evolution. Native build/Tester and read-only shadow remain evidence prerequisites within M2B/M2C; connected orders stay disabled until M1 and safety gates pass.

The first proposed implementation PR is explicitly limited to DecisionIntent/ExecutionRequest/ExecutionAck/ExecutionState/ReconciliationResult contracts, shared USD/CAD reference vectors and a fixture-only MQL5 validation/replay harness with submission absent. No implementation, deployment, terminal changes, broker execution or campaign restart occurs here.

Baseline: main adc8640 after merged PRs #13 and #14; no open PRs at inspection. M0A–M0C remain implemented. CMC failed and FOREX/provider campaigns were user-stopped; no sustained acceptance is promoted. Original PAPER limits and the five-second observation/two-second entry distinction remain intact. Fixes #66

v0.9.1 之后的补丁版，把 #65 的修复送到现网：

author: devglawkkj
body:
## Objetivo
Permitir desenvolver o esboço visual do front-end com produtos fictícios e um contrato HTTP estável. A captação real no Mercado Livre fica adiada por orientação do usuário.

## Resultado
- API somente de leitura em /api/v1: health, produtos paginados, detalhe e histórico de preços.
- Busca local literal por título e filtro por categoria; ordenação determinística e limite de 100 itens/página.
- Seis produtos inventados com sete observações cada, seis SVGs locais e links example.invalid, sem consultas externas.
- Campo source explícito: demo, manual ou mercadolivre. Migração preserva dados e referências existentes.
- Serviços de consulta independentes do FastAPI e DTOs explícitos; o futuro coletor alimentará o mesmo banco sem depender do formato de resposta do Mercado Livre.
- Token Bearer gerado no .env local, CORS por origens explícitas, sessões isoladas e erros padronizados sem expor SQL.
- Swagger e OpenAPI gerado e versionado em docs/openapi.json; contrato, exemplos de fetch e comandos Git em docs/api.md.

## Commits
- 8c5b3aa — feat: expose read-only products API with fictional demo data. Implementa API, serviços, dados/assets fictícios, migração e testes.
- 3eb3187 — docs: document demo API and frontend integration contract. Documenta escopo, contrato, execução, erros e conexão futura.
Os corpos dos commits registram motivo e validação.

## Validação
- 44 testes passaram: contrato HTTP, autenticação, CORS, paginação, filtros, detalhe, histórico, seed repetível, falhas sanitizadas e migração com referências existentes, além da suíte anterior.
- Um aviso de depreciação upstream do Starlette TestClient sobre HTTPX; nenhum teste falhou.
- pip check: sem conflitos.
- Migração e seed executados localmente: seis exemplos adicionados.
- alembic check: nenhuma operação adicional detectada.
- git diff origin/main --check: passou; árvore de trabalho limpa.
- .env e banco local continuam ignorados pelo Git.

## Como executar (dentro de afiliados-ml/)
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.lock.txt
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m app.setup_local
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m alembic upgrade head
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m app.seed_demo
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m uvicorn app.api.application:create_app --factory --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --reload
```
Abra http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs e autorize com API_TOKEN do .env. O token não é impresso pelo setup. Para front-end em outra origem, configurar CORS_ORIGINS como lista JSON. Imagens relativas devem ser resolvidas contra a origem da API.

## Escopo e limites
- Não inclui telas, importação JSON/link, coleta real, detecção de descontos, aprovação ou publicações.
- Os exemplos são fictícios, as datas de janeiro de 2026 são fixas e não representam pesquisas reais. A UI deve identificar source=demo e desabilitar compra nesses itens.
- Token compartilhado serve ao desenvolvimento local: não embutir em builds públicos. Hospedagem exigirá autenticação de usuários, HTTPS e política de limites.
- PostgreSQL continua sem testes reais. Reversão da coluna source exige SQLite 3.35+ ou PostgreSQL.
- Nenhuma promessa de acesso irrestrito à API Mercado Livre ou geração automática de links de afiliado.

Aguardar validação explícita antes do merge. Não iniciar integração real nesta etapa.

- Bygget med `vaerktoej-byg-hjemmeside-0311.py` (md5-port på `index.html` fra main = `ae41939a…`).

author: flo91360
body:
## Résumé

Étape 2 de la protection de DefilOrdi : sans clé accordée par un responsable, l’exécutable ne se lance plus (le contrôle côté DefilOrdi suit dans son propre dépôt).

- **Paramètres du projet → Licences** (responsables) : créer une licence (titulaire, postes, date de fin facultative), la désactiver ou la réactiver, libérer ses postes, la supprimer. La clé `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX` n’est affichée qu’à la création ; seule son empreinte est gardée.
- `POST /api/v1/licenses/activate` (public, 30 essais/min par adresse) : clé + produit (dépôt GitHub du projet) + empreinte SHA-256 du poste → jeton signé Ed25519 valable 30 jours, ou jusqu’à la date de fin si elle est plus proche. Le même appel renouvelle le jeton.
- `GET /api/v1/licenses/public-key` : clé publique à intégrer au logiciel. La clé privée est créée au premier besoin et gardée dans la base, comme les clés Web Push.
- La date de fin prépare l’abonnement (étape 3) : un paiement n’aura qu’à la prolonger.
- OpenAPI, `docs/api.md`, version 0.1.101 et changelog.

## Tests

- `tests/licenses.test.js` : création, clé jamais relue, signature vérifiée, limite de postes, autre produit refusé, libération des postes, désactivation, expiration, bail plafonné par la date de fin, suppression.
- Lint, Prettier et tests Node hors worker verts localement (les tests du worker échouent aussi sur `main` dans ce conteneur ; la CI fait foi).

author: root-agent-cloud[bot]
body:
Both starters' AGENTS.md now tell an app's builder how to avoid agent.cloud's review finding `unguarded-schedule` ("Scheduled jobs run in rehearsals too"): on an app granted a lake connection, every scheduled job checks `AGC_RUN` and skips its work, logging that it did, when it's `rehearsal`. This is the starters' part of agent.cloud's root fix for a recurring finding (RFR-10 in agent-cloud's `docs/specs/recurring-findings.md`). The finding was filed on 5 apps in 2 organizations in production.

## What changed

- **SPEC.md DOC-4** (first commit): `AGENTS.md` says a lake app's scheduled jobs skip rehearsals by `AGC_RUN`, and names `unguarded-schedule`. It is proven by `LINT:agents-md`.
- **`typescript/AGENTS.md` and `python/AGENTS.md`**: a new "A scheduled job on a lake app" bullet under "How to add things", next to "A background job". It names each stack's worker loop (`server/worker.ts`, `app/worker.py`) and that stack's schedulers.
- **`conformance/lint/index.ts`**: `LINT:agents-md` fails a stack whose AGENTS.md doesn't name `unguarded-schedule` and `AGC_RUN` (DOC-4). The fixture `node-good/AGENTS.md` has the line, and `lint.test.ts` checks that removing it fails.

## How I proved it

- `cd conformance && node --test test/lint.test.ts test/spec.test.ts`: 5 pass, 0 fail.
- `node run.ts ../typescript --lint-only` and `node run.ts ../python --lint-only`: DOC-2, DOC-3 and DOC-4 pass on both stacks, with 0 MUST failed.

## The release and the pin

The merge releases the next patch, v1.2.5, by itself (`release.yml`). agent-cloud's CLI pin (`packages/cli/src/starters.ts`) has to match the public plugin's pin (`plugin-package-parity.test.ts`), so moving it needs a plugin release. RFR's "Known gaps" says that waits for a person. The agent-cloud pull request below says so too.

## Breaker finding answered

The breaker said this diff adds no early `unguarded-schedule` check. That's on purpose: the early check isn't the starters' job. It is in agent-cloud's pull request: `agc check` warns a lake app, and so does a ship's start (cli-spec SCHED-1). This repository only holds the guidance and the lint that keeps the guidance present.

Companion: summationai/agent-cloud pull request on branch `root/732-recurring-finding-scheduled-jobs-run-in`.

Refs summationai/agent-cloud#4048

body:
## What changed

Asked in a channel for a flow ("a campaign flow of at least ten boxes, passing a derived value…"), Claude answered that none of its tools could build or propose a flow and wrote the design out in words. Two things stood in its way:

- The instructions the site serves (`ws_claude_routine_prompt()`) list the kinds Claude may put in its answer's `changes`, and no flow among them.
- Its channel answer (`ws_api_claude_answer()`) checks the changes with `ws_changes_input()` without the proposal flag, which refuses `{type: flow}`; only an application's `workspace.changes.propose` took a flow draft.

Now:

- `ws_changes_input()` takes a sixth argument `$drafts`: a flow draft is taken with `$for_proposal || $drafts`. Claude's channel answer passes it; a run on a task does not (no canvas there), and nothing else changes for proposals or Pinegrap AI.
- The served instructions get a flow section: read `GET /workspace/flow-kinds`, put the flow into `changes` as `{"type": "flow", "action": "draft", "data": {name, nodes [{id, kind, label, config}], edges [{from, to, on}]}, "reason"}`; box ids, one start box with no arrow into it, outcomes per kind, an approval box for a yes-or-no question, `{{node.ID.VALUE}}` / `{{trigger.FIELD}}`, no x and y; the person opens and publishes it, never "set up". Served by the site, so nothing is pasted again on claude.ai.
- `ws_flow_draft_proposal_input()` lays out boxes sent all in one place (`ws_flow_draft_unplaced()`: none given or the same x and y, more than one box) with `ws_flow_auto_layout()`, as Pinegrap AI's drafts are; boxes with places of their own keep them. This holds for an application's proposal too.

The draft is checked and kept by the same `ws_flow_draft_proposal_row()` (the asker's rights, `ws_flow_save_check()`), shown as the same draft card, opened and published by the person.

## Tests

- New `tests/workspace_claude_flow_drafts_test.php`: the instructions' flow section; the channel answer passes `$drafts`, the task run does not; `ws_changes_input()` reads either flag; unplaced boxes laid out (none given, all at 0, 0), placed ones kept.
- `tests/workspace_flow_draft_test.php`: `test_ws_flow_draft_input_boxes` now sends placed boxes, which come through as sent.
- Run: `php tools/test.php workspace_flow` (526), `workspace_claude` (14), `workspace_scheduled` (66), `api_` (803), `check_lang.php`, `check_api_schema.php`, `memory_index.php --check`.

## Could not verify

- Claude's own run against dev with the new instructions (after this lands and dev is synced).

## Memory
