author: jolley71717
body:
A player reported a loud, nonstop engine/generator-like noise that only they heard. It started each time a friend's NPC line (or Dogmeat's) showed at the top left, every new line added to it, and turning the volume down did nothing.

**Cause (likely, not proven in a game).** A friend's line is played as a plain 3D sound from its voice file (`Conversations::Play`). I read the engine's own actor voice calls in the game's code (Address Library 2229972 and 2229973, 1.11.240). They play `sound\` + the response's file through the same `BSAudioManager::GetSoundHandleByFile`, with the same usage flag 0x10 (plus 0x80 with priority 128, and 0x4000 in one case). The audio manager's file source (2267597) skips a .fuz's `FUZE` header and lip data on its own. So our flag and our .fuz are not what differs. What differs is the end. The engine sets the speaker's voice timer from the recording's length (`GetDuration`), and the line ends when the timer runs out. Our sound was only ever ended by that same speaker's next line. Worse, it was dropped from our list, with no way left to end it, as soon as the audio manager stopped reporting it as playing. So if a sound in a player's setup doesn't end on its own (a voice file that decodes as an endless buzz or loop, which a localized or repacked voice archive could cause), it runs forever, and every other speaker adds another. That matches the report. I couldn't find out from here what makes that one player's files behave that way.

**Fix** (`src/game/LineSounds.h`, used by `Conversations`):
- Every line's sound has a hard end: the recording's length read from its file (SubtitleTime) plus 1 s, between 2.5 s and 240 s (companions have 35-38 s lines; Magnolia's songs run to 214 s). If the length can't be read, the end is 15 s. The length comes from the start of the file that actually plays (lip sync and RIFF header only). Sounds are kept until that end and are never dropped early on the audio manager's say-so.
- At most 4 play at once; a fifth line ends the oldest. A speaker's next line still ends the one before.
- A sound that was made but never played is released.
- When a cut sound was still playing, an info line is logged (at most one per 30 s, with how many were skipped) (player N and the speaker's form ID, no names). Net status shows `sounds=`, `cutLong=` and `cutCrowded=` in the conversations part.

**Other sounds that play when a HUD line shows.** `Hud::Notify` passes no sound to `ShowHUDMessage`. Replayed gunshots already have a hard end (`ShotLoops::LONGEST_SHOT`, 6 s), and they don't come with HUD lines. `DoorShare.h` only lists scripts and plays nothing. Only DevCommands, WeaponFire and Conversations play sounds through the audio manager. Voice chat doesn't come with HUD lines.

No protocol or session-layout change.

**Tested:** unit tests for the bookkeeping (`tests/LineSoundsTests.cpp`); full suite 2645 tests, 0 failed. Not tested in a game.

body:
Audit finding: @sentry/electron enables console and network breadcrumbs by default. Vault logged search text to the console, and the Google, OneDrive and Dropbox request URLs hold search terms and folder IDs, so crash reports could contain them. That contradicts the privacy policy ("no file names, search queries").

- Main process: beforeBreadcrumb keeps only category electron (app and window events); drops console, http and fetch.
- Renderer: all breadcrumbs dropped.
- Removed console.log of the search query.
- sendDefaultPii: false made explicit.

Not covered: exception messages themselves (they could in theory quote a name from an API error). None of Vault code builds an error message from a file name or query.

Typecheck: only the existing import.meta.env and FileList errors. Goes into v1.0.3.

author: luender
body:
## Problema

Quem saía de uma competição só podia se reinscrever antes do início. Quem saía depois do início perdia a vaga de vez, mesmo com a competição ainda em andamento.

## Mudança

A reinscrição agora vale até o fim da competição. A competição precisa estar `SCHEDULED`, `ACTIVE` ou `PAUSED` e não ter passado da data de término.

**O que continua igual:**
- A saída segue bloqueada quando há pelo menos 1 vídeo enviado, inclusive depois de voltar.
- Inscrição removida por advertência (`REVOKED`) não pode ser reaberta.
- Em competição privada, só o admin reinscreve, e a inscrição volta para aprovação. Essa regra é compartilhada, então o admin também passa a poder reinscrever depois do início.
- Competição com aprovação volta para `PENDING`. PRO e banimento continuam sendo validados.

**Ajustes vindos da review:**
- Depois de voltar, as listas do card e do envio de post são atualizadas na hora, em vez de ficarem até 60s defasadas.
- Se a inscrição mudar durante a espera pelo lock, o clipador recebe um pedido para recarregar a página, e não a mensagem de reinscrição encerrada.

**Textos e audit:**
- Atualizei o aviso do diálogo de saída e as mensagens de erro.
- A ação de audit passa de `reenroll_before_competition_start` para `reenroll_after_withdrawal`. Nenhum código lê esse valor, e os registros antigos ficam como estão.

## Impacto em produção

- Não há migração nem SQL.
- Hoje há 265 saídas em competições abertas que passam a poder voltar.
- Nenhum ranking é reescrito: das 516 saídas em produção, nenhuma tem vídeo, e os registros de saída não têm entradas de ranking desqualificadas.
- A restauração de entradas desqualificadas pela saída agora vale só para rankings ainda abertos. Os que fecharam durante a ausência ficam como estão.

## Testes

- `vitest`: 738 passaram e 30 foram ignorados
- `tsc --noEmit` e `eslint` nos arquivos alterados, sem erros
- Novos testes cobrem o limite no instante de término e o fluxo de voltar, enviar vídeo e tentar sair, que continua bloqueado

Não testei pela tela logada do clipador.

body: Status: in progress (Draft) ## Why An Owner or Admin with several Environments in one Organization saw the switcher as a column of "Pracovní", each with "přiřazeno @login" beside it, and could not find a colleague's Environment at a glance. The Owner approved a switcher where the main word of a row is whose the Environment is and the kind moves into a group heading. ## What changes - **Rows** (`switcherList`, `view.ts`; drawn in `elements.ts`): - A work Environment assigned to a person: round GitHub photo (`githubPhoto`, initials when it does not load), the person's name in bold, the whole `@login` under it. Nothing is cut: the row wraps and the picker's list is at least 320 px wide. - A Team Environment: the users icon, the Team's name, "Týmové Prostředí" under it. - Server services, an Automated Environment and other work that belongs to no person: an icon (a building, or the bot) and its name, with the Dashboard's line of whom it is for (`who`) under it. - **Headings** Lidé / People (yours first), Týmy / Teams, Organizace / Organization; an empty one is not shown; within a group the document's (account's) order. Personal Environments and your computer stay in the personal space as before. Your computer, when it carries an Organization, is listed under People (it is yours). - **The same headings in the widened list and in the jump (⌘⇧E)**, nested under each Organization's title or head. A row no longer says its kind, so a list without the headings would lose it. - **Accessibility:** each group is `role="group"` with `aria-labelledby` its heading; the rows stay one list for ↑↓, Home, End and Enter, and `start` is unchanged: under the ordinary picker the current Environment (now counted in the groups' order); in the widened picker ("Všechny Organizace"), in a search and in the jump (⌘⇧E) the first entry. Search also matches the person's login and name and the heading's word. - **Column head, ``, the Environment browser's bar and title** share `environmentIdentity`: the person's photo and name over "Pracovní Prostředí"; every other Environment its name and its kind as a label ("Týmové Prostředí"), left out where the name is the kind's own word. In the 264 px column the picker's glyph box is its 24 px mark and its gaps 8 px, so a name of about twenty characters and "Pracovní Prostředí" show whole (measured with the vendored Inter Tight: 125 px for the text, neither line overflows); a longer name wraps to a second line and is cut only after it, and the button's `title` holds the whole identity. - **Who the person is:** - `assigneeName?: string` is an additive, optional member of an Environment in `lazurio.shell.v1` and `lazurio.account.v1`, through the one parser of both documents. It is kept only beside an `assignee`. Any other value is left out rather than refusing the Environment. - `described` in `merge.ts` takes it from the account like `name`, only for the same assignee, and keeps it in another language. - Main word: a name of its own (an Admin's rename or the person's label, the Dashboard's `name`) wins; the Dashboard's default "Pracovní"/"Work", or a name that only restates the login or the person's name, never does. Then the person's name, then the login. Under a name of its own: the person's name and `@login`. The Dashboard's "přiřazeno @login" is never shown under a person. - **Identity message (C9):** the glyph gains the kind `person` and the icon `building`; a view of an older release does not read them and draws the identity its own server gave. - **Decision record:** F36 addendum of 2026-11-03 in `docs/decisions.md`, recording that this changes "Druh Prostředí stačí" (root 0170's addendum of 2026-10-15) for the switcher and the column head, and that the root rule needs a follow-up addendum of its own. Base: `origin/main`, independent of the Accept-Language fix PR (that one makes the Dashboard's `name`/`who` arrive in the Environment's language; this one is presentation and the contract member). ## Verification - `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint` and `bun run check:public` pass. - `bun test` over every shell suite and the related Launchpad and browser-view suites (`shell*`, `environment-browser-view*`, `apps-view`, `environment-wording`, `launchpad-boot`, `launchpad-mausbot`, `first-run-*`, `public-*`, `server-services-*`, `try-overlay-preset`, `browser-contract-vectors`, `shell-interface`): all pass. The new `tests/shell-picker-owners.test.ts` adds 11 tests; the identity, picker, account, host, shell and browser-view tests are updated to the new naming. - Visual check: the shell bundle (`bun build src/shell/index.ts`) on a local host page with neutral fixture data, in the Environment browser. The picker, the jump and English were checked; screenshots are kept outside the repository. ## What stays open - **Dashboard:** send `assigneeName` (the assigned person's profile name) in `lazurio.account.v1`. Until then rows show the login. - **Root decision 0170:** "Druh Prostředí stačí" needs a follow-up addendum matching this one. - A person's Environment in words (a tab's title) now names the person, not the Organization. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) > [!NOTE] > ### Group Environment switcher rows by People, Teams, and Organization, led by the assignee > - Person-assigned work Environments now display the assignee's name, GitHub photo, and initials, with the Environment kind label beneath. The identity comes from `environmentOwner` and `ownerTitle` in [view.ts](https://github.com/Lazurio/LazurioPlatform/pull/845/files#diff-dcf79ec79048a8f9a9a4c1912ac6818077778708d15e81ad857cfc5ba4d11711). > - Organization switcher sections are partitioned into People, Teams, and Organization groups; the viewer's own assigned Environments and workstations appear first in People. - Fix: ``--fail-under`` now uses at least the decimal precision of the
  threshold for both the comparison and failure message.  With ``precision=0``,
  a total of 0.4 now passes ``--fail-under=0.3`` and fails ``--fail-under=0.5``
  with the message "total of 0.4 is less than fail-under=0.5".  Previously, the
  comparison rounded the total to zero and the message could claim "1 is less
  than 0". Closes `issue 2295`_.

- Fix: the HTML report escaped file names twice, so a name with ``&``, ``<``,
  or quotes in it was shown with entities like ``&amp;``. Now they are properly
  escaped only once.

- Fix: ``--source=/`` measured no files. A file system root can't be a source
  directory, so now it is an error. Closes `issue 2291`_.

- In an abundance of caution, prevent forged SQLite journal files from deleting
  files they shouldn't.

.. _issue 2167: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2167
.. _issue 2291: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2291
.. _issue 2295: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2295
.. _issue 2337: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2337


.. _changes_7-17-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.17.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 3.10.

- Binary wheels are now provided for iOS and Android. This allows the use of
  the optimized C tracer on mobile platforms.

- Fix: three or more levels of nested ``with`` statements could make a ``with``
  line look like a branch with an exit that can never happen. Using the
  sys.monitoring core, these phantom branches were reported as partial. Other
  cores hid the problem but still counted the phantom branches in the total.
  Closes `issue 1987`_.

- Fix: a comment or string that merely mentioned ``if True:`` or
  ``while True:`` could mark its line as a branch that is known to be partial,
  so a branch that never ran was reported as taken.  These built-in patterns
  now only match at the start of the statement. Closes `issue 2314`_.

- Fix: region detection missed functions defined in unusual places, such as
  ``else`` and ``except`` clauses. This is now fixed.

- Fix: recent versions of the lcov tool complain if the same function name
  appears more than once in a report. Python can have multiple same-named
  functions in a few ways, for example, getters/setters or conditionally
  defined functions. These are now disambiguated by adding a ``<line number>``
  suffix to the function name. Fixes `issue 2335`.

- Fix: The "Can't combine statement coverage data with branch data" error now
  names the two data files it couldn't combine. The :ref:`error description
  <error_cant_combine>` in the docs now lists common causes and how to find the
  process that wrote the file.

- Fix: at coverage totals close to 0 or 100, the XML report could get incorrect
  ``line-rate`` values like ``8.333e-05`` or ``1``. This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 2293`_ and `issue 2294`_.

- Fix: a parallel data file saved more than once kept the hash of its first
  save in its file name. Combining could then skip it as a duplicate of another
  file that had the same data at that point, and delete it, losing the data
  recorded after the first save. Each save now updates the hash. This had been
  a problem since 7.13.1. Fixes `issue 2338`_.

- Fixes for obscure but legal file names:

  - File names (and plugin names) can contain control characters, which are
    legal in POSIX paths but unsafe in reports: in XML 1.0 they make the
    document non-well-formed, and in a terminal they act as escape sequences
    (colors, title/clipboard sequences, cursor moves that forge output). Now
    the XML report, the text and Markdown summary reports, and ``coverage debug
    data`` replace non-printable characters in names. Printable names are
    unchanged.

  - A file pattern (from ``include``, ``omit``, or a ``[paths]`` alias)
    containing a newline sent the glob-to-regex translation into an infinite
    loop, hanging the process. Newlines in patterns are now handled like any
    other character.

- Fixes in the implementation of the C tracer:

  - If a plugin's ``dynamic_source_filename`` method raised an exception, lines
    in that function could be recorded as belonging to a different file. Also
    fixed some minor memory leaks in the C tracer.

  - The refcount of ``None`` was mismanaged during function calls, including
    comprehensions. This was unlikely to cause an actual problem, but is now
    fixed. Thanks, Andrew Dalke.

  - The C tracer held borrowed references to dictionary values, which was
    unsafe on free-threaded Python.  Now it takes its own references.

  - An internal error while recording a new file could be reported as a
    confusing ``SystemError`` instead of the actual exception.

- Performance: the text summary report (``coverage report``) held on to every
  file's parsed source until it finished, so its memory use grew with the size
  of the project: ten times or more what 7.14 used on large projects.  Now it
  keeps only what it needs to print. Fixes `issue 2277`_.

- Performance: HTML reports should be about 5% faster to produce.

- Kept the political banner in the README. Closes `issue 2344`_.

   ---------------------------

- Fix: on Python 3.14 and later, a ``for`` loop completing immediately before a
  function return could mistakenly report an uncovered branch. This is now
  fixed, closing `issue 2168`_.

- Fix: on Python 3.14 and later, the ``else`` clause of a ``try`` whose body is
  a ``with`` statement could incorrectly be reported as covered when the
  ``with`` raised.  This is now fixed, closing `issue 2289`_.

- Fix: with ``dynamic_context = test_function``, test methods written as
  ``staticmethod`` or ``classmethod`` were not given a context of their own.
  Now they are, on Python 3.11 and later.  Closes `issue 1923`_.

body:
Ledger #3034. A renamed worker loop keeps one row on the Dashboard's Agents tab, and an old name that meant two loops splits at a date. ```toml gonk.holder.alias = "lawnboy -> lawnboy-claude before 2026-10-21" gonk.holder.alias = "lawnboy -> lawnboy-codex" ``` ## What I reproduced `tests/holder_alias_3034.rs` was written first and run against the code with the rules parsed but not yet applied. 5 of its 6 tests failed: - `two_holders_fold_into_one_row`: rows were `["new-name", "old-name", "other"]`, wanted `["new-name", "other"]`. - `a_time_bound_splits_one_old_name_across_two_rows`: rows were `["machine", "machine-two"]`, wanted `["machine-one", "machine-two"]`. The sixth test, no rules means no change, passed before and after, as it should. ## What changed - **`src/holders.rs` (new)** parses the rules. First match wins, and a date is the UTC midnight it starts, with `before` excluding it. Refused at start, naming the line: - no arrow - a bad date - a row with a space in it, which is what catches a typo like `befor 2026-10-21` - a rule that could never match - **`src/agents.rs`** writes the rules into the SPARQL the tab asks. Each `?holder` becomes its own variable, with a `VALUES` of the names that may sign that row and a `FILTER` on that event's own time. One text produces both the number and its link. - **`urn:iki:gonk:agent`** lists rows rather than signatures, through the same rules. No ledger record is written. - **Stored questions:** `in-flight.rq` and `worked-on.rq` now also select the time they date a signature by. `agents.rq` gains a prefix. - **Page text:** a table with aliases says which apply, in a `

` before the table. - **Docs:** the README has the configuration line and a section on it. `ACCESSIBILITY.md` has a new evidence row and a history row. ## Decisions to check - **The sentence is per table, not one line over the tab.** It names only rules whose row that table shows, so a reader of one ledger does not learn the loop names of a ledger they cannot read. A caller who already knows a row's name can still see that row's rules in its link's query, through a ledger they can read. - **Rules take one step.** With `a -> b` and `b -> c`, `a`'s events land in row `b` and `b`'s in row `c`. This is documented; name the final row in each rule. - **An old name asked for directly** (`urn:iki:gonk:agent:holder:lawnboy`) answers for whatever no rule takes from it, which is zero with the two rules above. It is never the whole history. - **Held items are dated by `ledger:claimedAt`, which a renewal moves.** A claim taken before a rule's date and renewed after it counts in the later row. - **Two stored questions got stricter for every holder, not only aliased ones.** `in-flight` now needs `ledger:claimedAt` on the item and `worked-on` needs `dcterms:created` on the claim event. The ledger writes both on a claim. An item or event somehow lacking one would stop being counted. I did not check this against a real ledger's data. - **A claim event with no `dcterms:created` drops out of the agents list** once any rule is configured, for the same reason. ## How CI proves it `tests/holder_alias_3034.rs` runs over real HTTP: - two holders folded into one row, with the raw `claimedBy` records unchanged - the time bound splitting one old name, including the last second before the cut and the first second of it - every column's click-through query returning the number the row shows, for each folded row - the median joining a claim and a hand-back across a rename - the per-table sentence, and no sentence with no rules - a folded row with 1,500 hand-backs answering every question Unit tests in `src/holders.rs`, `src/config.rs` and `src/agents.rs` cover the malformed rules, that every stored question folds and parses, and that a holder no rule touches gets byte-identical query text. By hand on the real binary, both a rule with no arrow and a rule with a bad date exit 1 at start, naming the line. ## Measured Each question for one row with 1,500 hand-backs, once each after a write, on a debug build: | Question | Plain | Folded | |---|---|---| | in-flight | 4 ms | 7 ms | | worked-on | 35 ms | 39 ms | | completed-24h | 10 ms | 15 ms | | completed-7d | 9 ms | 15 ms | | handed-back-24h | 6 ms | 7 ms | | released | 56 ms | 68 ms | | median-claim-to-handback | 95 ms | 99 ms | ## Not done - No browser, axe or screen-reader run on the new sentence (`deno` is not on this machine). It uses the markup of the table's other notes, plus a small margin before the table. `ACCESSIBILITY.md` says no browser has run on it. - This does not set Brian's `holder` line or add these rules to any live config; that is the operator's step. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

# Pull Request

## Summary

- SR-7 (server review finding VO-2, ledger OC-0547): a moderator move of a member whose call is held in the 15 s reconnect grace window used to end the call and drop the server mute/deafen. Now the move is kept for that device session; its resume receives `voice_moved` and re-joins the destination with the flags restored.

## Changes

- `ws/voice_grace_modmove.go` (new): `parkedModMove` kept per user in `voiceGraceState` (session token hash, flags, queued frames, time, collected). TTL = grace window, at most 4 frames.
- `EvictForModeratorMove`: after tearing down a parked call, records the kept move with the flags.
- `SendToVoiceDevice`: keeps the frame on a kept move; reports true when that is its delivery, otherwise (already collected) falls through to the stamped connection.
- `registerNow`: a resume of the same session collects a copy of the move (stamps the connection as the moderator target, stashes the flags, sends the frames). A fresh connect drops it; another session never takes it. Collecting does not use the move up, so a resume whose connection dies before re-joining leaves it for the next resume inside the window.
- `takeUserModFlags` (every `voice_join`): ends the kept move and carries its flags when no connection has any, so a join on another device is never pulled away by a later resume.
- Any later moderator exit (`noteModeratorExit`) and a flag clear (`SetPendingVoiceModFlags(false,false)`, the handler's failure path) forget the kept move; `close()` clears them.
- Audit is `voice_mod_move` for this case now. AFK moves are unchanged (they already skip parked connections).
- Docs: `docs/protocol.md` (voice_mod_move), `docs/architecture/websocket.md` (voice membership), CHANGELOG, ledger OC-0547.

## Pre-flight

- Affected files: `Server/ws/voice_grace_modmove.go` (+test), `voice_grace.go`, `voice_moderation_move.go`, `voice_join_move.go`, `voice_moderation.go`, `hub_registry.go`, `multi_device_test.go`, `voice_moderation_test.go`, docs above, ledger.
- State mutations: `voiceGraceState.modMoves` (grace leaf lock; written by the moderator move under the target's member lock, read by `SendToVoiceDevice` without it, collected by `registerNow` and ended by `voice_join` under the member lock); `Client.voiceExitAt` (atomic, set on collect); the new connection's mod-flag stash (`voiceSlot.voiceMu`).
- Edge case 1, handled and tested: the resume registers between the eviction and the `voice_moved` send. The collect stamps the new connection under the same lock the queueing takes, so the frame is either kept for it or finds it by its stamp (`TestVoiceMembership_ParkedMoveResumeBeforeSend`).
- Edge case 2, handled and tested: a reconnect that supersedes the parked session. A fresh connect or another session does not collect the move (`TestVoiceMembership_ParkedMoveDroppedByFreshConnect`, parked case of `TestMultiDevice_ModeratorFramesReachOnlyTheCallDevice`); a join on another device ends it and keeps the mute (`TestMultiDevice_JoinElsewhereEndsAParkedMove`); a failed resume leaves it for the next one (`TestVoiceMembership_ParkedMoveSurvivesFailedResume`). Stale and cleared moves are dropped (`TestVoiceMembership_ParkedMoveExpiresWithWindow`).

## Process

- Built by: main session
- Review: opus-reviewer (voice lifecycle). It raised two items, both fixed in the second commit: a kept move surviving a join on another device, and a move used up by a resume whose handshake then failed.

## Test Plan

- [x] 4 build-tag variants build; `go vet ./ws/`
- [x] `go test -race ./ws/` green (577 s, first commit); targeted voice/grace/multi-device tests green with `-race` and `-tags deadlock` after the review commit; full CI green on the head
- [x] golangci-lint 2.14.0 on `ws` (default + guardrail linters with otel,wazero): 0 issues; invariants, comment-id guard, ledger check, prettier on edited docs
- [ ] Manual testing: none (covered by the grace-window harness tests)
- [x] No generated files touched
- [x] Docs updated

## Scope

Not included:
- A moderator kick of a parked member still delivers nothing on resume (the replayed `voice_leave` already takes them out of voice); not part of VO-2.
- A moderator stash on a connection that never re-joins has no expiry. That is the existing live-move behaviour too; worth a small follow-up, not this PR.

body:
## Summary

With Obsidian's **Settings > General > Advanced > Command line interface** setting off, the CLI answers every command with exit 0 and the stdout notice `Command line interface is not enabled. Please turn it on in Settings > General > Advanced.` The notice has no `Error:` prefix, so `dispatchOnce` resolved it as success. Each layer then treated it as its own normal output: `obsidian_exec` returned it as output, `read` as the note's content, the vault registry as an empty vault list (so `vaults` gave `{count: 0}` and named-vault calls failed "is not registered"), and eval-backed tools failed with an opaque `json-parse` error. This PR fixes BI-0132 with one dispatch rule, which every surface inherits. It took spec-kit's bug path: `/speckit-bug-assess` → `/speckit-bug-fix` → `/speckit-bug-test`.

> **Verification result: partial.** The automated checks pass, and a live probe with the setting **ON** came back clean. Verification with the setting **OFF** is still to come: live reproduction, live capture of the notice wording, and OFF→ON recovery are open, owner-run checks (owner ruling 2026-11-04, recorded under Status on BI-0132 and in `test.md` "Residual Risks").

**Records** (these stand in for the spec, plan and tasks):
- Assessment: [`.specify/bugs/bi-0132/assessment.md`](https://github.com/marwansaab/obsidian-cli-mcp/blob/fix/bi-0132/.specify/bugs/bi-0132/assessment.md)
- Fix report: [`.specify/bugs/bi-0132/fix.md`](https://github.com/marwansaab/obsidian-cli-mcp/blob/fix/bi-0132/.specify/bugs/bi-0132/fix.md)
- Test report: [`.specify/bugs/bi-0132/test.md`](https://github.com/marwansaab/obsidian-cli-mcp/blob/fix/bi-0132/.specify/bugs/bi-0132/test.md): `partial`, accepted by the owner (2026-11-04)

| Surface, command line OFF | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `obsidian_exec` (with or without `vault`) | success envelope, stdout = notice | `CLI_REPORTED_ERROR`, `details.reason: "cli-disabled"`, notice in `details.stdout` |
| `read` and other plain typed tools | notice returned as content | same failure |
| eval-backed tools | `CLI_REPORTED_ERROR` `stage: "json-parse"` | same failure |
| `vaults` | `{count: 0, vaults: []}` | same failure |
| named-vault calls (registry lookup) | `VALIDATION_ERROR` "is not registered" / `VAULT_NOT_FOUND` `unknown` | same failure |
| Output that merely contains the notice's words | success | success (unchanged) |
| Setting ON | normal | normal (unchanged) |

- **Dispatch** (`src/cli-adapter/_dispatch.ts`): `CLI_DISABLED_ANSWER` is exported beside `UNKNOWN_VAULT_ANSWER`. `dispatchOnce` rejects when `stdout.trim()` is exactly the notice, after priority (a) and before the other exit-0 rules. The error is `CLI_REPORTED_ERROR` with `exitZeroDetails(…)` plus `reason: "cli-disabled"`, and its message asks the user to turn the setting on. It matches neither `COLD_START_PATTERN` nor the app-not-running signature, so it is single-shot: no retry, no auto-launch. The registry caches nothing on failure, so recovery after the user turns the setting back on needs no restart.
- **Exact match** (assessment Q2, the BA's answer; unchanged when the partial result was accepted): no prefix match, so a note that starts with the sentence is not misclassified.
- **Discriminator** (Q3, ADR-015): a flat `details.reason: "cli-disabled"` under the existing code, following `obsidian-not-running`. There is no new top-level code.
- **Guidance**: `closedVaultNote` and eight `docs/tools` pages no longer give "its command-line integration is disabled" as a cause of the `Error: Command "<cmd>" not found.` failure; TC-00495 contradicts it. The README Errors section (the canonical place), `obsidian_exec.md` and `vaults.md` document the cli-disabled failure.

### Notes for the reviewer

1. **Partial result, accepted** (test.md "Residual Risks"). Three OFF-state checks are open for an owner-run session: (1) live reproduction with `obsidian_exec files total`, `read`, `vaults` and one named-vault call that resolves through the registry; (2) live capture of the notice, compared with `CLI_DISABLED_ANSWER`; (3) OFF→ON recovery in one session. The pinned notice comes from the single 2026-05-30 probe (TC-00495). If Obsidian's wording differs, the rule silently stays inert, which is no worse than before this PR. The fix then is to correct the constant and its fixture, keeping the exact match.
2. **Deliberate published-surface change**: the FR-018 baseline was regenerated (`npm run baseline:write`). Exactly the nine `closedVaultNote` tools' description fingerprints moved: bases, create_base, paths, pattern_search, query_base, smart_connections_query, smart_connections_similar, tag, views_base.
3. **Deviation** (`fix.md`): the registry case is tested in `vaults/handler.test.ts` with a `vi.fn` probe that rejects twice with a cli-disabled `UpstreamError`, the form the assessment's "Tests to add" describes. Review removed a first version that copied `server.ts`'s `invokeProbe` wiring by hand. The dispatch classification itself is checked in `cli-adapter.test.ts`, and `registry.test.ts` already covers generic probe-failure retry. No existing assertion changed.
4. **Left for docs-as-code**: `.docs-as-code/architecture.md` (~line 811) and the ADR-045 page (~line 46) still repeat the disabled-integration example. BI-0174 item 3 should follow this outcome rather than reword the same sentence.

## Evidence

- **Tests**: 15 new cases. `_dispatch.test.ts` covers the notice with LF, without a newline and with CRLF (full `details`, one spawn, no launch), eval, three contains-the-words successes, and a fixture pin against `CLI_DISABLED_ANSWER` and `COLD_START_PATTERN`. `invoke-bounded-cli.test.ts` covers `obsidian_exec` with and without `vault`. `cli-adapter.test.ts` covers `invokeCli`, `invokeEval`, and the unknown-vault rule unaffected. `read/handler.test.ts` shows no content and no disk read. `vaults/handler.test.ts` shows `vaults` and `resolveVaultPath` rejecting with the same cli-disabled error object from a stubbed probe, then recovering in the same registry.
- **Live, setting ON** (read-only, TestVault-Obsidian-CLI-MCP): raw `Obsidian.com files total` → exit 0, `807`. This branch's `dist/` was then driven through the facades and through the full server over an in-memory MCP client: `obsidian_exec`, `read Welcome.md`, `invokeEval`, `vaults`, registry `resolveVaultPath`, and `find_and_replace` preview. All returned normal results.
- **Not exercised live**: anything with the setting OFF (note 1).
- **Structural check** (CodeGraph, recorded in `fix.md`): no new error code or class, no DI factory import, `CLI_DISABLED_ANSWER` reachable from `dispatchOnce`, imports one-directional; no kernel node touched.

## Test results

- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`) and `npm run build` pass.
- `npm test` (coverage gate): 4854 passed, 6 skipped (+15 new, 0 regressions). Coverage: statements 97.09%.

## Constitution Compliance

| Gate | Status | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| Principle I — Modular Code Organization | Y | The rule lives in `cli-adapter/_dispatch.ts`, the module that owns the CLI answer signatures. The facades, handlers and `server.ts` are unchanged. New test imports run downward (`tools` → `cli-adapter`). |
| Principle II — Public Surface Test Coverage | Y | Failure and boundary cases co-located with each changed path: dispatch, both facades, `read`, `vaults` plus registry. Happy paths pass unchanged. |
| Principle III — Boundary Input Validation with Zod | N/A | No input schema changes. |
| Principle IV — Explicit Upstream Error Propagation | Y | A silent false success becomes an `UpstreamError` with stable `code` / `cause` / `details`, returned as `isError: true`. No new top-level code. |
| Principle V — Attribution & Layered Composition | Y | Edited files keep their `// Original — no upstream.` headers; no new source file. |
| ADR-010 / ADR-013 | N/A | No tool added or renamed. |
| ADR-014 | N/A | Not plugin-backed. |
| ADR-015 | Y | `cli-dis

author: movieholic-plex
body:
## 요약
몬스터 전투 도트 시트 칸 128·192·256(3×3·4×4)을 스토어·프로젝트 업로드에서 받고, 전투에서 크고 통째로 그린다.

- 스토어 형식·프로젝트 meta 타입·업로드 파서가 칸 128/192/256 을 받는다.
- `battleEnemyFit`: 칸 > 96 시트는 배율과 무관하게 맞춤을 잰다. 위 한계는 적 무리 상자 위끝(안내 창 아래), 발은 통째로 들어갈 만큼만 내린다(전장 아래 여백·이름표 바닥을 넘지 않음).
- 큰 시트 적은 뒷줄 왼쪽 끝에 서고, 나머지 진형은 모양 그대로 오른쪽으로 밀린다 — 보스가 작은 적을 덮지 않는다.
- 칸 48/64/96 · 100% 이하는 지금과 같은 기하이고 레이아웃을 읽지 않는다.
- 공방 생성기는 48/64/96 만 그리므로, 128+ 시트 재생성 요청은 `unsupported-cell` 로 거절한다.

## Summary
Accept 128/192/256-cell monster battle sheets (3x3 and 4x4) from the store and project uploads, and draw them large and whole in battle.

- Store format, project meta type and upload parser accept cell 128/192/256.
- `battleEnemyFit`: sheets with cell > 96 are always measured; top limit is the enemy group top (below the help window); feet drop only as far as needed, never past the field bottom gutter or the name-plate floor.
- A big-sheet enemy takes the back-left seat and the rest of the formation shifts right as a group, so the boss never covers small enemies.
- 48/64/96 sheets at <=100% keep today's geometry and skip the layout read.
- The editor pixel studio only draws 48/64/96, so regenerating a 128+ sheet is refused with `unsupported-cell`.

## 실측 / Measured (1440×900, 480×270 at 3×, stage px)
| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 96 @125% | 120, fit 1 | 120, fit 1 |
| 128 @100% | rejected (flat portrait 52×63) | 128, fit 1 |
| 192 @100% (4×4) | rejected | 141, fit 0.734 |
| 256 @100% | rejected | 141, fit 0.551 |
| 256 @100% + 2 slimes | rejected | boss 141, slimes 64, no overlap, all inside field |

Tests: `test/enemyPixelSheet16.test.ts` (big-cell store accept), `test/runtimeLagFixes2.test.ts` (128+ measures layout; 96 still skips). Typecheck: `typecheck:app` exit 0.

author: joshmann-inversionsemi
body:
Makes the additions to `inversion-fbpic`:
- Add mathematical expression interpreting, `MathExpression` (basic Python operators via `ast`, as well as `numpy` and `scipy` methods)
- Add a `ExpressionDensityProfile` which takes a `MathExpression` as the density profile
- Add a `_ParticleBeam` class for PWFA (or other) simulations, covering `fbpc.lpa_utils.bunch`; includes a `ExpressionParticleBeam` class which takes in a `MathExpression`
- Add FBPIC particle-beam diagnostics and beam-aware moving-window beta resolution.
- Permit laser-only and beam-only simulations; only background gas/plasma-only simulations are excluded
- Add a PWFA downramp-injection demo with post-processing.

A couple notes:
For the purposes of permitting users to use general methods to describe density and beam profiles, a limited `MathExpression` was preferred over an alternative native Python method + pickling scheme. Pickling would prevent the method from being readable or modifiable in its serialized form. It also brings potential security issues alla arbitrary code execution. I think we could and should extend support for this scheme, either with additional security measures or an insistent warning to the user, for the case that more complex logic is desired for the generation of these profiles. In the meantime, the `MathExpression` scheme should cover most practical cases.
A gap in the logic for determining a sufficient element configuration for a running simulation, where lacking a `_DensityProfile` is permitted, was left. In PR #37 , a `simulation_length` parameter was introduced. Once PR #37 is merged, this parameter is sufficient to replace the otherwise required `_DensityProfile` class. Presently valid simulations will still be valid whether this PR or PR #37 is merged first.

author: kravetsin
body:
The tracker on the shin and the regen suit's lit bands now cast their light on what is near them, through the lightmap, using the treatment the user picked (`cast`). Nothing glows in the air itself.

- **Tracker:** casts the player's colour within 3 cells, always.
- **Regen suit:** each lit band gives white-violet light at its wave's strength, so the wave climbs the wall too. The arcs give light as they flicker. The pip of an empty belt gives red light. A switched-off suit gives no light.
- **`render/Glow`:** now carries its own `Reach` and `Keep`, with the planner's screen as the default. `ScreenReach` moved into `Light`.
- **Light position:** each light gives off from the brightness middle of its picture (`HiRes.MiddleOf`).
- **Look editor:** its figure gives no light (`Figure.GivesLight = false`).
- **Numbers:** they are in `game/Content/logic/Light.cs`, toned down from the page's values after game frames: tracker 0.9, bands 0.22.
- **Docs:** ADR `2026-11-03-hero-lights`; crew and light README lines updated.

Tests: `game.tests` and `sim/Tests` pass on their own, and `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` is clean. During the full `dotnet test Stillwake.sln`, one sim test failed while the format check was running at the same time; it was not identified, but `sim/Tests` passed in full on a rerun. Frames were checked with `--anime=colours`, dark and lit.

author: sidhujag
body:
Ordinary wallet startup currently initializes the legacy Ethereum proof dependency tree through syscoinjs-lib. This consumes the shared 1.0.276 change that loads those modules when `buildEthProof` is requested. The proof API and implementation remain intact, and the dependencies remain installed and bundled.

Pins the reviewed local archive from source `841f99eca957b58108985f428e0a2ee091e0d6ff` with SHA256 `4ab88a2db5e7d944e0e658bd9ca50c9ea31d9cfe4434849da33faebf1f73598d`. The existing postinstall verifier now checks all seven transaction-library files alongside the unchanged 219-file keyring package, while preserving its existing API result. npm publication and replacement with a matching registry artifact remain deferred.

Validation:
- Fresh frozen Yarn install, 750 unit suites / 12,971 tests, TypeScript, changed-test lint, production build and all bundle budgets pass.
- A real Node child process loads both SDK entries with all three proof modules blocked; a proof request still attempts to load its dependency. A modified installed library file is rejected by the staging verifier.
- Real Chrome Ledger ownership/cancellation, Trezor import/lock/late-reply/reconnect, and the hardware chooser UI pass against the complete build inventory. These use public synthetic fixtures, not physical hardware or a live bridge proof.

Stacked after [Pali #1141](https://github.com/syscoin/pali-wallet/pull/1141). Shared source: [syscoinjs-lib #18](https://github.com/syscoin/syscoinjs-lib/pull/18), release version: [#19](https://github.com/syscoin/syscoinjs-lib/pull/19).
